analysis.name: Anqi Wu
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Too many terminologies make lecture hard to follow, many of them are not necessary to be introduced at very first. The definition of this course is ambiguous -- is it for experts or tyro? For experts, the course content is too out of date. For tyro, nana, it's not that friendly. Prof. Wu usually won't explain the foundation stuff. take again?No.
Boring lecture, total waste of time. The homework also makes no sense. No help before the exam. Make easy topics complicate and irritating.

Some homework and exam problems are worded so confusingly and different from what's taught in lectures that make you wonder if she reads her homework and exams before giving them out. Piazza questions can be left unanswered for days but when students complain, it's apparently our fault for not "not having an idea of the workload".

Do not take. Lectures are confusing. She gets confused by her own slides, so how are we supposed to understand? Clearly doesn't prepare for lecture. Midterm (early, easier topics) had mean and median of 50ish. Exam not returned to students so no change to learn from mistakes or contest bad grading. Free content (books, YouTube) more helpful.

The lectures are way too technical and move way too fast, even for people who have a strong math and programming background. Homeworks are extremely confusing and the "extra credit" questions are not fair. Furthermore the grading policy is constantly being changed and updated without clear communication to the students.

analysis.name: Alexey Tumanov
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He seems to care a lot about the source material, but it was a struggle to follow. The projects are absurdly time consuming and the instructions were unclear. If a certain few TAs didn't exist this class would be impossible if you're new to the topic. Lots of information but I feel like I barely gained any knowledge due to the lack of clarity.

Terrible Professor and TAs, I did not enjoy the class, he was very unhelpful with matters such as labs and especially exams, my online exam refreshed 5 times but they blamed it on me, no help provided. The professors tone on emails seemed very unwelcoming and unfriendly. Labs were insanely long and expected effort was not correctly disclosed.

The professor was horrendous at teaching and not helpful whatsoever. The TAs provided limited help and didn't seem to care much, just like the professor. It could've been a good class but alas it wasn't. Please avoid this class, the course content is sub-par, the difficulty is insane and expectations are unrealistic.

Really interesting lectures, but I recommend this class be avoided if at all possible: the projects take absurd amounts of time. I typically spent in excess of 15 hours per week working on them. The project specs are always very unclear, and getting clarifications out of the course staff is time-consuming, often futile, and invariably frustrating.

Absolutely awful at teaching, and extremely unhelpful with clarifications on the homework's or the subject matter. None of the TA's knew what they were doing and made the already difficult class that much harder. The expectations in this class were impractical. And the professors attitude in an out of the class was overall negative.

analysis.name: Alex Moutaftchieva
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great organization and structure throughout the course. Always accessible outside of class and clearly cares a lot about students' career placement. Consistently connects what you learn in class to real-world applications, which makes the material much more meaningful. Easily the best professor in the major.

Alex does a great job in teaching Intro to Construction Management. She introduces new concepts in a way that is digestible for all students. There were a lot of valuable lessons that came out of the semester-end project that could be applied to the Building Construction world.

Alex has a lot of industry experience and really cares about you paying attention in class. It's pretty obvious that she is teaching because she wants us to actually learn something, not just lecturing to lecture. Very open to questions and assigns work that is actually relevant to the industry and what we are learning.

analysis.name: Caitlin Anderson
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Chill class. Not many assignments in her class and when you do have something due, she breaks it down to a tee what she wants making it really easy to do well. There's the group podcast project at the end which was fun to do and easy to do well in if you put in the effort. Try to take her if you can, you won't regret it.

Outstanding professor. Took class over the summer so was a bit rushed with only 5 weeks of material, but one assignment was due at end of every week (Friday). Two day extension always available. No final exam but English Department requires reflective ePortfolio. A bit tedious, but plenty of time is given in class to complete. Def recommend.

Very clear on everything needed to do well on any assignment, and was overall a fun class. Definetly one of the best English 2 professors; no horror stories (apart from in the novels we read/watch) that can be found from other classes.

In my class she claimed Frankenstein was the 'first transracial and transsexual person' so yeh she's a little woke, but who really cares? What matters is the grade you get, and with Anderson you are guaranteed an A. She has like 3 total assignments in the semester each of which won't take more than an hour and lets you scroll tiktok in class.
She made the class fun and the lectures were interesting. There were some assignments but they were all interesting to do and the group projects were fun.

analysis.name: Anant Paravastu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He uses matlab very differently than 1371, so reference his example code and learn his style and adapt it to yours. He tries to be pretty accessible and cares about his students so put in the work and talk things out with him if you need help because he'll definitely tries hard to help his students.

Dr. Paravastu is very passionate, comes across nice and seems genuinely concerned, but he DOES NOT know how to teach 'Thermo'. He taught the class for the first time, only presenting derivations and concepts. But we are tested entirely on problem solving, with absolutely no practice given. His tests are nonsensical relative to what he teaches.

Dr. Paravastu doesn't fit in this class. He doesn't help develop a foundation, provides no relatable links to a student's previous knowledge, assumes the student follows all his disorganized derivations and messily structured notes, and makes his tests far harder than any examples or help provided. A worthless class that is unnecessarily hard.

I can't even fully blame him because the course is designed by the department in this way. Whoever thought thermodynamics is best learned through fill-in-the-blank notes should not be allowed to be designing courses. Professor is often not sure of what he is teaching as he is following someone else's lectures. ChBE should follow MSE and Dr. Speyer.

If possible, do not take him. He uses another professor's notes and it's often clear he isn't sure himself about what he's teaching us. I just couldn't understand how he wanted us to apply concepts we learned in class. Intentionally designs exams so nobody can finish and questions are worded weirdly too. But I can see he's trying.

analysis.name: Arnold Schneider
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Did not care about his students - wrote chicken scratch notes for every lecture that were based off accounting text books. Talks way too fast and writes so quickly/poorly, that it is just better to read the textbooks. Exams are extremely difficult and practice problems were not representative of biomedical engineering applications. Avoid Avoid!!!

Class time purely goes over examples from the book - don't expect to go into lectures and actually learn anything, the expectation is that class time clarifies what you've already learned. 

In class he reflects his hand-writing on screen and its awfully scratchy - it's incredibly hard to read and follow along. 

Terribly downgrade from Deby

Mr. Schneider knows accounting very well and ask lots of questions during class to get class participation, but I could never participate unless I read the chapters before hand.  Its all about working problems.  The material isn't hard but its not an easy A.  He isn't very eager to answer questions and can often be condescending.

Lectures somehow go too fast and too slow at the same time. He handwrites notes in class. Its supposed to line up with the textbook (that he wrote himself) but he jumps around like crazy and doesn't even cover everything in the chapter. Reading the textbook is equally difficult. Nothing is clear and practice problems don't have answers. Avoid avoid

This professor wasn't as bad as the reviews made him out to be. He's ok. lectures are kinda boring but he gives extra credit. Your final grade is based on tests and homework, there aren't any projects or anything like that. You get a cheat sheet on the tests. He grades pretty easy and gives partial credit where he can.

analysis.name: Aibek Musaev
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 165 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: How can I begin to describe this class? Professor Musaev is hands-down one of the best professors I've ever laid my eyes on at Tech. I'm only 3 weeks into the course, but I've already learned so much about what I don't want to become in the future: a CS 2340 professor!

I honestly don't understand all the bad reviews. He is a nice professor and does a good job teaching concepts. Most students tend to just blame the professor whenever they struggle lol. Go to class, ask questions, and practice and you will be good. HWs are long and suck though.

Biggest troll I have encountered in my ed career. Copies slides from textbook & codes demos super fast. Instead of lecture read his slides, do slide practices & read textbook if stuck. TAs are amazing for HW help & explaining concepts. Start HW early. Teaches surface level of content to have time to ask riddles & gets mad if you know the answer.

What professor you take doesn't really matter in this course (idk if there's even multiple options). This guy seems alright though. The course itself is a decent amount of busy work and lecture attendance is required, but otherwise its chill.

This class has been the worst class I have ever taken. There were a million ways this class could have been structured better but the professor chose to make a project based class more dependent on rote learning 1200 slides instead of the project which you will spend most of your time on while being 27% of the grade. Some TA's also on a power trip

analysis.name: Andrea Parker
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The main grade for the class is a semester-long project, where you conduct user research and make Figma prototypes. It isn't bad if you have a good team, but it's a lot of writing and busy work. The lectures are honestly super boring and don't cover much to complete the project, so you don't need to pay attention to them.

I'm learning literally nothing in this class, it's the epitome of stupid busy work and wasting your time.
There's so much possible stuff to learn in the field of UI but she manages to avoid all of that useful stuff and find the most boring useless things to cover.

Great UX/UI course. I learned a lot and I found the class very useful since I want to do UX/UI as a career. The entire class is centered around group work however, so CHOOSE YOUR MEMBERS CAREFULLY. There is a lot of work, but they give you lots of time to work on it. Stay organized !!! Attendance done thru turning point/point solutions.

The class only consisted of attendance, small presentation, and semester long group project. The group project is the biggest part of the class worth 75% so choose your team members wisely. She had fun lectures to listen and learn more about UI/UX. Overall I enjoyed the class.

analysis.name: Rachel Behrmann
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I can't stress how easy this class with Professor Behrmann is. Attendance is technically mandatory but it's only enforced with participation quizzes that she gives every two lectures. I barely showed up but she uploads extensive notes, and allows you to have a flashcard for the exam. Weekly quizzes are open note and on Canvas, AND, no final.

Prof. Behrmann is awesome. She is super friendly and is extremely passionate about economics. The class is fast-paced and lecture heavy, but the exams are not that difficult. Assigns easy weekly HW quizzes that boost your grade and allows notecard crib sheet for every exam. Overall, I enjoyed taking this class and learned a ton.

Great professor with good lectures. The course itself is a bit challenging if you have never taken economics. The class is also very exam heavy (64% of grade) so slipping up once can mess you up for the whole semester. Overall not too hard or stressful though. Attendance taken only a few times using an access code.

Great professor. Super helpful and willing to answer any questions. You can always go to her office hours for help. Explanations are really good. Weekly quizzes and tests aren't too hard. Participation isn't required most of the time, but other times there are participation checks on canvas. Recommend taking her class!

As long as you show up and do your work, this class is very passable! Weekly homeworks that are not long and are very similar to the exams, plus you get a notecard for each exam. She is very accessible and wants you to do well in her class. Encourages coming to office hours and participating in class.

analysis.name: Justin Biddle
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Biddle is a very passionate and interesting lecturer, and the class is pretty discussion-heavy.

Dr. Biddle is NOT accessible outside of class. Does not respond to emails. This sucks because each absence from his class is 2% off final grade and it's hard to communicate. However, class is relatively easy and discussion based. I've learned a lot from his class. I just wish he was more lenient to absences and more responsive. He's cool I guess.

Dr. Biddle is a chill and awesome professor. I would recommend taking his philosophy class. Participation counts and the semester is broken into 3 parts: 1. do reading before class and have discussion on Perusall & have discussions in class, 2. individual essay (some in-class time given), and 3. group essay/presentation (in-class time given).

Dr. Biddle is a great professor and his lectures are interesting and enlightening. His class consists of daily readings and lectures that clarify the author's message. The only graded assignments are weekly pop quizzes to ensure you're actually reading, and take-home essay exams for the midterm/final. Understand the material and you'll do fine.

Prof. Biddle cares about his students, and wants his students to learn. Had to read before each class (1.5 hrs of work) to be able to do his pop quizzes and participate in class (there was no homework). However, pop quizzes are easy - they are very high level. The midterm and final were take-home, and consisted of a few essay questions.

analysis.name: Abrahim Ladha
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 173 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Take if you are 100% sure that you will attend all lectures + solve all homework + all practice problems + spend a lot of time trying to combine your knowledge from the lectures with the extremely difficult practice problems, and expect even more "creative", harder questions to appear on your exam. You need to practice as if this is your only class

I think Ladha is a chill guy. However, it's pretty clear that the expectations of the course don't really align with the reality. I don't think the exams are fairly written and there should be, at the very least, an exam drop for this class (like other CS2050). The TAs need less power though; they practically run the course and not in a good way.

Why is this called an intro class. Homeworks take min 6 hrs a week, TAs cant help much, it's too hard. Test reviews are so useless from TAs. If you get a C on 1 exam, no chance of an A.

He's a nice guy, content itself isn't even really that bad, but the class structure is absolutely abysmal. Save yourself the headache and transfer in the credit.

Ladha himself is a good lecturer and a good person. It's his TA's that make the class a nightmare. Just because they went through hell in their semester they think it's their turn to give us hell back. HW's took 6+ hrs per week and exams had singular questions worth 5+% of your COURSE GRADE. Absolutely do not take this class under any circumstances

This class actively regressed my knowledge of discrete mathematics and math as a whole. If God wished to give his strongest warriors a challenge, he would send students to CS2050 Office Hours to face the awful TAs for this class. Such students would emerge Navy SEALs.  Ladha is a terrible lecturer and teaches content that cater to few. Do not take.

analysis.name: Rodrigo Borela
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 84 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great professor. Interesting lectures. Maybe I'm just bad at coding, but for this class, you MUST lock in. Go to every lecture. Go to recitation. Office hours were so bad because they never had enough TAs for everyone. Sometimes I'd wait hours during office hours for a TA to help me.

I'm gonna preface by saying that I'm not good at CS, Rod was a decent teacher, he was quite passionate and funny and had pretty good lectures. For a GT requirement however, there was a lot of learning you had to do on your own that was not in the lectures, use the online textbook. Make sure you do the homeworks early and look at old exams.

Although the course material itself was difficult, the lectures were very thorough. Attendance not mandatory, but sitting through lectures really helped a lot on the tests. TAs were all very knowledgeable and he was very approachable if you had any questions. Tests can be difficult but past exams were very similar. Very sweet!

CS1301 isn't a real intro. Rod goes way too fast. Labs and TAs are awful. Never take robotics. They claim it's easier but it's hell, with async topics that don't belong in an intro. No lab help, TA helpdesk is slow and rude. Grading is sloppy, robots are disorganized. This class made me cry. Never again, made me reconsider my major as an EE.

I had literally no coding experience before going into class but found is really manageable. Lectures are recorded, so you don't have to go to class. I would recommend going to recitation and doing practice exams. Also there's like 2 points of extra credit added onto your grade at the end.

analysis.name: Matthieu Bloch
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I don't think he deserves all the hate that these reviews have been giving him. The class was fair and the exams were very similar to the homework. He is a nice person and mostly accommodating. He is very slow, but he also doesn't normally teach, and his section was only added to accommodate the influx of freshmen. This is not a deadly class.

Professor Bloch is an extremely caring professor, who is always willing to distribute knowledge on any subject he has on hand. Signal processing, machine learning, life lessons, he has and will teach about anything. Being in this VIP course has taught me so much, even when I started from no knowledge at all.

Lied to our faces about exam questions multiple times. Emphasized proof-based math questions instead of engineering/ system design ones, where the slightest error could cost you half credit. Only covered half of the material listed in the syllabus; we have to catch up now. His reviews for the graduate-level classes have the exact same complaints.

We got to early October's material in December. He regularly makes promises he doesn't keep.

He has described his own grading scheme as brutal. Every (lengthy) question is 2 points. If you write down anything you get 1 point. If you get the entire problem correct with no small errors at all, you get 2 points. 85% of the course grade was exams.

I thought he great, other guy talking about his french bit is just a hater. His lectures were super engaging and in depth, I feel like I really learned why things are implemented the way they are. The homework was also very helpful and translated well to the tests. It is true that he was behind in his material, but you can tell he's just passionate

analysis.name: Gerandy Brito
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 154 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Brito's teaching pace is great, and he keeps class very interesting: extremely funny. Sometimes doesn't follow the textbook or slides, but normally his ideas are better and simpler than those presented. Struggled to fall asleep in linear algebra, that's a feat.

I loved this class and Professor Brito. One complaint however is with the TAs. This is the first class where TAs are less approachable than the Professor and this might be due to how the class is structured. Some TAs were really nice and helpful but others TAs (namely one) on Piazza who would demean students constantly with their replies.

Brito is a great professor who clearly has a passion for the material and can keep students engaged. HW seemed like a lot for me but it really helped me learn the material. There is adequate study material for each exam and Brito tries to keep the class as engaging as possible.

Being an easy professor who gives high grades despite failing exams does not translate to being a good professor. He never released homework answers or exam answers or even feedback, just whether it was correct or not. This made doing homework worthless. For the final, he explicitly said specific topics were not on the exam--they were on the exam.

His tests are easier than the other sections, which is big in 1553. His lectures are pretty funny and entertaining, and he's a really nice guy. At first I thought he was going to be really disorganized, but he really knows his stuff and he's pretty good at teaching if you pay attention.

analysis.name: Sven Behrens
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: PHYS 2231 (Honors Physics I) He's a super nice guy, not a super nice professor. I ended the class with a 79.4 and didn't get rounded up, but he rounded up another girl's 76 to a B. Tests were weighted pretty heavily and they were extremely difficult. Averages would be failing and he would say "I don't see any means for a curve"

Behrens is such a great professor and person. Took Phys2231 with him, and while it was an incredibly challenging class he worked hard to make sure every one of us succeeded. Put in the work to the class and he will put in the work to help you. Such a funny, earnest guy who really does care about his teaching. Got a 76 in class but rounded to a B.

He did a very good job of teaching the material and explained concepts well with good practice problems. Also is super funny and genuinely one of the most caring professors. Really wants his sections to succeeds, is super available outside of class, and frequently asks for and applies any feedback given very happily. Would definitely recommend.

I struggled significantly in this course, but that was no fault of his. Honestly, I believe I may not have even had the chance at passing this course without him. Dr. Behrens is very kind and considerate of his students. He goes above & beyond to help his students succeed. If you have to take this course, he is by far the best professor.
He was so kind and genuinely cared about each of us. He made sure his office hours accommodated every single student. He cares so much about us and physics which made the class more enjoyable.

analysis.name: Leonid Bunimovich
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Seems like a good guy, but is really  bad at explaining material and is very disorganized. He interrupts you when your asking a question because he thinks he knows what your asking before your finished, so this process takes a while, by then you give up and learn nothing. Tests could be simple but not clear at what he wants you to give,  etc.

Horrible note-taking professor. He writes on the board in no particular order and then changes most of it later. Thick eastern-european accent, difficult to understand in lecture. To be fair, he was helpful when I had a problem with a test and have me a fair and deserved grade.

Appears very inviting of questions, but then calls them harsh names. 2/3 stopped attending after 1st lecture. >50% failed the first exam and the bell curve was a straight horizontal line. When approached, he got very close and said that "Other professors have a h€art atta¢k when they see me. I am the greatest statistician in the U.S."

He is horrible at explaining everything. There were topics I learned from other classes, but didn't understand how he did it. I asked questions about specific homework problems and he complained that "You're only asking questions about problems. You need to ask questions about concepts." Tests are NOTHING like homework. He's only at GT for research

The professor's teaching style is out of date. This should be an easy class and he makes it very hard by not being able to talk without 3-4 um's and uh's between 2 words. He is a very tough grader confirmed by course critique. The professor seems to be stuck in the USSR in mind. He might be very intelligent, but his skills in the classroom are weak

analysis.name: Bob Myers
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Clearly presents information and is a very good lecturer

I don't know why everyone is hating on this professor. His class is actually so funny. He is a little goofy and loves to talk about all things GT but his class is SO easy. Literally all you need to know is read the articles for the week and only write two reports the entire semester. This class is so easy and he's so funny.

Has to be the worst professor I had at Georgia Tech. He isnt a very nice person and has very little understanding of what goes on in students lives. His lectures are ultra boring as he goes on the incoherent ramblings that are just weird and awkward for the whole class. He assigns a case study every night for homework and his tests are so unfair!

Kind of a waste of time and money. He doesnt really teach anything practical in this MGT3510 class. He essentially just goes over a lot of case studies as you have one every night for homework. The also gives you a blank notes packet to fill out in which he hardly covers any of the notes. Then on test days he asks super specific case questions

Hands down worst professor I have ever had at Georgia Tech, the professor goes on and on about random topics in class. In addition he has side conversations with individual students so it seems like he ignores half the class and it makes it super awkward. Definitely take another professors supply chain/IT elective if you can!

analysis.name: Calton PU
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Pu is the most inconsiderate and laziest professor at tech In lecture we watch videos of him softly mumbling slides in a thick accent 2-4 papers due weekly The week where our semester group project proposal was due we had 4 papers due An extension was requested He responded by blaming students whom he called noise makers for gaming his class

He asked us to summarize each lecture in which he only played pre-recorded videos reading each word on the slides out. Two reading assignments on each week requiring one-page commentaries. He was extremely MEAN when commenting on project proposals, showing his perfect mastery of rhetorical questions and sarcasm. DON'T TAKE THIS COURSE!

NEVER TAKE THIS COURSE. Firstly, he is very aggressive and inconsiderate, and any reasonable request is called gaming his course. Secondly, most self-drafted semester-long projects are said to be worthless, and he expects us to produce more creative and better projects than commercial products. Do not let this course be your nightmare.

Despite being somewhat easy, this was by far the WORST class I have ever taken. He just played videos of himself talking during class, which were incredibly boring, unclear, and unnecessary. The requirements for the class are unclear, which he justifies by claiming that its about "autonomous learning." Poorly structured and poorly taught. Beware.

Replays video lectures during in-person class times. Will repeatedly interrupt you during office hours. Dislikes being questioned on the structure of the class to the point of sending long rant-like emails not even a month into the semester. Incredibly time consuming class with most of the difficulty coming from the interactions with the professor.

analysis.name: Onur Birol
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 61 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Birol is one of the worst teachers I have ever had. He makes his tests overly difficult and is not open to the student's concerns. The test is in 50 minutes and I have to search through over 500 pages of notes so you're set up for failure. He doesn't respect students at all/very passive-aggressive. I would avoid him if you need to take BIOS 1108.

Made physiology very interesting and made topics relatable. Exams were straightforward, but some questions were difficult. Final exam was light, 60% of it came from previous midterms. You can do well by going to class or self-studying with the book. Homework = easy grade booster. Pre-lecture quizzes were annoying timing-wise, but he dropped a lot.

Dr. Birol co-taught this class with Dr. Richards. Birol is clearly passionate about biology. I went to 70% of the lectures and made an A. He is a good speaker and helps us understand material better. The only issue is that some of the exam questions were based on what was said in lecture and not found in the slides, but it wasn't that big of a deal

Dr. Birol's lectures were extremely helpful, and I felt that exams accurately reflected content taught in class. Pre-readings were required for this class. If I did not understand a pre-reading, I knew that if I went to class Dr. Birol would clarify it for me. Great teacher!!
To do well, attendance isn't necessary. Just rely on the textbook.

co-taught w/ robbie richards. birol focused on animals and was generally better. didn't ramble as much. he tries to draw focus to what goes on the test, but there's just a great amount of content. recitation is helpful. some tests focus on what is explicitly talked about in class and not clearly shown on slides, but attendance isn't mandatory.

analysis.name: Charles Peak
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: unorganized + needs a writing class since he's bad at writing coherently and without grammatical/phrasal errors making it harder to answer basic questions. When questions arise during exams, he wastes precious time by simply reading the question again. I also have eyes. That is unhelpful.

He is approachable one-on-one outside of class, but grading is very strict and can feel snarky. Assignments often lack clear guidance, yet points are deducted for minor errors like spelling. The class may feel discouraging, but students can improve by adapting to his expectations.
Snarky and rude. Picky comments and feedback on work. Could/should have shown more kindness towards students. Don't take his class if you're looking for respect.

analysis.name: Carla Gerona
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Truly horrible class. She struggles with technology, gives heavy readings weekly with around 4-5 hours of lecture time per week. Everything you do will contain a quiz. You will have to memorize EVERY detail of the textbook if you want even a semi-decent grade. Many trick questions on the test asking information not in the textbook or class. AVOID.

This class was harder than every one of my major related classes. Get ready to spend about 15 hours per week on this class, and then barely passing because you didn't remember what color George Washington's uncle's underwear was at the battle of peepeepoopoo.

My relationship with this class was more toxic than my relationship with my ex. I put in around 16 hours of work per week, do all the assignments and readings, and I prepare relentlessly for exams. There is nothing I could have conceivably done to memorize the sheer level of detail that her tests require, if you want to even PASS. AVOID AT ALL COST

Prof. Gerona is wonderful. Her online lectures are engaging and a good balance of independence. Just make sure you do not forget about the deadlines or you will need a deans letter, no exceptions. Exams are very hard, so make sure you rigorously review the lectures-- they have all the info you will need! The lectures are interesting tho, really.

If you like reading through 905 pages of mostly unimportant textbook information from 1500-1877, completing quizzes that have little to no connection to the class and don't give an accurate representation of the material, and having to memorize how many pounds of meat and canoes two guys ate and built in 1837, this is the class for you.

analysis.name: Colin Parker
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He expects you to have come into class having a background in Physics and also keeping up with the textbook readings. (note: textbook is paid). In my opinion, I thought he focused too much on ideas that didn't matter that much to the class like derivations, and wouldn't spend enough time on the bigger picture that would be important for exams.

The class is structured well, especially for a class that most of the school takes. Dr. Parker seems very knowledgeable, but often expects us to know the concepts before lecture, and spends more of lecture doing examples when a lot of us don't know the concepts. Physics at Tech is hard, and I ended up watching Dr. Munoz's lectures to study.

I took AP Physics C1 in high school, so I may be a bit biased, but I thought Parker was a pretty good lecturer. Sometimes he would start class with a problem you hadn't learned how to solve yet, but he'd go into the lecture material after that so it wasn't a big deal. He's a really fun, good guy and I enjoyed his lectures and demos.

I took AP Physics C in hs and without that I would've been cooked. He often spent most of the lectures trying to figure out practice problems for himself and would get them wrong everyday. It really annoyed me that someone with a physics PHD couldn't even teach physics 1 well. Just watch Alicea's lectures and ignore him.

definitely not intro friendly so if you haven't taken physics before, don't take this professor. its easy to get lost in lectures and i would often find myself more confused after. physics is just hard in general so take it easy on yourself and take alicea if possible

analysis.name: Thomas Collins
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: There were 2 projects with opportunities for extra credit if you put in significantly  more work. Imo project 2 way easier than project 1. The first half of the semester was insanely easy but everything is concentrated in Late October->December so plan for that. He has a tendency to not understand your question so you need to be specific.

2 projects with plenty of extra credit. All lecture slides are online. Make sure to start projects and homework early. Plenty of practice tests available on canvas. Office hours help a lot from what I have heard. Great professor, but I have heard Wills might be slightly better, but both are great. Pretty easy class, not very test heavy.

Pretty good professor, makes it very clear whats going to be on the exams. the 2 projects are weighted the same as the 3 midterms, so gotta start those projects early. Lots of opportunity for extra credit with the projects, and very lenient late policy.

Skip the pointless reading from Rapid Prototyping and lecture. Labs are as simple as following the (confusing) lab manual. Second practical exam was basically impossible, and the ONE exam asks about details so specific they're basically irrelevant. Extremely condescending when asked about grading mistakes. Pre-labs and lab reports are lengthy.
A really enjoyable and light class. Exams are extremely fair and there is ample opportunity to get extra credit on the two projects. Though, both of them are pretty time consuming. Highly recommended

analysis.name: Kelly Comfort
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class was alright and I made an A. However, the professor doubted that I was capable of writing Spanish at a high level despite having done two different study abroad programs. Moreover, she was more obsessed with how dolls perpetuate racial stereotypes and other absurd activist themes than teaching us practical uses of the Spanish language.

Professor Comfort was great! One should know this is very much a Spanish LITERATURE class, so be prepared to read some abstract texts and discuss stuff like symbolism and metaphor. If you really want to push your Spanish comprehension abilities, then this is a great class with a wonderful professor!

Amazing professor! You can tell she cares about her students and is so well-versed in the subject matter being taught. I feel like I learned so much and I greatly improved my Spanish skills despite being a native speaker. The readings can be a little dense but the homework is fairly easy and doesn't take long to complete.

Really great teacher. If you have any questions about readings or essays, go to office hours with a thesis or something and you'll leave with an exact plan for your essay. Lectures are engaging and different each day. Does require participation and presentations but kind of expected from a spanish class.
I absolutely loved her class - she is engaging, kind, and interesting. The class is not difficult. Show up, participate, and do your work to earn an easy A!

analysis.name: Christopher Jankowski
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 108 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: His lectures are great; I even have friends that wake up for his 8 AMs that aren't registered. He paces himself well and clarifies any questions. You don't have to go to class except for the occasional in-class poll (3 get dropped, 5% of grade). Quizzes are pretty easy (1 gets dropped), and midterms are fair (but slightly harder than other profs).

Really good lectures, really enthusiastic that makes you enthusiastic about math (which is a feat in itself). Pretty tough exams, but usually the averages were right in the middle of the curve of the other classes, so they were fair. Very helpful in office hours, etc. Highly recommend.

This class is not too hard to get an A in if you study well. The tests are kind of difficult and it's easy to get points off because a lot of questions are true/false or select all that apply, but if you understand the content well enough, it's usually fine. He has lecture videos and slides posted, so you don't have to go to lectures either.

Professor Jankowski is a great professor. He was a good presenter and would explain in class. It is easy to access him via Piazza, office hours, or after class. Apart from being a good lecturer, he was a personable guy and would yap about his life stories. He is the course director and posts plenty of resources. Use resources and ask for help!

The concepts in this class can be pretty confusing but he explains them pretty well. I think his lectures are fine but from what I've heard none of the other 1553 lecturers are good and people end up going to Jankowski's lectures instead, so he's definitely the one to pick. Do practice tests to review for the tests because they are very similar.

analysis.name: Danielle Geary
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: GREAT teacher! Had for both 1101/1102. She's extremely interested in how her students are doing in classes as well as everyday life. Uses book a lot but also has supplemental materials which she uses to make sure students fully grasp the concepts taught. Best Spanish teacher ever!

Dra. Geary is an amazing professor! She communicates deadlines clearly and is very responsive over email if you ever have any questions. The online mini classes and TalkAbroads are not graded harshly and really helped me get better at speaking Spanish. The online textbook is mandatory for weekly assignments (costs $50 I think).

Genuinely one of the best teachers I've ever had. She actually cares about her students in and out of the classroom. The class isn't hard, if you care about learning you'll thrive in her class. Very available for help/email, and has a genuine desire to help her students succeed. Definitely recommend her as a professor, very positive energy

Sra. G was amazing! This class was super fun - I practiced my Spanish in a chill, encouraging environment. I loved the telenova, group convos, and video calls with native speakers. Heads up- some of the class materials cost money (~$110). If you're nervous abt speaking broken Spanish, take this class, it will really help you solidify and practice!
really wants you to get better at the language so lots of speaking involved. theres a good deal of work to do outside of class but not too much or difficult to deal with.

analysis.name: Rachel Dean-Ruzicka
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Dean has been a very pleasant professor to have! Accepts late work and is not a harsh grader/most grades are completion. Very friendly and makes it easy to participate and do the assignments without feeling forced to. She won't be like those English professors that are always looking for a specific answer.

I took Professor Dean blindly. She has a very interesting topics (Monsters), and she has a labor based grading system. She made attendance guidlines easier later in the sem so attendance is not too bad. She gives good feedback, and lets you redo assignments and projects. She is very understanding and helpful. Would def reccomend this English class.

She was very caring and sympathetic towards the fact that many students at a tech school don't care about English. The topic for my 1102 course was very interesting and our assignments were not just standard essays. Every assignment was graded on completion (as long as you met all the requirements) aside from reading checks.

As long as you do your work and put in a decent amount of effort, you will get a 100 in this class. She is a very easy grader and she gives excellent feedback. She also really puts an emphasis on creating an inclusive and welcoming space for all students. 10/10 would recommend her!!!

While she didn't lecture much, she was quite friendly and made herself accessible. The assignments do take a little while to complete, but grading is practically for completion, and she gives incredibly clear feedback on how to improve your projects.

analysis.name: Danny Woodbury
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Woodbury is a good professor. Class has two parts: watch online lecture and answer some homework questions online, then in class he builds on the lecture and you do a worksheet graded on completion (so go to class). You have 2 midterms and 1 final which combined are probably 60% of your grade. Tests & class not too hard. There is some extra credit.

Dr. Woodbury cares a lot about his students and wants them to succeed. Just make sure you keep up with the homework deadlines as they aren't the midnight standard. Attendance isn't mandatory, but there are in-class work (for credit) that you may miss if you skip class. Make sure to use the scheduling site to setup an appt with him if you need help.

Class meets in-person 1x a week. I'd recommend showing up to that class because of occasional in-class assignments and extra credit opportunities. The exam's are very similar in structure (MCQ, Multiple Select, and FRQ). FRQ were always practice problems. MCQ and Multiple Select were difficult, I'd take notes on textbook chapters. Not-too-hard A.

I do not have a good experience with this professor. Difficult to get a hold of and not very willing to go out of his way to support individual students. His lectures are hard to follow along with the criteria he is producing. Some may disagree but not the professor for me.

Take him!! I have nothing but great things to say. If you do the homework on time and study the practice problems he gives, you have absolutely nothing to worry about. We also only meet once a week instead of twice. I've thoroughly enjoyed his class so far, I'm understanding the content, and don't feel stressed at all. HIGHLY recommend.

analysis.name: Carrie Shepler
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 170 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: I love Dr. Shepler! Her lectures are easy to follow and she makes a lot of difficult concepts easy to understand. She will also go out of her way to provide office hours and extra help to those who need it. That being said, this class requires a lot of work, especially with the lab component added on. You have to put in a lot of effort to get an A.

Dr. Shepler is awesome. I had her for 1211, and I have her now for 1212. She is always willing to help you and is very supportive both academically and personally. If you go to office hours, she remembers you by name. She has comical ways of remembering tricky concepts. If you wanted to get an A in the class, you definitely could.

a professor that does the flipped classroom model correctly. office hours are good, lectures are good, and videos are good. I would recommend using the videos for cheat sheets because if it's in the vids it'll be on the test (lectures get derailed sometimes). Make sure to get all the final exam tokens. The questions are really easy. Learn sig figs

I love this professor!!! Please take her if you want amazing lectures, a kind and caring teacher, and just a great experience with CHEM1212K :) Dr. Shepler puts her lectures online in a flip classroom method but the videos are a masterpiece. They are super easy to follow and she explains everything in a clear and consice way. She is just wonderful.

Dr. Shepler is easily one of the most empathetic and sweet professors to roam this Earth. She structures the class with the understanding that this course is difficult. I won't lie and say the class is easy, but she definitely does everything in her power to ease the burden on her students. If you have the choice, don't take 1212 with anyone else!

analysis.name: David Rodin
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Best thermo proof at Tech. Does not make the class any harder than it has to be. All of the practice material is exactly like the exams so if you do all of it you will be all good. Super great guy he makes what could be an evil class so doable!!

One of the best professors I have had. Very accessible outside of class and lectures were engaging. Weekly homework. The grading scheme is very test heavy but he does give extra credit. Test are not very difficult if you do the practice tests.

The GOAT! Amazing, thorough, and incredibly helpful lectures. Super understanding guy. Tests are worth a lot of your grade, but they're incredibly fair, and if you do all the homework every week with fidelity and do the practice exam, you'll be set for an A. Overall, if you put in consistent but reasonable effort every week, you'll do very well.

He was great at adapting to the class and actually teaching the material. Very lenient and understanding in general. He was also effective at guiding his students through this coursework. The best professor someone can take thermo from.

analysis.name: Frank Dellaert
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Not sure why this course gets so much hate. Dellaert is a caring professor that listens to students' concerns, and actively tries to ensure students in lecture understand the content. The content itself is quite difficult, but there's more than enough time provided to complete projects and receive full points. No in class exams reduces stress.

Goes far in depth about statistical and mathematical concepts, but still interesting to learn about. Projects can be done without a solid understanding in material, but it's more fulfilling to solidify your understanding of concepts. Really caring and interesting professor.

Is very passionate about the topic he teaches, however completely centers his course around a textbook he wrote and a library he created. This feels less of a lecture/course and more of him flaunting his own works and forcing students to use them, even if they can be useful. Homework is long and lots of busy work. Lectures are complex but useless.

I've never felt so entirely lost. Unless you have a really solid stats background before starting this class, it feels like you're doomed to take away nothing. Pretty intense math/concepts and new ones every lecture. Difficult homeworks feel like "so what?" when you finish them. Entirely dissuaded me from doing robotics ever again.

it takes weeks for grades to be returned to you. in addition, the criteria for the lengthy reflection portion of projects is extremely unclear, and the weight for each project in canvas is wrong, causing unnecessary stress for students. lectures were also incredibly hard to follow. don't take this class.

analysis.name: Dan Lotan

review_highlights.comment:
major discord mod vibes, confusing instructions

don't take his lab unless you enjoy wasting tuition
he reminds me of a discord mod and talks with a lisp. whatever you do, don't take his class.

analysis.name: Damon Williams
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment:
he has good things and bad things about him. he does like to intimidate and show off how smart and powerful he is. also during the class he's always going off-topic and making jokes, so i learn maybe half the material in class. this guy is just doin too much.

on the other hand, i think he means well and is a pretty funny guy

The kind of prof they make movies about. Hilarious, engaging, AMAZING lectures. Yes tests are hard, but very very fair, if you put in the work an A is very achievable. Got a B because of daily quizzes- the one awful part of the class. Do NOT miss a single class. He really cares for students and teaches you what ISyE is all about.

most difficult prof ever he makes fun of students but disguises it as "tough love" he thinks his class should be our top priority and humiliates students for not understanding concepts. if hes so committed to us learning the content why doesnt he teach it? he wastes everyones time by spending class time having side convos w his select fav students

Having Damon as a professor my freshman year of college changed my life. Easily the best professor I have ever had at GT, made me passionate about industrial engineering and taught me that hard work will pay off. The course is pretty tough but if you follow his steps for success and put in work outside the classroom, you will do great.

Damon is quite a character, as you can see from the other ratings he is very polarizing. I thought he was great and funny but I see why some people don't like his personality. Anna the TA is great though. Daily quizzes every day, 2 midterms which were fair, do all you can to not take final, I hear its impossible. Life lessons will be dispensed.

analysis.name: Denis Dorozhkin
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 94 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: No tests, 2 easy pop quizzes.  Attendance is 100% mandatory.  I took him his first semester here for 1770.  He has a thick Russian accent but I never have trouble understanding him.  Lots of work, but that's the nature of the course.  Pick simpler topics for projects and pray to God that your group isn't bad.  Would take again.

Chill prof and very useful class. I learned almost everything through the VERY LONG hw and lab assignments, not his boring lectures. Assignments graded quite harshly, taking off for little things. Should be an easy A if you do your work with decent effort. Oh also he'll call you out in front of the class if you're late or on your phone or whatever.

There are many benefits of taking Professor Dorozhkin compared to others (access to the best project materials, has free voucher codes for ~$100 SolidWorks test certificates, more flexible for deadlines/requirements, etc.). However, his fast-paced and somewhat monotone nature made some of the important, dull topics less engaging than they could be.

Insanely funny and chill guy, he makes some of the most annoying parts of this class fun. Workload is a lot. The TAs are nasty graders and will take off lots of points for small things. The team and individual projects are massive time sinks. But he gives you enough resources to succeed and makes lectures fun. Take him if you can.

He is an awesome and very understanding professor. He makes his assignments very doable, although some might take longer than others. If he saw that few students had turned in a homework he usually gave an extension to all his sections, which was very nice, especially during exam heavy weeks. Can't recommend him enough!

analysis.name: David Joyner
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 167 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: This is perhaps the best class I've taken. You can go at your own pace, and you cannot receive less than a one hundred on any homework assignment unless you give up. You get multiple attempts on test questions, and you can submit coding problems as many times as you want before you get it right. This class is very easy and works to any schedule.

This class was very easy. The first few units are simple, even if you don't have experience, the videos and practice assignments make everything understandable. The practice quizzes/tests are very similar to the real ones, so just study those. The class is organized well. Overall, as long as you do the work and stay on track, you're guaranteed a A.

Being required to take a cs class at tech is challenging for people like me who study neuroscience and have no interest in computer science but this online course was phenomenal. The material is easy to grasp and there is a lot of practice. The tests are very straight forward and exactly like the practice. There is also tons of extra credit.

If you don't already have knowledge w/ CS this can be a very long and challenging course. Wayyyy too much HW for an intro class, but there is extra credit. The tests are hard because they are all or nothing, so it's easy to get a poor grade if you don't write out the solutions perfectly.

Dr. Joyner is the best teacher I've had at Georgia Tech and I took the CS 1301 online class with him. His video lectures were clear and concise. I had never taken any CS course before this one. I only had to complete 3 problems on the final for a 95 overall in the class. Definitely recommend him.

analysis.name: Jeff Epstein
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He touched me emotionally. This class was inspiring and all the kids loved him! Would take again
Unfortunate name, but great prof. Is quite strict about talking or eating in class. Great otherwise.
Dr Jeff Epstein is such a heart touching professor. He would often times make us take field trips to this private Island. He is willing to help you reach your full potential!

He's my favorite professor at Georgia Tech. Great lectures with discussion questions. Labs are very well designed with extra credit, clearly documented and commented. ACA is definitely a challenging course — especially since I hadn't taken the prerequisite (ECE 3057) and no C++ experience. Despite that, I managed to make it through successfully.
The class field trip was NOT what I expected it to be 😖

analysis.name: Daniel Spieler
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He is a nice guy, but, he is one of the worst professors I have had at Tech. He is not very good at explaining concepts, which is needed in a stats class. Tests are extremely difficult, so don't be surprised if you fail them. He does curve the class though to compensate (I got a B). Go to class...even if it feels pointless. Good luck...trust me!

I didn't go to lecture because he would talk about nonsense instead of explaining anything. He gave 8 random quizzes. Lab was terrible, always took 3 hours. Homeworks were difficult, don't wait until last minute on those. I failed both exams, although we got 3 crib sheets for the exams. The grading was very harsh, but there is a curve.

The professor gives you a topic list to study off for midterms and finals, but questions are very confusing for an intro class. Some questions are too specific and frq grading is pretty strict. No clear guidelines for the frq. Lectures had a lot of unnecessary information and the professor often rambled a lot which can be confusing. $100 textbook.

Prof Spieler is a kind person but psych1101 was very frustrating. Test formats were unclear, I did horrible on the first midterm because the FRQ was difficult to understand. Lectures were easy to understand but I ended up just learning everything outside of the class on my own. TAs did not know what was happening in the class and were unhelpful.

FIND A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR OR DONT TAKE THE CLASS. Seriously it's not worth it. Made psych way to diffuclt for what it is. I was so jealous of my friends who were telling me they had take home online tests while I was working my butt of for a literal 70 on the first midterm. This is an intro class, should not be that hard. Bro deserves more 1 stars

analysis.name: Eunbee Kim
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: honestly an not a great professor all around. not engaging when she lectures, rude, does not reply to emails ever which makes it impossible to have your attendance corrected when you miss class. attendance is mandatory and you lose points if you come in >5 mins late, which is unfortunate when i'm the one PAYING for these courses.

graded by too many things when clearly some grade categories are not even necessary for the class. has article quizzes which tests on the specific content of a research paper, so it's irrelevant from the topics learned in class. the supposed "homeworks" are just writing practice questions for the article quizzes. she makes the class impractical.

The professor is honestly not bad but her lecture slides can be sort of confusing to look at. But she does try her best to teach by providing practices and study guides. The course content is pretty easy to grasp as long as you're willing to put extra time. Did not attend most of the lecture/lab but ended with an A, so it is definitely doable.

i'm sure she's a great person, but she was one of the least engaging professors i've ever had. in-class activities were inconsistently weighted so get ready to either sit through every lecture or watch the canvas uploads like a hawk. she does post exam study guides, though, and the content wasn't too hard. watch out for research article quizzes.

Prof is clearly an intelligent person but that does not make her a great teacher. She does not teach the basics of the concepts we learn in class well. You will have to teach yourself most of the material. The lectures do not really help unless you already have a proper understanding of statistics. She definitely makes the class harder than needed.

analysis.name: Michael Evans
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: He is constantly losing his train of thought in class and getting things wrong, which confuses everyone else. Ruined my ability to like chemistry. Three exams that are sort of fair, but then an exhausting, outlandish final. Save your GPA, as he ruined mine. He's knowledgeable, but an awful teacher, and isn't empathetic.

Dr. Evans seems kind and is ready to help students. However the content we learn in class and that is on the assigned homework is SO MUCH easier than the tests. The tests are insanely difficult that it feels rigged, especially the final. Don't expect a grade bump either and no extra credit in the test category.

I took him for 1211 and I have him for 1212 at the moment of writing. He's a good dude, funny guy with an obsession with Ke$ha (yes the singer). However, the tests are a little difficult and he likes to test if you actually understand why you are doing the things you are doing and not just doing them. Overall, good prof if you rly apply yourself.

honestly your grade will depend entirely on you so don't procrastinate. lots of homework and free points. iclicker questions in class counts so just go to lecture even if you're not going to pay attention. he was funny and nice and always super cheerful so that helped. exams will get you if you don't study. thermodynamics absolutely destroyed me

It is unfortunate that this is the best professor for gen chem at ga tech. He is an amazing lecturer and really makes concepts digestible but his exams are extremely difficult and NOTHING like the practice exams. No matter how much time i put into the class my grades barley reflected it.

analysis.name: Elizabeth Miller

Absolutely lovely human being. Dr. Miller was a super caring and sweet professor for ENGL 1102. Her course theme is Dark Academia which is a lot more interesting that you'd think. There was only 1 essay, and 2 group projects that were fun to complete and very engaging. She is also super understanding about other classes and workload. Loved her!

She's a really sweet person who clearly cares about her students. While some of the projects did feel unnecessary at times, they were reasonable enough, and you can definitely learn *something*. She's extremely friendly and approachable, and I will miss having her class next semester!

I took her English 1102 class, and the class was incredibly easy yet interesting. We only wrote one essay while the other two big projects were unique group projects of creating a podcast and a website. Both projects were thought provoking and highly interesting. Dr. Miller explains everything well and is very flexible, truly caring for you.

Elizabeth is great! She is a very caring and kind person. Her first priority always seemed to be our wellbeing and how we were adjusting and doing in more difficult classes, and the coursework was simple and very helpful like creating a resume or linkedin profile or just meeting with our academic advisor.

analysis.name: Bachir El Fil

HW graded harshly and barely any review material. Ok to reach.

Avoid at all costs. He's a nice guy and cares a lot but his expectations are way to high. Teaches purely conceptual in class and then expects you to learn everything on the homework, which is impossible without a software that he doesn't teach you how to use. Class is 20+ hours of work per week. Tests are abysmal and good luck finishing in time.

Only section that didn't have a take home final, and got the lowest avg on the 2nd exam. The hw's are long, and graded harshly and the lectures are conceptual. I helped other sections study for their finals and their review question were far easier. We got only two review questions per test. Hardest tests I've taken at GT. Caring guy.

On the final, there were things that we had never seen before. Teaching-wise, a limited amount of foundational concepts were covered, and you were just thrown into the fire to figure it out.

Definitely the hardest class I've taken at tech. HOWEVER, Dr. Fil is the best. Very caring and great dude. I really enjoyed his lectures, he was very enthusiastic and man do I know thermo now. Fair grader. The homework was a full time job and the exams were brutally hard though.

analysis.name: Edwin Greco

Completing one problem in an hour class period was an achievement. He explains almost nothing thoroughly. Wastes too much time in class on jokes rather than actually achieving any useful level of instruction. Would not recommend.

Most of Greco's lectures are spent listening to his jokes and maybe watching him work a couple of practice problems. Really nice guy but not a very good teacher and comes off as somewhat unapproachable. Tests were pretty hard and he didn't curve. Wouldn't recommend. I barely made a B and I had to work ridiculously hard for it.

Most of the professors at Tech can teach fairly well but Greco is an exception. He is one of the worst teachers I've ever had and cannot stay on topic for more than 30 seconds. Not a terribly hard class but if you take him prepare to teach the class to yourself!

Most of what you learn is from the textbook. He NEVER teaches substantially in class. I really liked physics but after going through this class I dread it. Sets assignments on topics he hasn't covered. Didn't enjoy this class at all….

Physics is not an easy subject, but Greco makes it enjoyable. He emphasizes understanding the subject rather than just memorizing formulas. He goes out of his way to make himself accessible to student, but he is not always the best at explaining things. The tests are difficult, but Greco tries to give you as much credit as he can.

analysis.name: Edvard Bruun
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Bruun was an amazing COE 2001 prof. He makes the notes easily accessible and works through lots of examples in class. The grade cutoff for an A is 85, and there are a decent number of extra-credit opportunities, which made it easy to get an A. The homework takes a decent bit of time, but the homework questions are very similar to exam questions

Agree with other reviews. Thought some of the homework and practice problems were harder than the tests. Great prof, teaches really well. 3 extra credit surveys and extra credit on every test. Optional final. By far the easiest of the statics class while still actually learning. 100% pick Prof Bruun if he's teaching statics.
I would like him to teach every ME class at tech! The most chill professor I have ever had. 85 was an A at the beginning of the semester.

great prof! Made it really easy to get an A because the grade cutoff was only an 85. he was super nice and posted his notes, which were super digestable and easy to read. textbook was helpful too. tests were not easy, but again only needed an 85 for an A. also offered good extra credit and would curve. loved this class!

analysis.name: Todd Fernandez
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The pre-PSS lectures are longer than they should be for the amount of content they cover. His expectations are unrealistic and will lowkey try and gasliight you into thinking that you did not read the instructions clearly, when he CHANGED THE INTSTRUCTIONS after multiple groups submitted and he realized he does not like it

Very unorganized. Good person who's bad at teaching. Grading is unnecessarily complicated and the homeworks take forever. The tests are poorly written and when asked for clarification, he just reads the question again, which is entirely unhelpful and condescending.

Todd clearly cares about your success. However, his questioning and guiding is unclear. He will let you redo a portion of the course if he feels your work is not good enough, but then you are missing out on 1/3 of the course material. The lecture content is unhelpful. Why wait until the presentation to tell you that you are on the wrong track?

The lead instructor (not PSS) for 2250. Nice guy & fun to talk, but class was severely unorganized with assignments not clearly posted on Canvas (deadlines very hard to find). Chaos ruled and TAs + PSS Professor greatly helped in guidance, but class lacked structure and was a hodgepodge of work to do, found BMED 2310 to be much better organized

He will confuse you and likes to make his expectations seem higher than the actual grading criteria. He loves to yap so he'll ask you super deep questions that you don't actually have to answer or consider for deliverables. Way too much "busy work" for a like 1 hr course and just a giant group project but it is what it is. He is nice tho.

analysis.name: Nabid Farvez
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Farvez gives intense lectures. He's very vocal, and his oral skills are through the roof. I've never been so satisfied in such a long, hard semester, but he's honestly the best. I spent a lot of time in one-on-one office hours. Despite the tight deadlines, he encourages hard work with rigid schedules and stiff grading.

Professor Farvez was an extraordinary teacher. He reached above and beyond what should be expected from a professor, and always offered up advice or just a friendly face to talk to whenever his students needed it. Ask him about his youtube channel!
In these trying times, Professor Farvez was honestly a bright spot in a difficult semester. Despite his intimidating accomplishments, he's a humble and nice instructor who truly wants you to succeed.

I haven't gotten a chance to take any of his real classes yet but I hear he's an overall nice guy. Not too strict and knows Tech students go through a lot so tries to be understanding and lenient with grading. Likes to uplift lectures by sharing memes. Actually not a professor yet but maybe one day.
Professor Farvez really makes you work hark in this class, but you learn so much! One of the best professors and best classes I've had and taken at Tech. Truly lifechanging.

analysis.name: Nihad Farooq
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: i used to like her in the beginning of the semester, but the readings were just way too much. also, she does not put grades in until the end of the semester so you never really know where you stand. she does not like when you use the computer in class for some reason? even if it just means taking notes. however, the lectures were interesting.

The class itself is really interesting and the professor is the nicest person I've ever met. The one test we had was pretty difficult, but it was mainly memorization. Very reading-heavy, but interesting ones. There was a group project that was pretty easy to do and a final essay/project that was decently designed.

Very few professors connect with students the way Dr. Farooq does. She assigns a lot of reading but it's not impossible to keep up with it and most are interesting reads. If you show interest in the class and reach out to her if you're having difficulty, she will help in any way she can. She's incredible and I encourage anyone to take her classes.
Take another professor. Readings were way too much, so make sure to study for the exam. Also only graded by a few things.

Dr. Farooq is one of those teachers that you simply have to take at GT and she is genuinely one of the kindest and best professors I have ever had. Note to future students though, she does not post grades so make sure to keep in mind the breakdown of grades from the syllabus. Participation is key and can make or break your grade.

analysis.name: Edward Botchwey
