He has horrible handwriting and doesn't know how to use his own technology. Poor grading system with little structure. Most test were curved because the average was below a 50.

This class was very disorganized, and there was a general lack of communication. Dates of HW, quizzes, and tests were almost always changed. Also, these usually had to be done on paper and then uploaded to T-Square, which was confusing. However, Dr. Botchwey was frequently willing to listen and make changes. Most questions came from the book.

Dr. Botchwey is terribly disorganized and you will learn very little without complete dependence on good TA/self effort. His general format for class consists of telling students to open a practice quiz and work on it in groups, later going through the problem in a disorganized if not incorrect fashion. He is regularly not present either

Dr. Botchwey is a funny guy, but he is often absent for the courses that he teaches. It seems like he's got a lot of other commitments so no shade or anything, and in 2110, it didn't end up mattering all that much but do be aware of that.

He was very disorganized. He has horrible hand writing and uses an iPad to hand write his notes.. a horrible combination. He is very uncleAR about his expectations for assignments and very rarely gives out an assignment sheet. Every due date usually changes.  He also is not very clear about material for tests.

analysis.name: Phillip First
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Excellent and kind professor, extremely hard class. The course material is definitely not easy for a freshman. Be ready to read the textbook and spend a long time studying on weekends. But he curves a lot for us, so even though you get a low grade on exams, you still have a high chance of getting an A.

Nice guy but very disorganized class. Everything was posted late and he was frequently late to class at 2pm. Slides were just screenshots of the textbook. Sometimes made concepts more confusing than they had to be, but had a good sense of humor and lectures were somewhat enjoyable. Homeworks were very long.

First is a great teacher. Great sense of humor, clear explanations, and friendly. Homework was heavy and tests varied in difficulty, but mostly hard. I took 2 classes with him and would take more. To the posters below: This might be because he had to teach intro physics to you...
The professor was not really helpful but the class was not hard. Attendance optional.

analysis.name: Fatiesa Sulejmani
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Sulejmani does at good job at helping you think through problems. Compared to alot of professors at Tech I feel like she actually wants to see students succeed and always makes time for students in office hours and answering questions outside of class. She is very responsive and explains things in detail.

Dr. Sulejmani is by far the best prof I've ever had. I had her for 2310 and 3410, and her lectures in both were easy to follow. She is super approachable and very funny, and she cares deeply about her students' success. If you need advice in pretty much anything related to BME, go to her office hours!!!

Dr. Sulejmani is by far the best prof that I have had a tech. She is patient and kind, and incredibly smart. Great balance of problem solving and lectures. As long as you study and put in the work, you will be fine. Biomechanics is a hard class but she made it so much easier. If you ever get the chance to have her for any class, take it.

Dr. Sulejmani is great! Biomechanics is not as bad as people say it is, especially if you have her for PSS. Her PSS mini-lectures and the fact that she would walk through each PSS problem step-by-step helped a lot. She also holds extra office hours during busier weeks which is super helpful.
She is passionate and explains the content very clearly while asking good questions to stimulate our learning. She makes it super easy to understand

analysis.name: Daniel Forsyth

review_highlights.comment: We are only 4 days away from final exam, yet no information has been posted, no practice material, no topic list, nothing. Overall, this class has been run very poorly this semester, and at this point I'm just glad it will be over in few days.

Projects are long, help is rare, and the course can feel like it sets you up to fail.

Homeworks and projects are busy work and provide very little learning since TAs refuse to grade homework and projects on time.

Reads off a powerpoint that is filled with errors. Cool. I'll just go to office hours. TAs don't even show up to office hours most of the time. I wait 45 minutes for a TA in queue. TA says idk just read the book. Great. Open notes also got removed so there is lots of memorization of weird information.

Homework every week plus projects that span 3-4 weeks. Project content not taught until week before due but told to start early. Lectures are a bore, just read the textbook, they cover the exact same thing. Expect to not get help from TAs, you will wait for hours in OH just for them to not be able to answer your question. Not impossible, but hard.

analysis.name: Farjana Siddiqua

Teaches straight from the slides but she has her own notes that helped a lot more than just taking notes from the slides. Will answer questions but her answers can be a little confusing. Lecture before tests is just her reviewing/answering last minute q's.

I can kind of understand what she is trying to explain but she doesn't really explain things in a clear, concise way. I can't really say much though because I only went to lecture the first 2 weeks of class. My studio TA taught well though so I did just fine by only going to studio.
Just watch the online lectures of another prof instead. lectures are straight garbage

It was honestly quite hard to understand her during lecture, and the topics oftentimes didn't really make sense from her explanations. The tests are quite difficult, but that is from the course coordinator and not her. Avoid taking if you want clear explanations.

analysis.name: Michael Goodisman

Dr.Goodisman is a not good at explaining in lectures. He talks and talks about stuff ,but never points them out on the slides and never give examples of the concept to help us . lectures are really boring and honestly don't help. class is extremely fast paced so i would recommend doing A LOT of work outside of class. he just recycles hw, learning catalytics, and textbook questions for the tests so they're pretty predictable

He is just hard for no ready, exams are so long and hard, he is a nice professor but he take his class so seriously

analysis.name: Georgia Persons

analysis.name: Jonathan Gaines

Don't take him he doesnt really teach but just reads over his hand writing in class... no communication... moves too fast in class... lots of filler words with no real meaning

Gaines is one of the most unqualified and incompetent professors at Tech. He cancels over 60% of classes and can't answer basic questions. The only thing in your favor is that his exams are open-note.

Extremely unorganized. Complete waste of a class. You learn how to do HIS problems, and walk away with no general real world knowledge. Chill dude but needs to lock in so bad

analysis.name: Gordon Kingsley
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

Dr. Kingsley is one of the best professors I have had at Tech. He made me love political science through his super interactive lectures/simulations and he genuinely cares about his students. The tests are a little on the hard side but definitely doable with some studying. I wish he taught other classes because I would take all of them!

Dr. Kingsley is your best bet if you're a PUBP student needing to take 2030 and you actually want to learn. He truly has a love for the subject that he's teaching, and with such passion like that coming from your professor, it doesn't matter how you feel about the material. He makes you WANT to learn about it, and he makes it fun. Man has a gift!

analysis.name: Lelia Glass

Too much work for a humanities class.

analysis.name: Frederic Faulkner

review_highlights.comment: One thing I'll add to Professor Faulkner's list of compliments is how well he introduces ideas. Honestly I feel like most of these reviews are written by his TAs. He's a good lecturer and understands the material. But his handwriting is SO BAD. Entirely illegible if you want to review his notes. The exams also feel really shoddy and like they want to make hard questions just because they can

Professor Faulkner is an excellent professor. His lectures are clear, well-paced, and easy to follow with annotated OneNote slides. Pretty good professor but definitely overglazed on rate my professor. Lectures are not very good for actually learning, but are decent for reinforcing prior knowledge.

Faulkner is a GOAT professor. In terms of learning from lectures, his lectures are far easier to follow than HB's, as he keeps things at a moderate pace with annotated notes on OneNote. He always keeps things straightforward, and if you pay attention in class, it is p easy to get an A if you also use the pseudocode they provide in course materials.

No attendance, but random quizzes in class. She can't teach and homework is on chegg. YOU WILL NOT LEARN IN CLASS. The light grading I've read on RMP is hit or miss. She would grade bad for me, but super well for my friends so beware. Doesn't explain anything, just follows slides, ridiculous for a class that requires a lot of written work shown.

analysis.name: Manh Khang Huynh
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

review_highlights.comment: The course is very difficult, but it isn't difficult to get a decent grade. Passionate but lacking teaching style. Lectures are inefficient; he frequently stops to wait for students to figure out proofs, saying "anyone?" on repeat, wasting time. Some may find him rude. Difficulty is moderate, but class is frustrating at times.

Im convinced every positive review on here was done by him. He laughs at people when they get things wrong, even though he sits there and begs us to interact with him. His lectures are awful and uninformative. He pretends like he wants us to get excited about math but clearly is just teaching this course as a power trip.

analysis.name: James Hays

review_highlights.comment: I thought James was a pretty great lecturer, and he explains a good amount of detail outside of what's written on the slides, so attending lectures is helpful for quizzes. lectures are not great, prof is unable to answer some questions students ask, really mumbly/hand-wavy, unclear what topics we need to know for the class, but they are recorded. final grade is based on 6 projects/labs and three quizzes with lots of opportunity for extra credit.

analysis.name: Hannah Smith

She was very good at explaining biology and her lectures made sense. The class itself is not too difficult but it does take some time outside of class to go through the material.

The class was very difficult for me, however, she is a very good lecturer and is very well at conveying and explaining the concepts of the course while remaining engaging. I did struggle throughout this course; however, when she taught the lectures, I understood the material better than when the other professor lectured, as the two rotated units.

analysis.name: Hsaio-Wen Liao

Dr. Mayer is such a great professor. analysis.name: Hunter Lehmann

What you put into this class you will get out, and nothing is too difficult with plenty of chances to make up past prob.

Y'all should be grateful this man isn't teaching multi next semester. Tests are nowhere near easy if you're not good at what he's good at in terms of sketching and thinking about math. Take him if you enjoy math!

analysis.name: Haley Steele

I don't understand why there's so many good ratings. Bad lecturer and tests are very hard. The grading is harsh and you can't afford to do bad on any assignments. analysis.name: Yi-Hsien Ho

analysis.name: Harish Ravichandar
