Miserable experience, I would not take this prof if you can avoid it. I will probably end up dropping this class.

analysis.name: Joel Sokol
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Professor made the class fully asynchronous and did not review important concepts for the exams. 
His lecture videos even were very short. When students are paying for this degree, I do not think the instruction that was provided warrants the cost.

He is very well spoken and went over the concepts well overall I will say

My first course in Georgia Tech's OMSA program was an excellent decision. Dr. Sokol's lectures are concise, informative, and often humorous. His teaching style made complex material approachable and enjoyable. Dr. Sokol has a gift for not wasting words — I learned more in a 5-minute video than I normally do watching other, longer videos from others
Good prof, explains well. Homeworks are interesting to do.

Sokol is really nice and you can tell he genuinely wants his students to learn the material. Tests make up 75% of your grade and can be a bit tricky, though he does allow crib sheets. Lectures are solid, but you're expected to watch the video lectures beforehand which makes them redundant. Homework is graded by the TA, which leads to less feedback.

Dr. Sokol is a great teacher and very skilled at summarizing things into their core substance and imparting the knowledge. I did not realize how great Dr Sokol was until I took a few more professors to compare. He's really been the best.

analysis.name: Shana Kerr
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 62 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Seems really approachable in class BUT BEWARE if you go to her office. You will likely see students in tears.  She is not known for her personality!

Kerr seems approachable and nice when you first start out, but it is quite the opposite! She talks faster in her lectures than any human should ever be able to speak. Be prepared to "infer" (her words) what parts of the book you should be reading because the readings don't match the homework or the lectures and of course not the test.

The most important thing to do is to read and take notes on the textbook, as her lectures are basically regurgitating that. You can get around the participation by doing the learning catalytics from home; going to the lecture isn't necessary as long as you read the textbook. The tests can be difficult, but reading the textbook helps.

I saw the other rating, and it's accurate. She appears nice and approachable but when contacted one-on-one does not care about the success or feelings of students. Also, her lectures are a little all over the place because she often loses her train of thought and often can't answer questions confidently.

She goes so fast you cannot possibly take notes, and doesn't explain things well. She doesnt take time on the parts that are the most confusing, and goes on long tangents about stuff that isnt relevant. There are assignments unrelated to the content are harshly graded, and take up time. During office hours she is condescending and confusing.

analysis.name: Vladimir Kolesnikov
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The professor genuinely seems like a cool guy who is very knowledgeable, but he's condescending if you don't understand advanced concepts he touts as basic. Quizzes impossible to prepare for, no matter how much you study. He teaches concepts in class + textbook is informative, but the quizzes test situational what-ifs and suck and are unfair.

While his slides are clear and he communicates the material somewhat well, his quizzes and exams are obtuse and impossible to prepare for. I understand the material. This material makes sense. However, every quiz and exam is a roll of the dice.

Prof Vlad is a decent professor. First half of the class was very theory heavy. Second half was more projects and assignments. Weekly quiz and they were difficult, which would be open for the first 10 mins of class. One midterm which was worth 30% of your grade. It's not an easy class you can breeze thru.

Took blockchain section with Vlad. Fantastic dry nerd humor. The theory lectures (1st half) are hard but Vlad does a great job explaining. Has the audacity to ask the class if a quiz was easy when the median is 60. Projects, both research and programming, are fun and good additions. Not hard to get an A if you try

analysis.name: Kevin Johnson
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 97 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Class structure is horrible, the pre lab quizzes somehow are worth more than the actual labs. The quizzes focus on minute details of the pre lab and actually don't test your knowledge on Digital Design concepts at all! The labs were actually quite fun and engaging and the TA's are awesome. Kevin himself is sort of just there. Final is horrible.
it seems like kevin puts all of his teaching effort into making this course less fun.

This class is called Digital Design Lab yet the majority of the assignments are about semantics. Kevin treats Piazza as a way to give students a scavenger hunt instead of just simply answering questions brought from the confusion of his own instructions. Also assignments seem to have random due times, sometimes 11:59 pm sometimes 6:30 pm, or 8:00.

The test and the quizzes were based on how well you can remember miniscule details instead of actual comprehension. Kevin himself is very narcisitic and unhelpful when you ask any type of question. Dont even try asking a question on piazaa, as he will simply answer it with another question making you even more confused.

If you can take another professor for 2020 do it. Kevin's lectures are overly dry and simple especially compared to homeworks and exams. His grading criteria is very unclear and he'll take off a lot of points on tests with no clear reason. Somewhat condescending when you ask questions. TA was great though.

analysis.name: Lauren Steimle
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Best professor I've had at GT. Lectures are thorough and make concepts easy to grasp if you put in the work. Homework is hard but great exam prep. Exams are heavily weighted; midterms were easy, final was difficult (I suspect they apply a curve - they dont give us the final back). Group simulations were boring and time-consuming with random groups

Dr. Steimle is one of the best professors at Georgia Tech. Her lectures are exceptional and she provides plenty of help resources as well as very interactive office hours. The class itself wasn't hard at all, but you just need to make sure you don't get lost and she makes sure to put enough resources for that to be totally on you. Take her class!!!

I have never enjoyed a class as much as I enjoyed this one. Her class was incredibly enjoyable and the weekly study sessions she hosted were beneficial. If you have the opportunity to take this class, you should hope she is your professor.
Spectacular professor, probably the strongest I have had so far. Dr. Steimle has a lot of passion and breaks down difficult concepts clearly.

Dr. Steimle's 3232 class is one of my favorite classes I've taken at Tech. She clearly cares a lot about the content of the course, and she literally gets a smile on her face whenever students ask a question. Really great lectures, building up concepts from the ground level so that the intuition behind everything covered is very clear.

analysis.name: Mike Lehman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Unnecessary, repetitive workload; Delayed feedback + grading; Unclear directions; Boring lectures; Says he's available outside of class if needed; Bulk of grade dependent on group work; Kind of goofy; If you submit + try on everything, you'll probably get an A, but he'll make you sweat for it

Assignments are typical for an English class, but many of the instructions for larger projects can be too vague and "open ended" leading to confusion and lower grades. Feedback is not good and inaccurate, and when asked about it he can be very condescending and counterproductive. Depends on his mood sometimes but got an A so its not impossible

assignments are pretty lengthy but have extremely ambiguous grading criteria, overall chill but tedious class. However, talking to him was like talking to a brick wall. impossible to get clear feedback and he regurgitates buzz words in a circle. Tanked a 60 because I was so fed up trying to talk to him. Not the worst but heavily recommend diff prof

not a hard class but def my least favorite english class I've ever taken. no assignment was difficult, but most things he would grade for completion until he randomly gave an 80 on an assignment worth 20% of your grade. I think pretty much everyone gets an a since he is generous with participation and portfolio grades.

I would recommend Dr. Lehman. I had him for thesis writing, and he provided good feedback to help get it polished before submission to my advisors. Was also really flexible with deadlines if you email before the due date.

analysis.name: Linda Wills
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Wills is a great professor and I would highly recommend her for ECE 2035. I was teetering between taking 2035 or 2036 bc I'm EE, but I chose to take 2035 because I heard she is a great professor and that was definitely true. Clear lectures and expectations. Just make sure to pay attention in class and you will be ok!

Honestly if you spend a good amount of time on the projects, you should be set for the class. I got a 50 on the 1st project and still ended with an A after doing extra credit on proj 2. Exams are fine as long as you do the past exams she gives out! Pretty fun game project.

Very easy class, exams are very easy as long as you practice. Start on the projects way ahead of time. Lots of opportunities to get extra credit and good grades. Weak lecturer in my opinion, but not too bad. Overall, class was very fun and the content was very interesting to learn

Prof Wills was great for 2035. Sometimes she can be a little scattered during lectures but she is very intelligent and knows what she is doing. If you don't understand something in class she is very approachable during office hours and will help you. The projects can be difficult, but some involve extra credit. Tests can be tricky. Study study.

Don't even scroll any further down the page! JUST TAKE HER!!! Tips: - Start the final project as soon as you get the PDF. I started the final project the week before thinking I would have enough time but was not able to finish - Don't undermine the extra credit - Practice exams are golden resources for the exams. Do as much of them as possible

analysis.name: Chin-Hui Lee
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: His lectures have to be the worst I've ever experienced. This course is on the harder side, but Dr. Lee can't explain a single concept clearly; all of his lectures feel like a review session, and he teaches like you already know everything about the topics. Might as well read the whole textbook. He cares about students, but absolutely can't teach.

I just took his class and got a C average. I could have done better by working harder to understand the course, but I might as well not have even attended the lectures. His teaching style really doesn't communicate concepts or expectations well. You'll succeed best if you treat it like a self-study. Overall, I would recommend exploring other profs.

Your succes in this class depends on who your professor and recitation prof is. Prof Lee seems to be a nice guy but can't explain a darn thing!  Even when asked a direct question to clarify a topic he was not able to give a direct answer. If you are the type of learner that needs to understand what is actually happening behind the scenes its a NO!

You will read the entire text book in this class cover to cover. The labs are time consuming but not difficult with a solid understanding of matlab. His lectures are not very exciting, he is somewhat monotoned. However, he is very accomplished an offers a wealth of knowledge. This course is the perfect example where practice makes perfect.

The class is known to be difficult and requires a lot of work, so it may not be entirely his fault. There were homework and labs every week, often on topics we would cover after homework was due. The homework was extremely helpful for tests, and the class was curved in the end. Lecture seemed to gloss over topics.

analysis.name: Chao Li
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: 学习中文很有意思！李老师 has been my favorite professor at Tech so far. His lectures are fantastic, his enthusiasm and energy is unparalleled, and his grading policies are very reasonable (and flexible if needed). I came into the class knowing no Chinese but feel much more confident now. Homework can be a lot (Chinese is hard) but is well worth in my opinion.

Literally one of the goats of all time. Li laoshi is really kind and understanding and tries his best to make Chinese as easy as possible for us (it is a hard language). Quizzes and tests are pretty easy if you do your hw and study. He's very silly and also gave us chinese snacks twice :))

Awesome professor, very kind and caring towards students. Although Chinese in general is a pretty difficult language, Li Lao Shi will help you a lot and is extremely lenient in grading as he clearly wishes for all of his students to be successful. Take his class, you won't regret it!
I learned so much Chinese from him. When I started the class I didn't understand a single word. Coming out of the class I am basically fluent in speaking now.

Professor Li cares a ton about his students and is always trying his best to make sure you not only understand the class, but are also happy in it. Expect manageable homework and quizzes, with extremely fair grading. 10/10 all around great man

analysis.name: Ling Liu
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I have been in GT CS for 5 years and this is THE worst of all the ones I have taken. The instructor is knowledgeable about the content she teaches. However, she is extremely rude to students and makes the course overly arbitrary. The rubrics for assignments are vague and the workload is too heavy for the final paper. Time wasted.

The CS6220 course experience is one of the worst at GT CS. TAs are non-existent. Homework is poorly designed with little instruction on what to do. Grading is quite random as well with no clear standard. However, if you just need an easy A and don't care about course experience, this course might actually be pretty nice.
Using public humiliation as a form of motivation is not valid. I don't need to know that another student is doing poorly in the class or is going through "family issues"

This is not a Systems course. This is rather a collection of topics the instructors is excited about. The same is reflected in the assignments, project-topics, and the review subjects. This class felt more ML and LLMs heavy than Systems heavy.

Also, lectures felt very vague, and most of the learning happened during the assignments and projects.

Genuinely a crashout, rude, grades hard for the projects and has a huge final paper. Haven't finished yet, but I've heard the curve is huge because of this. Most of this wouldn't be too bad if she wasn't extremely rude too.

analysis.name: Martin Mourigal
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Mourigal is a great professor, he was excellent at teaching, fun, and he really cares about the success of his students. The difficulty of the class is due to the physics department, not to him personally, and he really tries to help you learn the material. Overall, he's a great professor and my favorite I've had after a year at Tech.

Prof. Mourigal is a great lecturer, he clearly is very interested in the subject matter and engages his students. That being said, classical Physics 2 is one of the most difficult classes I've ever taken. Expect to work in this class.

He is excellent at explaining what is one of the hardest subjects at Tech. Had the best lecture notes I've ever gotten from a teacher and he was pretty good about posting them after each class. Those notes were a life saver during homework and while studying. Keeps class interesting and is pretty funny

Mourigal cracks jokes and is funny. Lectures: he writes everything down on a whiteboard (no slides), so pay attention to his drawings/key concepts when he writes them. He doesn't cover new material super efficiently during lecture, but the next day, he'll do "review" of the previous lecture, clears up confusion. Expect exams to be pretty difficult.

Physics is a slug at GaTech because they make you do a lot of work and the coordinator makes the tests really hard. Through all this though Martin is a great teacher! Hes funny and engaging, if there is one thing I wish he used slides for notes instead of just using the board as it is hard to follow later. That nitpick though, Martin is the goat.

analysis.name: Michael Specter
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Specter is a knowledgeable lecturer with seemingly genuine interest in the content. This semester's structure was basically the same as previous 3210 sections, except for addition of some attendance quizzes afaik. Labs are notoriously time consuming but do-able with TA help, reading, and effort. Exams are pretty difficult but curved when needed.

Very knowledgeable professor with highly-relevant industry experience with Operating Systems and security. Attendance is mandatory due to pop-quizzes. Projects are difficult... but it's a difficult course in general. Lectures are helpful in theoretical understanding. Projects test applied understanding.

This guy is the least accessible professor I have ever taken a class from. It feels bizarre to be in a class of less than 20 people and still somehow never be able to get in to contact with the professor. If you ever attempt to approach him after class he will instruct you to just email him. If you ever attempt to email him he will not respond.
Lots of reading, but interesting work and research!

analysis.name: Maysam Nezafati
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Nezafati is a GOAT! He is a very understanding and caring professor who takes time to make sure his students understand the concepts of class, not just a pattern for problems. PSS was very helpful, and his lectures reinforced material well. The homework was time consuming and quizzes were hard, but by the exams you were good and an 83 was an A.

Dr. Nezafati cares a lot about his students and if you're going to take bmed2110 definitely take it with him. The class itself is a lot of work but if you take the time to watch the lecture videos and understand the homework, the quizzes and tests aren't terrible.

Great teacher! 3 exams (1 was the final) - each one was based on what we had learned since the previous exam so nothing cumulative and each one had 3 attempts (with grades averaged). Explained everything very well. Rounded my high B up to an A (I went to every class and did every assignment) and I'm very thankful. Very manageable class!

Dr. Nezafati has been a great 2110 professor, especially with learning such different concepts than normal classes. He has always been very open to questions and helping outside of class. He seems to really enjoy the material and makes the class a lot more interesting. There is a lot of homework but TA hours are always really helpful (PAUL!!!)

Dr. Nezafati was very enthusiastic about the material. He explained everything very well and was very helpful when asked questions. He emphasized the small details, which are very important for this difficult course. He also made the online lectures this semester which were great. Definitely wouldn't want to take this class with anyone else.

analysis.name: Sasha McBurse
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Poor lecturer; goes deep on the wrong content and gives actively problematic assignments. Take her class if you're okay with location-verified attendance, taking photos of all your meals, and writing research papers where 16 peer-reviewed journal articles receives half marks on the rubric. TL;DR - You'll get an A, but at what emotional cost?

Although lectures were mandatory, we all just did work for other classes/ played Clash etc. She knows we all don't take this class extremely seriously, so she makes her lectures very fun and social. I made some new friends. Extremely chill professor who truly cares about her students, she even goes as far as trying to get to know all of us!

Had more fun in this class than I expected. She kept lectures engaging, and provided more than enough extra credit opportunities so there is no reason to not get an A. Just complete the assignments/hw on time and put a decent amount of effort into the final project and you will be fine. Mostly did other work during class.

Just show up to class and do other work. As long as you set aside 1.5 hours for each homework assignment, 3 hours for project, and do decent on the take-home quizzes, your grade in this class should be a fairly easy A. My friends who took online lecture said their class was easier, still an easy A either way, however.

She is an obstacle to one's education. Not because the class is in any way difficult, but because that is all the class serves as. She could very well cut the filler and give students lectures and quizzes every so often, instead she decides to be a nuisance and treat her students like a kindergarten class.

analysis.name: Nikki MacKenzie
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof MacKenzie is chill the work each week is light of just watching videos for lecture, doing an online quiz, and doing the online assingment. Lecture in person is also useful shell do practice problems and re explain the concepts from the last weeks lecture. Exams were easy usally about 20-25 mcq and 2 written questions.

Accounting is like learning a new language so it was extremely difficult at first, each test is worth a big chunk of your grade so be careful. She is a good professor with the hybrid class, and prepared us well for the exams. Don't fall behind, or else its extremely hard to catch back up and truly grasp the content as the tests are in depth

Kind of confused by all the low ratings. I had Professor Mackenzie for my online accounting 2101 class. It was very easy to follow along with the online lecture and guided notes. She explains concepts very well and in depth and makes it easy to understand. Exams were mostly multiple choice and were not to tough.

Accounting was new to me so I had to put a lot of time and effort into studying for this class. The professor is pretty nice, although sometimes what she says about the level of difficulty in a test is not true. The homework takes forever. If you can avoid the hybrid class, do because I think in person would have been better.

idk if all the other reviews just were horrid test takers, but this was actually one of my lowest effort classes. read the syllabus, watch the lectures, do the practice in the notes, show up to class (or not honestly) and u will be fine. group project was annoying but manageable, plus done by thanksgiving. boring teacher but what can you do...

analysis.name: Nivedita Bhattacharya
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 72 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Bhattacharya is an amazing teacher and her class notes are the best! She provides a lot of learning resources and explains concepts very clearly. But what stands out most of all in my opinion is her respect for the students.

She was a true gem virtually. Whenever I needed some clearing up or had a question on piazza, she answered in LESS THAN AN HOUR. Her lecture videos were very well done. Even when I had technical issues on the first exam, she let me email my exam to her with no complications, she was totally understanding. I WISH I COULD TAKE HER AGAIN!

Professor Bhattacharya was very knowledgeable and delivered clear and informative lectures.
She doesn't go too fast, and you can tell she cares about her students. Also answers questions thoroughly.
Very clear on how to succeed in the class, and she provides numerous resources like class notes and practice
exams to help you.

Professor Bhattacharya is one of the best professors I have had at GT. She is very accessible and helpful. She will respond to emails very quickly, and if your question can not be answered via email, she will set up a private call with you. As a non-ECE major, I felt she did a fantastic job at making the content understandable and not too complex.

One of the best professors at Georgia Tech hands down. Professor Bhattacharya is very caring and she really just wants you to understand the material. If you have any problems she will understand and help. The only downside is that the class was fully online this semester, but at least the lectures are recorded.

analysis.name: Namrata Dey Roy
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Dey Roy is one of the best professors I've had in all of literature. Our class focused on Disney's literature and critical analysis in the pieces. She definitely cared about the students, and helped everyone whenever necessary. Her grading was constructive and accommodating. Participate in class; it's worth it.

She was an amazing professor. Her English class topics are always so interesting. She was always so caring and kind. She really fostered a love for English that I never really had before college. She doesn't do book reading, instead more focuses on movies, excerpts, theories, shows, etc. Also, her feedback is tasteful and helpful. :)

This class had a fun theme and was very light. We had 3 major assignments that were all given 3 weeks before they were due. Grading was easy and clear, and the attendance/participation grade comes from discussion posts in Canvas. I had a good time in her class she is very flexible!

I took Dr. Dey Roy's ENGL1102 class over the summer, and I absolutely loved it. Every day was interesting, and we frequently watched movie clips and had debates. Grade was based on a few major artifacts and one final portfolio. Extremely funny, kind, and accommodating professor, would 100% take her class again.

Dr. Dey Roy was very caring and kind with students. The class was very fun and only had a few projects as grades and a final portfolio. What is needed to make an A is very clearly written in rubrics. We often watched movie clips and class discussion was a huge part of class. Occasional readings but no other homework besides that.

analysis.name: Jiaxi Nie
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The professor was friendly towards students and accessible. Lecture content straight from the textbook, so I ended up skipping almost all the classes. Homework & Exam questions from the textbook. The only problem was the grader, who would deduct points for solutions that were more descriptive than those in the textbook. Curves median (74) to B.

The course was quite challenging at first, and at times I couldn't fully understand. However, the professor's office hours were quite helpful. He was effective at breaking down questions and explaining concepts clearly, which genuinely increased my interest in the subject. He was also supportive to students, and grading was fair and generous.

Decent professor but reads straight from the textbook (Axler) during lectures. Doesn't really provide ample motivation for the reasons behind proofs which makes the lectures extremely dry. Goes at a decently fast pace which doesn't help either as the demotivating portions are essential to the interesting segments.

Professor essentially just read off textbook to us(Axler). There isn't much you'd get from lecture you couldn't get from reading the textbook.Grading felt unreasonable as I never recieved any feedback as to why I lost points.

His first time teaching the class. The content was quite hard and abstract, as was the homework. But after taking his course, I feel that I've learned how to self-study proofs and have improved my mathematical proof-writing.

analysis.name: Nimisha Roy
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 62 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Outstanding professor to take for a class that people only appreciate after getting an internship. There are a lot of people who are just rude to a really good Professor. Professor Roy makes the class interesting and while there are a lot of work, people need to keep in mind this is not a 2 credit hour course.

Pretty great teacher. Was very receptive to feedback and genuinely wanted to improve the course. Lectures are pretty fast, but I found that to be a plus. Overall, 2340 as a class just sucks, but Prof. Roy tried her best to make it somewhat enjoyable.

agree with other reviewers in that ur experience rly depends on whether u get a good group or not. MAKE SURE u get a good group (or switch) so ur not bogged down by project work all sem like me 😭 class is p hands off and material isn't too difficult, but assignments + tech (android studio) can get annoying and stack up if ur not on top of things

Prof. Roy did a great job with the hybrid format, although I am not a fan of the format.  She figured out a balance between hybrid, providing long-form videos with in-depth notes while summarizing the important details in class. Getting a good team in class really helps.

2340 is an awful class, but Professor Roy did a good job running it, and was very responsive to questions and overall helpful. The midterms and "mini-assessments" don't weigh a lot but require you to actually learn the "content", which led to poor performance that seemed to bother her more than it did the students. A fine professor for a bad class.

analysis.name: Osvaldo Cleger
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Cleger is such a pro. His classes are interesting, easy, and informative. You'll always ba able to get a lot out of his lessons, and he's kind of a pro in general. You should definitely take his class if you get the chance.
Osvaldo is the man!! He is adorable, and I absolutely love this class. He is very smart and entertaining. If I could retake this class, I would. Osvaldo is amazing. Highly recommended.

He is a really cool guy and cares for his students. I didn't do as well as I would have liked but mainly because I didn't participate in class that much. He is difficult, but maybe just shouldn't be teaching 3111. I recommend him to people who are very knowledgeable of Spanish.

Loved taking this professor! I learned a lot about Cuban immigration to America and more about assimilation of Cuban Americans into American culture. The papers and weekly speaking also helped me improve my fluency and depth of knowledge of the Spanish language.

A passionate and funny professor. Expects a lot out of his students in upper level classes. Sometimes expects a baseline of knowledge in other subjects (ie, got upset at class for not knowing economics principles.) Remember, upper level Spanish classes are moreso random history classes just taught in Spanish. Expect to read a lot.

analysis.name: Omar Asensio
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of those teachers yaps each and every class period. This class has a lot of potential, but unfortunately, professor Asensio makes it far too theoretical. If you want a relatively easy class and need to fulfill degree requirements, take this class and push through. If you want to learn, STAY AWAY.
Too technical, experience given for granted, too many speakers.

analysis.name: Thomas Orlando
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Decent lecturer, very disorganized class. Files were extremely disorganized and deadlines kept moving, there were two textbooks and it was often unclear which one he was referring to. Many exam questions were exact copies of homework questions, but no crib sheet or equation sheet. Letter grade was unknown until the end of the semester.

He attempts to keep us engaged in lectures. He shows derivations in lecture instead of applications, but HW and exams test on both. Weekly HW that's graded on accuracy, but textbook usually has answers. 80% of grade is from exams that reuse HW problems. He'll give more weight to your 2 midterms OR final, whichever you do better on.

Dr. Orlando is a great lecturer, but the class felt disorganized at times due to the nature of notes (no slides, only handwritten notes) and the grading scheme (he doesn't tell you what the A or B cut off is and there's random extra credit and participation points that aren't clear where they end up). Overall, good class but lots of effort needed.

The class/content was just hard itself- thermo/derivations. He posts hand-written lecture notes and goes over them in class; he'll tell you to read (I never did), but he clearly states what will be on his exams. Review sessions were helpful; study the homeworks. There were 2 exams + 1 final with 2 possible grading distributions. EC given.

Has handwritten notes that are really disorganized instead of any PowerPoints. During lectures, he goes on tangents. Tests are difficult but predictable. Extra credit involves reading scientific papers (most of which are his) and reviewing them. Class was fair enough, but it was disorganized, which made it a lot harder.

analysis.name: Dmitrii Ostrovskii
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the best math profs I had at GT. Dmitrii is knowledgeable and clear with well-structured notes, plenty of textbook references, and intuitive and interesting examples. He will make you think and put real time in, but well worth it and makes one really learn. Highly recommend PhD students to take a class with him. Prereq in analysis is helpful

Dmitrii Ostrovskii is highly knowledgeable and supportive. He's very accessible outside class and gives great help in office hours, including useful research feedback. He also provides strong resources. The presentation/paper discussion (instead of an exam) was very helpful for grad studies.

You should take his class if you want to do math. I think the bad reviews come from people who expected high school level lectures or dislike math itself. He's very smart, I learned a lot in his class. Lectures were tough, yes —as a math class should— but grading's very soft. And his availability is without exaggeration the best I've had in GT.

Higher effort (and higher reward) than I anticipated. I think he understands what he teaches on a much much deeper level than teaching the class requires. Attendance isn't mandatory, but it's fun to see how passionate he is about the material. Definitely take if you care about getting an A (plenty of opportunities to do well) or you like research.

Prof. Ostrovskii is a fantastic teacher for a challenging subject. He presents high-dimensional statistics with clarity and insight, connects theory to intuition, and is very thoughtful in his explanations.

analysis.name: Olivier Pierron
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 34 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Great teacher. Definitely knows his stuff. Entertaining lecturer and lectures are very important. Tests make up 80% of grade and they are never curved so be prepared on test days. Overall very reasonable and makes the class enjoyable.

Pierron was not good for dynamics. It was his 2nd semester teaching it, 90% of grade is from exams (2 midterms, 1 final) and 10% is from HW. HW is just write 2 questions about the problem. Spent too much time deriving equations, attempted examples, didn't finish them and sometimes was wrong. Class attendance dropped so much after a few weeks.

Dr. Pierron is a great professor. While the class itself can present difficult problems, Dr. Pierron's lecture style involves working through a variety of different scenarios using a game plan that can be applied to any statics problem! 90% of your grade is from tests, but he's a fair grader and you know what to expect each time. Caring guy too!

Avoid if bad at physics, otherwise you'll be fine. 2 midterms + 1 final = 90% of grade (9 problems total). Takes off a lot of points for messing up the math, but also gives 70% for just showing you know the process. 
Depends how you look at it, for me it made the tests more stressful and that didn't go well with my other classes.

His lectures were clear and well structured, and the homework was a breeze. However, 90% of the grade was from the exams (40% midterms and 50% final exam), so you absolutely must do well on them. Fortunately, all of the problems are from the textbook, so pracitce well and you should be fine.

analysis.name: Lee Oh
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: There are so many things I want to say but not enough words in the English language to describe how goated she is. All I will say is she has never given a student below an A in her entire history of this course and she gave out max score on every assignment as long as you did it. Goated person and goated course.

I took KOR3415 online with her. The best professor ive had at tech, she is so sweet and genuinely cares about her students. she is very understanding, and her feedback on assignments is so kind. best prof ever

I can not even begin to describe how amazing of a teacher Mrs. Oh is. She is caring, kind, funny, and a great teacher. She always has a smile and never makes anyone feel left out of the class. She wants you to succeed and asks how you are doing even outside of class. 100/10 teacher and would take again if I could!

Professor Oh was incredibly kind, funny, and helpful. She made the class fun with plenty of games and snacks. We moved pretty quickly in lecture but homework was graded easily, so it was easy to make an A in the class if you studied. There was less emphasis on speaking and practice, but she provided office hours for those looking to talk.
One of the best professors at GT! She is quite caring and provides great feedback on assignments. This was an overall easy class but engaging.

analysis.name: Phanish Suryanarayana
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: His lectures are entirely from the textbook, and the examples he does in class are the ones already solved in the book. Don't really need to go to class. Homework is straight out of the book. Tests are not too bad if you understand the examples and homework problems. Final exam was much harder than any test. WARNING: he grades on a bell curve.

Prof. Suryanaryana is a really solid professor. it's only my first sem. at Tech and considering he's my only real "engineering" class take this with a grain of salt. As other's have said, he goes off of textbooks, but doesn't post his lectures online: VERY lenient grader on tests, and utilize TA for hw's cuz its free 25%, do textbook problems

First test wasn't too bad, but the class kind of bombed it, so he made the second test and final so much easier with extra credit. He gave out so much extra credit, so as long as you go to class and somewhat understand physics 1, you'll probably be fine.
His lectures are very boring, and he doesnt upload any content whatsoever onto canvas so it is very hard to continue learning outside of the classroom

Skip lectures if you want. Just study textbook or notes you will be fine. Grading will be very easy. Professor will make the final easy if he sees everyone struggling in the class. HW are directly from TB.

analysis.name: Milos Prvulovic
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very caring and passionate professor, who is interested in answering students' questions and helping them out. Good guy, interesting lectures. Easy test(s).The projects were a logistical mess though -- released quite late into the semester, deadlines adjusted, but still we had less time and test cases didn't seem well written, causing stress for me

All the time spent for this class is on the 5 projects. You have the test cases, so pretty much a guaranteed 100 if you spend enough time and finish. 1 midterm that is pretty much IDENTICAL to the practice exam lol. Made our final optional; can use our midterm as final exam grade. Didn't go to lecture because repeat of 2200/4290. Relaxing class

Wonderful professor, makes the class very engaging and answers all in-class questions with good enthusiasm. Exploratory teaching. Slides content might be little poor but he makes up for it with good lectures

Generally good professor. Exam was super easy (exact same as the practice he gave out). Projects, although usually easy, are plagued with issues in the instructions. In many projects, students had to post their own workarounds for the rest of class to rely on. TA announcements often contradict the assignment instructions, which don't seem to update

Milos is very knowledgeable regarding what he teaches. This course was honestly really easy this semester. The lectures were interesting for the first 2/3 of the course, but then he ran out of content and they fell off. The projects weren't too hard, you could have a partner. The instructions were wrong sometimes too.

analysis.name: Olufisayo Omojokun
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 174 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: The lecture videos are pretty brief but cover enough to do the assigned homework. You don't really see the professor much outside of his videos, so your experience is based on your TA (shout out to the head TA in the dual enrollment section). Also, idk who makes the instructions for the final but I had a stroke trying to understand.

This class was essentially entirely TA ran. I only saw the professor during major exams and he rarely answers questions on piazza. His lecture videos were okay but lack details, you're better off finding yt videos online. 80% of the grade depended on 4 exams and a lot of the questions were memorization based and some weren't even relevant.

I tend to prefer asych classes and have performed well in them before. However, this class is horrible. The videos hardly cover the basics and then ur expected to apply that to the really complex hw's. Feels like you are trying to code without rly understanding how or why any of it works, which makes it rly difficult. would not recommend
Tests - 80% of class grade - full of trick questions and/or topics not covered in lecture.

I thought that the amount of effort put into the creation of this class was just pathetic. The lecture videos used are of such poor quality that any random YouTube video would explain the concepts better. It's a complete waste of a class if you are genuinely trying to learn new content (I already knew most of this so online was better). HW was ok

analysis.name: Matthew Powell
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I would give zero stars if I could. Professor docks points for not showing work in the exact format he has in his head. Students shouldn't be punished for actually understanding the material. If the answer is right, the thinking was right. Avoid if you have any other option. Your grade will reflect his inane standards, not your actual knowledge.

Don't be fooled by the bad reviews. Powell is a very good teacher, multi is just a class that combines linear algebra and calculus so people dont do well. His lectures are very clear and paced well, and you are encouraged to ask questions or solve examples in class. I would definitely reccommend taking his class.

Best professor I had this semester. Very passionate about abstract linear algebra. Exams and quizzes are manageable if you are willing to work. The class was tough due to many abstract concepts but it was fun and worth it. Definitely choose over MATH 1554, but expect to work harder.

Although professor doesn't really matter for large classes, I will say this professor teaches like you're reading a mathematics proof textbook. He introduces topics in a very formal and theorem based way followed by examples I found helpful. It works for some ppl and doesn't for others. He's a knowledgeable guy, but remember it more abt the TAs.

Dr. Powell is one of the greatest professors I've encountered- not only are his lectures phenomenal, they're accessible for people of all ability levels, and he is very approachable for question and clarification- including mid lecture.

analysis.name: Hang (Jerry) Qi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He was super nice, but not the best lecturer. A lot of the example problems were never finished and he does have a bit of an accent which made it hard to understand him. Exams were exactly like the homeworks and you got 3 attempts per question. He was also very generous with partial credit. If you study the practice problems, you should do good.

Great professor. Def bods can be a little rough sometimes, but he is good at explaining the concepts and will go over them again if you ask questions. Would take again 10/10. The homework is from the most recent ed. of the textbook, but I just checked it out of the library when I needed it, and I relied on his lectures and slides for the material.

He's a decent, not great lecturer but has a really good understanding of the material and gives good advice. Tests and homework assignments are very short with multiple attempts per question and generous extra credit. The tests are very heavily weighted and the final is 40% though.

easy to follow if you pay attention in class. very similar to physics; if you understand physics this class will be fine. the only thing is that the class is very test heavy (exam 1 15%, exam 2 25%, and final 40%), but the homework helps set up well for the exam problems

Bad lectures, hard to understand. Left practice problems unfinished. Gave good partial credit on hw and exams. 3 attempts per question on hw and exams. Exam questions came directly from textbook, which had over 100 per chapter. Self study class basically

analysis.name: Qirun Zhang
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Very kind and approachable professor who is always willing to help and accessible during office hours. However, in-class examples were often hard to see due to small writing. Piazza responses were sometimes indirect, and grades were released very late, making it hard to know how I was doing before the drop deadline.

Really nice person, very clearly cares about students. Would even go out of his way to talk to me outside of class. That being said, he's a pretty dry lecturer and he teaches off slides he did not make. He does not answer most piazza questions with anything other than 'talk to me after class or in OH'. However, homeworks and projects are easy.

Professor Zhang is a very good lecturer who describes the content in a very methodical manner. The projects, while really involved, were super interesting, and I feel like I understand a part of Computer Science that was opaque to me before this class.

analysis.name: Moinuddin Qureshi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took ECE6100 (x-listed with ECE4100 & CS4290/6290). Lectures are not recorded so attendance is mandatory if you want to do well on exams, though, they are very engaging. Exams are a little tricky but there are ungraded "homeworks" with very similar questions and you can make a crib sheet. Labs are fine if you know C/C++ and are fairly scaffolded.

Awesome lecturer but slides aren't so good and lectures are not recorded. So attendance is mandatory if you actually want to understand content. Also made the first lab worth 4% of final grade due during the first week (while registration is still open). Exams are difficult purely bc of the amount of content you need to know, there is a lot

Great professor! Probably the best lecturer I've had at GT. Teaches with slides but in the most ideal way possible by using them as support, not as a crutch. Projects were fairly simple if you have decent C/C++ knowledge. Tests were a little difficult as they were modeled after the ungraded homeworks, but doable.

Lectures like he's telling a story–makes potentially dry content exciting. Projects were excellent (if a bit hand-holdy), with smooth debugging and problems interesting enough to ponder AFK. Tests felt hard, but there was so much curving and extra credit by the end that lower quartile class grade was a comfy A. Kind prof who will brighten your day!

Took CS6290 (crosslisted 4290/ECE 4100/6100). Lectures extremely engaging and helpful. Tests a bit different than lecture content, but studying previous exams and practicing computations helped. Final was ‘Do-No-Harm'. Projects were well structured with TA debug outs. Small extra credit opportunities were given. Favorite prof at GT, he knows a lot!

analysis.name: Qi Wang
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: She is super passionate about film and also extremely educated. The lectures can be boring since she doesn't follow a specific curriculum, but cool. The entire grade is based off attendance, your final, and weekly film screenings. She def gets strict when it comes to the final project and your essay/film ideas. Do NOTTT take it at 5pm

Very sweet and passionate about film. Lecture isn't always the most engaging since she's speaking the whole time. For final projects, there were creative options (short films, poster series) or you could write a 10 page paper. She's always open to questions and is very willing to help or give feedback.

I think Dr. Wang is the victim of a poorly executed curriculum. She is a wonderful and bubbly human being, but she failed to pique my interest in film. Her class is strictly attendance mandatory (25% of grade) but absolutely does NOT need to be at all. She's worth taking as a professor in general, but I would avoid this course specifically.

Professor Wang is sweet and caring. But most of the grade goes to the midterm and final essays, which must be 10+ pages long, personally, I found that a bit annoying. There's a screening and a discussion about it on Canvas every week but you only have to finish 7 discussions for the semester.

Professor Wang is very sweet and cares a lot about her students. Lectures are long but the topics are often interesting and it isn't vital that you pay attention or read the textbook. The only grades are attendance, a weekly discussion post on an assigned movie, and two papers. She is very lenient on extensions for the papers and easy to contact.

analysis.name: Dong Qin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Qin puts in a lot of effort to be accessible and helpful for students. She cares that students learn the material and tries to keep interest high in the content. Tests are relatively straightforward if you read the textbook and lecture notes, but grading is very strict which can make getting high grades difficult.

As person, I liked Dr. Qin. She loves talking to students and having them show up to office hours. However, her lectures can be confusing and she doesnt explain concepts well. The quizzes are alright, and exams are pretty easy.

Dr. Qin is SO caring and gives great lectures. However, she's a very tough grader, and oftentimes expectations for assignments weren't super clear because of that. The expectations are high and can be tough to meet. Overall, I learned a lot from her lectures and assignments but this class will be more effort than you expect if you are an undergrad.

Qin is great, nice, & helpful. KEY TO AN A: During her lectures and office hours, if you listen to her, you'll hear tons of hints as to what will be on the test and by the time it shows up, you'll basically know what exactly is on it. The tests and quizes are also basically the exact same every semester so just study them & you'll do great.

There are quizzes every week, so make sure you're in class on those days. Her tests are EXACTLY like her practice tests so if you memorize those and past quiz information, you should be all set for tests. However, she is a super hard grader so if you miss even the smallest detail it's possible you only get half-credit for the question. Super nice!

analysis.name: Raghuram Pucha
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 93 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor was boring overall. Lectures were fine, work was easy, he posted all the instructions to canvas and you could figure out most of the coursework without his help. Very available in office hours. The problem came when we were presenting our final projects. He insulted groups projects in front of the whole class and was incredibly unkind.

Boring. Switch if you can for this course. All was fine in the class until the project presentation where no real rubric was given and then he was upset that projects did not have what he wish they would. After a section of presentations, he complained that he was tired and called other groups boring and said he was falling asleep watching them.

So much work. The drawing portion of class (first 4 week) had so much HW. After that, all homework and lab assignments could be completed in class. There is an individual and group project that occur concurrently, which take quite a bit of time to do. Its a lot of work but easy A. TAs knew nothing. He is impossible to reach via email - go office hr

I heard horror stories about him from upperclassmen before I took his class, but he was far and away my favorite prof. and class in Fall 2025. I entirely learned SolidWorks from no prior experience just due to his teaching and assignments. If you're looking for easier, try Jacobsen or Dorozhkin, but if you want to really learn, take Pucha.

Despite being a 3 credit hour class it felt like a 5 credit hour class. You will do much more work outside of class compared to other ME 1670 professors. There are also often unclear instructions on assignments. Very difficult to access outside of office hours as well, responded to 1 of 4 emails sent throughout the semester.

analysis.name: Qiqin Xie
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The professor's grading structure has changed from previous years; there is no EC on quizzes and only a little on exams. The content and lectures are mind-numbingly boring. Homework is not graded so the exams are weighted heavily. I went to her office hours twice, once she was late the other time she did not show up.

Lectures aren't the most exciting but cover everything on the tests. Helpful but infrequent office hours. Generous class policies/extra credit and the tests are reasonable but not easy by any means. Can be hard to follow the lectures because they move so fast and cover so many topics, but that's just combo for you. Would recommend her in general.

She gives a HUGE amount of extra credit that it's almost impossible not to make an A. She is a great lecturer and explains concepts clearly, and she's very good at explaining what you're expected to know for exams/quizzes. She gives 20 pts extra credit on quizzes and 100 pts (yes, 100 pts) extra credit on tests. You can exempt the final (95+ avg)

Theres no extra credit on quizzes, only 20-30 points on tests (but its usually EXTREMELY hard to earn even one of these). Quizzes are weekly and difficult, and theres only two tests and a final besides that. She does give other extra credit opportunities that I would recommend taking advantage of. Its a hard class but I heard she's the easiest.

Weekly quizzes are time-consuming to prep for but not bad if you review lecture notes. The textbook isn't bad for this course but I mainly prepped for assessments using her lecture notes. For her exams, the best way to study for them is to go through the practice questions released before each exam (problems mimic those practice questions).

analysis.name: Richard Vuduc
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: God awful class. Teach yourself to code, no instruction or guidance, fill out the notebooks to perfection after 20 hours of banging your head against your keyboard, hope TA is helpful, over rely on AI cause whats even happening, take exams with unforgiving autograder, heres some math sprinkled in here and there. whole course needs to be redone

The pace of the course is quite quick. All the work is through Vocareum(similar to Jupiter), but the app has issues with connection and others. Vocareum may grade you wrong because it only recognizes commands given during class.The class is online and there's little support from instructors.The class needs a lot more instructors to help students
The lectures are completely unrelated to the exams and the professor clearly doesn't care about teaching or whether students actually understand the material.
Teach what you don't test. Test what you don't teach. That is his motto.
I think professor Vuduc gave up on teaching a long time ago. Google could teach this class better. Tests do not reflect anything actually learned. Do yourself a favor and prepare for the worst

analysis.name: Tobias Ried
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I am pretty sure this is his first class, so he didn't really have a great grasp of what type of exam to give. He sounds like a nice guy in class, but the first exam was diabolical. There are a lot of improvements he can and should make as a professor overall, but outside of that exam, I cant really hate him. Pray in his next class he improves.

I will say this. Professor Reid is a very kind and caring man, and he genuinely does seem like he wants success for his class. I emailed him to speak a bit louder and a tiny bit slower during lectures, and the very next day he made the improvement. That said, he operates using the European style of teaching, which can be rough if you're like me.

Super nice person and professor. He very passionate about what he teaches and you can tell. However, if all differential classes were theory heavy I wouldn't have a problem, but comparing test to different sections it's kind of ridiculous. If you like theory take it with him, if you want an easier A just take it with someone else.

Professor Ried is a great professor. The lectures and tests are theory focused, yet he cares about what he teaches. He wants his students to succeed. When he gave a hard exam, he clarified he did not intend any harm, and gave a great curve for the whole class. He is very caring and is energetic during lectures every day.

analysis.name: Sandra Reid
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This might just be me, but I personally had a hard time understanding Professor Reid's lectures. I'd already taken this class in high school, so I didn't learn anything from going to her lectures. However, whenever I did go to them, they explained simple problems in a complicated manner. The tests were always way harder than the lectures as well.

Professor Ried is hands down one of the best Math 1551 professors out there. Her lectures are very entertaining and she always uploads her lectures with additional help if needed. Besides her lectures, she is very helpful in Office Hours. If you at least pay attention in class and went to Office Hours, Math 1551 is a breeze. She really is the GOAT!

I feel like exams are graded weirdly and do not accurately show your knowledge or progress. There is nothing that I specifically disliked about her, I just don't think she explained the material too deeply or explicitly.

Very chill professor. I went to about every lecture and at first she didn't use the screen and did everything on white board, but then mid semester she genuinely took the feedback from the surveys and switched to doing it with the screen. She's obviously new at teaching, but for a first ever semester teaching, she did a better job than most profs.
It was obvious that she was new to teaching, however it seemed as if she really cared. Hopefully with time the teaching becomes a lot better and easier to understand.

analysis.name: Sedina Tsikata
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Tsikata is very caring and helpful. For fluid mechanics, whilst attendance isn't mandatory, you will really be screwed if you miss a lecture! Also, the lectures themselves are quite long and have SO MUCH material, so I personally found it difficult to digest all of the information and feel comfortable for the exams.

Homework 40%, 2 Midterms 15% each, Final 30%. Lectures were boring, and slides had a lot of information, but not all of it was necessary. Grading took forever. Concepts were difficult, but she was nice and cared. A seemed impossible after M2, but there was a lot of extra credit at the end to get points back on the midterm and a curve for the final.

Short Answer: Only take if you don't want to learn the subject or want an easy class. DO NOT TAKE HER IF YOU WANT TO LEARN.

Dr. Tsikata is by far my least favorite professor I have had at GT. She does not care about you or teaching. She showed up late to class routinely and constantly had excuses for severely delayed grading and posting solutions.

Dr. Tsikata is a great human being. Her lecture slides can be somewhat uninspired, but she deeply cares about her students. I learned a great deal in her class. She is very busy, so she may seem distant at times due to this. I would recommend her still.

Often unreachable and condescending. She's straight up said she wouldn't respond to emails after I told her she had missed mine for a couple weeks. The one midterm we had was overtly difficult and no one finished in the allotted time. The content wasn't bad but the professor made it worse than it had to be

analysis.name: Sashank Varma
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: take robotics instead if youre a cs major

Attendance is required one lecture a week as he gives quizzes based on readings (they're either through Canvas with a code or paper and pencil), and these quizzes are very specific so you have to actually read. The rest of the class is very chill (though it depends on the TA) and easy to do well in. Plus the content is actually pretty interesting!
lots of reading and essay writing, course is structured more like a humanities course than a CS course. take robotics instead.

He really knows his material. I only participated in about half the classes (i.e. the days we had quizzes), but even then I could tell just how good of a lecturer he is. Looking back, I do regret not attending and paying attention to every single lecture, because I think I would've gotten a ton out of this class. Weekly discussion posts and papers.

Class is overall pretty easy. LOTS OF READING!! I only went to class the day we would have quizzes bc his lecture style wasn't beneficial to me but I enjoyed the structure of the class. ACTUALLY READ THE READINGS because he will ask the most specific questions on weekly quizzes that you wont know unless you read it (even though they are open note)

analysis.name: Zhaiming Shen
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
