Lectures were not that useful for me, so I can't comment on that. But the assignments are good and the project is cool. He's pretty generous and gives a grace period for every assignment as well, although I suspect he just uses it as an excuse to not let students who have submission problems complain to him.

Lectures are very dry and are just presentations with 60+ slides per, ended up not showing after a few weeks because it was hard to care, maybe its me but the lectures just were not interesting in the end.  Homeworks were annoying but did not take too much time.

The professor is not caring about student and lecture accumulates a lot of materials and TAs are not respectful. Also, the quizes are so hard and the materials also disorganized. I feel the prof did not prepare the materials well.

"-1 Too verbose: 5 or more sentences" for a question that did NOT say anything about being brief. Lost another point on another homework for another UNWRITTEN requirement (had 96% accuracy needed 97% or something for full points). They made a question that was IMPOSSIBLE to get full points (needed 100% accuracy with 0 model size).

analysis.name: Clint Zeagler
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Easy class; however, it entirely depends on your section TA. Some TAs legit don't care and give you a 100 for almost everything, and one in particular... is lets just say takes she takes her job too seriously.

TAKE THIS DUDE, absolute goat. tells you what's on the test and CIOS is up to 5 points on final grade. Mandatory lectures are easy to attend, easiest class I've taken at tech. Couldn't recommend more.

He has amazing lectures and often tries to facilitate discussion among students. Lectures are short, but definitely informative, and he makes it abundantly clear that the class will be easy as long as you put in the work. If you do take him, make sure to participate! Most people don't, so it makes you stand out and will make lecture so much better!

Lectures were engaging and lasted 20-30 mins each. Tells you all the questions on the upcoming exams the class before, so you don't even need to study. 

Discussions vary based on TA, so this will be a hit or miss. Still, interesting and not difficult.

This is probably the easiest CS class you will take at Georgia Tech. 100% would take again.

I got the impression he was tired of teaching the course since not enough people engaged properly, but he taught the class well. Section was great and the TA I got did a great job of facilitating conversation.

analysis.name: Zachary Tidler
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great guy, super funny, loved his class. Has a lot of passion for what he teaches and it's evident in his lectures. The workload was NOT difficult at all, and he really put in the effort to make sure that his assignments were interesting rather than busywork for the sake of assignments.

GOAT Professor. Chill class. Lectures were there if you needed them, but otherwise his tests were very straightforward and 80% of questions came from the practice tests. Overall, very good guy and pretty funny sometimes.

rlly recommend this class, easy A and gpa booster. practice quizzes are given for midterm and final and theyre literally the same thing so just memorize. i spent lectures doing work for other classes, but his lectures were still intriguing, hes nonchalant. most assignments were discussions boards and surveys, didnt need effort for the class at all

Genuinely interesting class even though it's a gen ed that everyone has to take. Lectures were super interesting, Professor Tidler definitely knows what he is talking about and is interested in the topics. Enjoyed going to class, exams are copied from practice given in class, meaning they are not hard if you put in a little bit of work.

I am such a fan of Prof Tidler's lectures! He was very informative, but he made the content feel super interesting and fun and relatable to students in his lectures. He is forgiving with grades and offers late submissions. The only issue I had was I missed some of the in-class work, so make sure to stay on top of that if you take his class.

analysis.name: Leonardo  Abbrescia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the better teachers for MATH2551. His exams are generally easier than other teachers, and although his lectures can be boring at times, he is lenient in terms of grading, always looking for areas to give points back. Overall, he is a good teacher. MATH2551 requires effort to grasp some of the concepts, but nonetheless I would take him again.

he's not exactly the most “student” oriented prof, as i think he prefers teaching mainly upper level math majors so teaching a sophomore math gen ed didn't seem up to him. regardless i think he explained topics pretty well and dr lehman's videos could supplement any lectures you missed. wish he had more office hours tho. made tests decently fair

He's a great person, but inexperienced with teaching an underclassman course. He wrote all lecture notes from scratch with questionable handwriting, so I spent most lectures deciphering instead of understanding. He doesn't post note templates; homework content was not tested. I didn't know what I should know for exams until the end of the semester.

tbh I learned mostly from studio, do NOT skip it if ur taking multi it's a lifesaver. Lectures could have been way worse, he's good at introducing topics but usually started losing the class during example probs. i agree that it would have been much MUCH easier if he simply copied the alr typed out notes from dr. lehmann, as his exams were similar

I see why people weren't happy with Dr. Abbrescia, but I was also able to manage an A without being exceptional or great at math. He did a lot to help us after a really bad first exam by giving us a curve and lowering grade bounds by 3 pts and his other 2 tests were pretty fair, j lots of algebra. Honestly I learned mostly from lehmans videos too

analysis.name: Abdon Neto
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He used a cheap microphone with a hurricane wind sound effect. Lectures felt like they were inside a wind tunnel, and the teaching style with many fragmented and repetitive sentences didn't help. All lecture notes appear to be created with an index finger and trackpad. Many students got tired of copying down random squiggles and left mid-lecture.

There are 104 students registered in my class. For the past 2months, I am one of the only 2/3 students who show up. Don't take this professor. His accent is unintelligible, and so is his handwriting. He doesn't use the whiteboard/ppts/computer; instead, he writes on a messy piece of paper and projects that, but it is impossible to understand.

There were 105 people signed up for this class, I walked into a lecture recently and there were 2 people still showing up to class. He seems like a great and caring guy, but you LITERALLY cannot understand a word he says because of his accent. Avoid taking him, but if you do, understand you'll be watching online lectures from Barone/Mayer to learn

Professor is hard to understand during lectures and has bad hand-writing. It's not that bad because lectures aren't attendance mandatory and you can always go to a different section, so if you have his class I would either go to another one or read through the posted lecture notes.

It's difficult to read his handwriting and even more difficult to understand what he is saying. I only attended class to get the extra credit, and I typically spent that time watching the lecture videos or reading the notes of other professors. You can succeed in his class, but only by learning the content elsewhere and paying attention in studio.

analysis.name: Abigail Mills
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Mills is solid-- a good lecturer and great with offering resources. For 3127 though, attendance wasn't required for lectures but WAS for the studios w/ TAs. With how lenient she is with access to resources, you don't have to attend many lectures. Be weary of written assignments you get b/c they come up pretty often and are fairly long (1000 words).

Attendance wasn't required for main lectures, but studios run by TAs were mandatory. The professor assigned many readings and writing-based assignments. She was very involved during lectures and explained concepts clearly.

Professor Mills is like a breath of fresh air while at Tech. Her lectures are good, and tests are easy if you do the readings. Some of the readings are a bit long, but very helpful for the papers you will have to write.
Lots of reading. But the lectures were interesting enough. I didn't get a ton of feedback up front, but her office hours were great.
She's just rude. Like in class she seems nice but comments she leaves and emails she has ATTITUDE. Cant stand her tbh.

analysis.name: Abdul Zureick
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Zureick is super laid back and insanely intelligent. His courses are on the unorganized side, but you will learn SO much. He is caring and wants people to learn. What I loved about this course in particular is that he reads through the code and dissects it in lecture, and then does example problems. It helped drill the concepts down.

I LOVE Dr. Zureick. He is so caring and helpful. He is very laid back and does not state due dates or a schedule. He gives 2 exams, a group project, and hw. The hw is average and he is very willing to help during office hours. The exams are a good reflection of the hw and open notes. He is willing to change lectures to what interests the class.

Homeworks in this class is pretty light, but a lot of the grade is from your exams and the research/special problem project. Lectures can be kind of boring. Class is very disorganized as you get very little instructions for expectations of the project, deadlines, etc. Midterm was easy but the final was rough imo

analysis.name: Alex Abramson
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Awful professor, doesn't know what he's talking about. Uses TA's for everything and then doesn't check it leading to numerous errors. His teaching is writing another professors notes on the board that he messes up and doesn't understand. He overall seems to not know the content or care enough about the course to put in effort.

Abramson was super apathetic towards the class. There were only 5-6 people in the class and he delegated lecture time to an uninterested grad student who was always unprepared and bad at teaching. There were also constant mistakes in the homework's. Just a poor job and I hope he improves. I would look for a more experienced prof.
Super based. Gave me the highest grade on the project out of all the professors teaching the class.

analysis.name: Agniva Roy
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof Roy's classes and homeworks were very proof heavy, but the exams were pretty easy. He knows the material pretty well and really cares about his students. The exams often had extra credit too. He spent some time reviewing 1553/4, so there was only a little bit I had to do by myself. If you got through 1553/4 ok, this class won't be bad at all.

Professor Roy is incredibly understanding and cares about his students - he was one of the only professors to modify the class and communicate with us clearly when we moved to remote learning. His lectures are interesting, and the weekly assignments aren't difficult. Exams are straightforward and fair, just study the lecture notes and do the HW.

Professor Roy truly cares about his students. He is very understanding and will accommodate to his students as requested. His class is distributed by the homework, midterm, and final exam. You need to go to class and follow the textbook or you will be lost. As long as you work hard, you will get the grade you deserve. 10/10 TAKE THIS CLASS

Professor Roy is a great professor with very reasonable grading criteria and class structure. He is a solid lecturer, and I would highly recommend him to other students. As long as you keep up with the material and stay consistent, you will do fine in this course.

analysis.name: Haiyu Zou
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 83 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He's just beyond the average human in every way.

Lectures are fine, very fast-paced. Doesn't fully answer questions when you ask, just reiterates the answer he got. TA was bad, didn't explain answers to worksheets well. I failed the first midterm (hardest one) and never seemed to recover (test heavy course). Will ask you to simplify difficult fractions in a short amount of time (EX: 9.5/5).

Overall he was a good professor that cared about his students, but 1712 is a heafty class and the lectures were extremely detailed and in depth. The course is mainly graded on 3 Midterms and a final, but there were plenty of extra credit opportunities. If you struggle with probabilities, you will find this course very difficult.

He is a mid professor, my TA was awful which made this class more difficult than necessary. The grade inflation at the end of the semester goes crazy with homework and extra credit, so most people end with an A or B. 2 weekly homework and if you go to all the studios + lectures you get extra credit. Not the worst ever, but doable with some effort

Class is very test heavy, but overall it was an easy class! Lectures jump around a bunch of different math topics and he posts the slides on Canvas if you miss them. Haiyu never hesitated to answer questions or give help if someone was confused. Make sure you go to studio, you'll get 1-2 extra credit points!

analysis.name: Pradeep Agrawal
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: AMAZING professor. You will here stories about this class, and while he is an extremely difficult professor, he is an excellent lecturer and is extremely willing to help you out! Also, if you put in the effort, a B is atleast manageable, because he has an enormous curve (anywhere above a 65 should guarantee you atleast a B)

Although Dr. Agrawal does give difficult tests, he is a great lecturer and very willing to help you during his office hours. You will learn so much in the class and taking a class with Dr. Agrawal is very worthwhile. Definitely one of the best lecturers in the chemical engineering department.
Worst professor ever. English is bad and he cannot hear you too. Homework grading is harsh and unreasonable. Exam is hard too.

analysis.name: Ian Afflerbach
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Afflerbach is the kindest and coolest professor I have had so far. His classes are very interesting, and the projects assigned are very manageable. Though there is a lot of outside reading, be sure to do it so you can participate in class. 20% of the grade is participation. Afflerbach is very responsive to your comments in class and is  helpful

Dr. Afflerbach is great. Interesting/engaging lectures. While he can be a little bit of a tough grader on some things the main thing he's looking for is effort. If he sees you're trying, you will be rewarded. Any time I needed help or had any questions his feedback was always EXTREMELY helpful. I would recommend his class.

Dr. Afflerbach was an amazing English teacher! You can really tell he is passionate about teaching. Although there was a lot of reading, it was interesting and the discussions we had in class were always great. And go to office hours! He always gives very helpful feedback and seems to genuinely care about his students.

Dr. A is hands down one of the best teachers I've had. His class is structured as a discussion that he facilitates incredibly well. He's knowledgeable,  fair and engaging. He sincerely wants to help you succeed as long as he sees your efforts.

If I had another English class to take, I would 100% take another class Afflerbach taught. If you need help, stop by office hours. They make a huge difference. He is very responsive to emails as well!

analysis.name: Phillip Ackerman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Brilliant professor and clearly a top-notch academic with a lot of knowledge about the history of the field. Comes across as intimidating initially but he's very approachable in truth. You'll learn to think about things differently from taking his class, and it's nice that the tests are very straightforward.

He is really smart, knowledgable and passionate which is great if you are interested in what he is teaching. His tests are pretty much exclusively beaded off his notes and I think he does a great job of testing the important stuff as opposed to the minutia.
Dr. Ackerman is a big name in his field and teaches quite well for a Georgia Tech Psychology Professor.

analysis.name: Aditi Das
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Das connects course material to real-world examples. She occasionally goes on tangents, drawing on her own experiences and broader scientific topics which makes the class fun. The class required significant studying. I appreciated the open-note format, though she mentioned that future offerings may be closed to internet access.

Instructor was an expert in the subject matter and taught with a lot of enthusiasm. There was lot of opportunities to score through homework, quizzes, and open exams to promote conceptual learning. However the lectures was fast pace with occasional misalignment between lectures and exams. The FRQ portion of the exams were hard.

The class was engaging and rewarding . Dr. Das's enthusiasm and emphasis on understanding the “why” behind complex pathways helped me move beyond memorization. The course felt like a meaningful exploration of metabolism pathway and strengthened my appreciation for biochemistry as I pursue medical school.

This class prepared me for metabolism and the TCA cycle, which is great for MCAT. Real-life examples made complex ideas fun and memorable. She didn't make us memorize TCA cycle which was a big relief.  The mechanistic approach in the class and challenging ‘what if' questions pushed my thinking. Overall, I liked the class.

Course was reasonably organized, engaging, and intellectually stimulating. It is application-based, with problem sets and exams that emphasize critical thinking. There are also a lot of easy quizzes. The professor is supportive and creates an inclusive environment. Exams are challenging and office hours are helpful. Gets you ready for med school.

analysis.name: Adrian Gardiner
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: His lectures were unengaging and by the end of the semester there were probably less than 10 people who would show up. I had to self study all the topics for the midterm and final which ended up being fine. Most of the grades came from the homework/projects so that helped a lot. He also gave us 3% extra credit added to our overall grade.

He cares about the class and is helpful if you ask, but he struggles to connect with students or make the material engaging. Lectures are long slide walkthroughs not reflected on exams. You're expected to learn SQL, Excel, and Orange on your own. Practice exams help, but most learning is self-taught, and in class content is not helpful.

Really interesting class, he is a really chill and funny guy, but lectures were dry, but you don't really need them for the assignments. Cool to see new ways to make business processes better including work with AI agents. Mainly includes group and individual assignments on various ways to improve business processes and individual work in SAP.

Had Prof Gardiner for 2200 & 3745. He's a nice person, but very boring lecturer, so its hard to make yourself go to class. His exams are always tricky & require a ton of studying. He pulls from the readings for the non-coding part of exams. There is a project in 3745 as well as coding challenges and HW that help your grade a lot.

This rating is meant to help future students as well as Adrian Gardiner if he is reading this:
The teacher only taught about theory in the class, speaking at about 15 words per minute. He taught a total of about 3 classes on the technicals of excel and SQL which is OUTRAGEOUS considering the homeworks included FAR more than what we learned in class

analysis.name: Ali Adibi
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great teacher, easy grading policies - 2 grading schemes based on whether or not you want to do the homework (+5 points if you do). Wants everybody to learn alot and do well in the class. Hands out extra credit points for class participation.

He is a great teacher. He teaches very difficult topics in a way that everybody can understand. He asks questions during the class and offers extra points for that. For his grad courses, you can easily get A. So respectful, friendly, and caring professor. One of the best teachers I have ever had during my education.

Professor Adibi was awesome. Had him for ECE 3025 (not listed as a code) and was one of my favorite ECE classes. Amazing lectures, covers a lot of ground but in a way that made me interested in the subject and engaged the entire period. Exams were tough but he always had review sessions outside of class plus lots of EC.

Great guy, with a great way of teaching the course. Gives you extra points for answering correctly in class. Doing all your homework can get you up to 5% extra credit. Not an exceedingly strict grader either. Very approachable and all in all, a great teacher.

Dr. Adibi is a fantastic lecturer who is clearly very passionate about the material in this course. Participation can grant you extra credit. While the homeworks are challenging, they are graded generously and also provide opportunity for extra credit. Exams are fair so long as you understand the examples from class.

analysis.name: Ada Gavrilovska
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Difficult to understand as she speeds through topics in rote fashion. Can't keep up unless you are already familiar with the material, but then what's the point of her teaching? Basically worthless if you are actually trying to learn something. You're better off studying a good textbook, otherwise, the class only serves to validate prior learning.

I strongly believe that anyone with any passion for computing should take this class, you learn about so many foundational papers and implement some of them in very interesting papers. Only downside is the TAs are not too helpful as they all say different things and constantly grade wrong but can be rectified with a piazza post

Ada teaches super important OS fundamentals pretty well and provides a ton of insight into how the systems we learn about have affected the world. Midterm + final are pretty difficult, and there is some ambiguity on projects, but overall one of the better classes I've taken.

This course has the workload of 2-3 courses and needs to be rebalanced. Though the projects are super hard, the tests (midterm + finals) make up for 50% of the grade which is unfair as not everyone tests well. I also frequently ended up watching lectures on the same subject on Udacity to understand things.

The projects are the most difficult projects I have done in the grad school. There are 46 papers to read in the entire semester. The exams were not so difficult but to prepare for the exams it takes a lot of time.

analysis.name: Alexander Adams
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great intro to health sensing with hands-on use of ECG, EMG, RESP, and more. Alex is a supportive instructor who gave thoughtful one-on-one feedback and cared about our success. One of the most unique MS courses at Tech—covering biosignals, sensors, software, and many topics of your choice. No prior experience needed. Would definitely take again!

This is an enjoyable, project-based course with a strong hands-on component. Through practical labs, we learned various techniques for processing health-related signals. Professor Adams is approachable and fairly lenient with grading. He's also very supportive when it comes to helping refine the research topic for our final paper.

Alex is a very kind professor. I had minimal coding knowledge going into this class, and he and the TAs made sure I was supported throughout the whole course. The class emphasizes process over a perfect final project; if you show effort and growth through your work, you'll get a good grade (and likely learn some new skills, too!)

Awesome summer class! Learned so much about sensing methods and designing future devices. Assignments were engaging, and Prof. Adams was generous with guidance and resources. Put in the effort, and you'll create a project worthy of your résumé. Highly recommend for anyone interested in health sensing!

I really enjoyed Health Sensing and Interventions with Professor Adams. The class was interactive and project-focused, with hands-on work using real health sensing hardware. No exams, just meaningful projects that helped me apply what I learned. Highly recommend for anyone interested in health tech and biomedical applications!

analysis.name: Austin Adams
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The GOAT. Not even a real Professor, but he's a Professor in my heart. Piazza posts were fire, class was fire. Real zoomer energy, super approachable. Probably my favorite teacher this year; knows what he's talking about too, so not just a set of jokes in a trench coat but actual good educator. Wish he could teach the rest of my sysarch classes.

Even without being a professor and teaching for one semester, he is the best you can get at GT: Easily understood lectures, numerous metaphors for concepts making them easy to grasp. As long as you attend lecture (they are a good time), you will get an A. He is just that good. More professors need to look towards how he teaches o7

The best thing about him was he didn't read of the powerpoint and made us understand the lecture but one thing is he writes most of the stuff on white board so if you sit really back you probably wouldn't see it clearly but overall still the best one I have had at tech
Great teacher. Clearly passionate on what he is teaching. He explained everything really well and did a great job of creating connection between the class and real world applications.

Got put on the spot to teach 2110 and did an amazing job with it. Super funny guy and very knowledgeable about the content, he had no problem answering any question thrown his way even if it was out of the scope of the class. Class is very project heavy (50% of grade) and content is not a walk in the park but Adams made it enjoyable and manageable.

analysis.name: Aditya Kumar
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class has very little example and lots of derivations. He tends to repeat derivations that he already did the class before rather than doing actual examples. He's very accessible and helpful outside of class but he can be a bit condescending at times if you don't understand immediately. Overall he's pretty good.
His lectures were really good and he posts all of his notes online. Tests were fair, study the homework and practice problems and you'll be fine

Dr. Kumar is an incredibly kind professor, and he makes the material super easy to understand. Sometimes his lectures can be boring, but he posts all his notes later on. He was always willing to talk after class. The tests were pretty easy if you did the practice problems.
Great Prof. Extremely helpful outside of class. I struggled in Defbods, but he helped me out a lot.
Great at teaching the content of the class. Makes it very easy to understand.

analysis.name: Adegboyega Oyelere
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Avoid at all costs for this class. Terrible lecturer, no practice or homework, and we are behind Biochem 1. Worst communication I've seen in a while. Even with GT documentation, he will not follow up for exam remakes. Class grade comprised of exams only and two random concept quizzes. Poorly paced and condescending. Tests don't reflect content.

Awesome professor Biochem 2 is a p hard class. Grade is just 90% exams and 10% quizzes - quizzes are open note. Exams are straightforward for the most part but you definitely need to study for them and he provides a fair study guide and practice exam. He's really knowledgeable on the topics and good at explaining!

I'm guessing that the difference between current and previous semesters was the modality, but if you can take him in person, avoid it if you can. Lectures were extremely poorly paced, and tests were badly designed, which doesn't make sense for a class almost entirely graded by exams. Very little structuring or support materials, and no crib sheets.

Lectures were super disorganized and the slides were super unhelpful for studying. He speaks so quickly, has really poor transitions between concepts, and just does not explain things well. I probably learned 5% of this class from him and the 95% rest from YouTube. Exams were fairly easy but there was basically 0 review/prep material for them
This class is so weird. Nothing feels to match up and exams take up so much of the grade. If you can take another class, do it!

analysis.name: Adam Steinberg
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Steinberg is phenomenal. AE2010 thermo-fluids is an extremely difficult course, but Steinberg made the material very clear. The homeworks are hard, as are the tests, but the TAs and professor grade rather generously. The lectures are optional, but I strongly recommend going. If it is too early for you, the professor posts the lectures online.

Genuinely great professor. The course isn't easy, but Steinberg really does his best to make sure his students understand both conceptually and practically. As long you as also put in the same effort as he does, you'll do fine. Tests are open note, open book, so they can get pretty difficult

Steinberg was a great professor, and his lecture style was beneficial to my learning. He explains concepts which we then apply in the homeworks (41% of total grade), but also does a few basic examples in class to help students. Tests are extremely difficult, but open notes and textbook, and he is a very lenient grader. Would recommend taking him

Dr. Steinberg is a decent professor. Early on, he mainly lectures without examples, making concepts harder to apply. However, he improves over time, balancing examples and lectures better. Homework is challenging and heavily weighted. Exams are very tough, but the class is curved, so doing well is possible if you do a LOT of practice.
Grades incredibly harshly, test averages were in the low 60's high 50's. I took the course since many people gave him a high RMP rating, but I honestly regretted taking thermo with him.

analysis.name: Ahmed Saeed
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The professor is knowledgeable about Networking, but the course management was lacking. ALWAYS REQUEST REGRADES for homework, as TAs rely HEAVILY on the autograder. The professor's handwriting is VERY hard to read, and lectures focus on concepts while exams are calculation-heavy. The midterm had unfair conditions that the take-home didn't balance.

Take-home midterm did not offset the unexpected technical difficulties of the original midterm, which had unfair testing conditions. Lack of feedback on HW and exams; many unanswered Ed posts. TAs/prof gave misleading info about HW/exam questions. Lectures are very conceptual while HW/exams are very computational. Prof Ahmed is pretty solid though.

Spam regrade requests on EVERYTHING! Make up any reason or else they'll never give u partial bc TAs only autograde (half can't even explain anything). Pray u don't have to talk to the prof bc he does not care. Take a diff prof, others are actually nice & don't expect u to "already know the answer" to the HW (which is why they never release answers)

Professor is super passionate about the material. Lecture notes are not great and the textbook is hard to read. Exams are super content heavy so its best to stay on top of it individually. Homeworks aren't that great of a prep resource as  hws use wireshark and terminal which aren't tested on exams. Programming Assignments are not really useful.

Passionate professor who cares about networking and his students. Admits his mistakes clearly and works with students when they have issues. Handwriting in notes can be hard to read / understand sometimes though. Tests ended up being pretty hard (Fall 2025) but they got curved pretty hard so it ended up being fine

analysis.name: Ahmed Ahmed
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Extremely easy class. The summer online class is asynch with a couple of weekly assignments. Each week, you have reading quizzes (very light) and discussion posts. The only major assignment was the final "exam", in which you had to create a presentation on one of the multiple Arabic topics learned. Overall, the class was very easy, and I recommend!

I took his class for ARBC 3501 (Men-Women in Islam) and I really enjoyed the class. Probably the easiest option for a humanities credit. Sometimes assignments could be annoying but even the slightest effort can get you an A. Also very understanding and let me turn in a lot of stuff almost a week late.

Prof. Ahmed was a very helpful and respectful professor who made this class an enjoyable experience for his students. You have to show up to class and you get 3 absences before it affects your grade. The quizzes are not worth much and are easy. Just participate and you should get an A for both 1001 and 1002. Great professor and cool class!

Great professor! He does a good job of teaching Arabic basics and providing lots of different types of practice (reading, listening, speaking, etc). At first the class was intimidating since many people were already able to read Arabic, but I felt much more confident by the end of the semester. Very welcoming class environment!

Prof. Ahmed is so so kind and really caring. Sometimes the lectures are sporadic as theyre based on what students need, which was more difficult for me. No previous experience for me, so definitely had to put in work. Once we sat in the dark and just relaxed for a bit during a miserable hell week. Prof Ahmed is so sweet and it was a great class.

analysis.name: Mustaq Ahamad
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This professor has vague expectations.  He does not grade anything in his courses, yet claims that each assignment is crucial.  He does not teach anything, and he often invites guest faculty to lecture.  Final grades are arbitrary based on how much he likes you.  If you're an InfoSec major, good luck because this professor's courses are mandatory.

I'm giving him +1 pity point because he comes off as a nice genuine guy. His lectures are extremely dull and dry. He took an interesting topic and made it as boring as possible. Another major flaw was that all the projects were very poorly written and outdated. Errors in those instructions probably wasted hundreds of man hours across all students.

This professor is unclear and not helpful. He is unaware of what he is discussing in class and forgets what he tells students. He is not consistent with his grading, and changes his standards of grading each week without telling students. He does not understand the meaning of communication. Good Luck, avoid a class with this professor if you can.

I took him for Secure Computer Systems and found him to be knowledgeable with great recorded lectures (online). Two exams are worth 60% of your grade, but grades on a curve based on class performance. There is a quiz each week (worst 3 are dropped) and 4 projects ranging from easy to hard (proj4, start early). I learned a lot, would recommend.

His class is pretty useless, and his lectures are dry and boring. All you do is read boring papers that you learn almost nothing from. I did learn a little bit from the projects, though. I think his grading is predeterminedno matter what you do or don't do, it seems he's already decided what he's going to give you. Avoid if possible.

analysis.name: Krishan Ahuja
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: His course consists of filling in the blanks in his lecture slides. It's pretty boring. Mac-PC compatibility messed the pictures up. All in All pretty good.

He is an OK professor. His tests are almost easy if you have good memory. He is very quick in teaching, doesnt explain alot. always says "I dont have time to go in detail, please refer to you textbook". Tests consists of fill in the blanks which are directly from his slides, and the rest is problems. Thermo is supposed to be hard. but it was easy!

Prof Ahuja is your good old-fashioned professor. He goes over the material quickly, and often refers to the textbook, which you can for tables. The slides are often a mess, which requires a better understanding of the subject. However, the tests and quizzes are very doable. You can get an A in the class, just make sure not to fall behind.

Dr. Ahuja is an expert on aeroacoustics. His lecture slides are very organized and handy to use for whatever purpose. He doesn't go through details in lecture so after-class reading is important, even though the exams are really easy. Be intuitive and active in his class!

analysis.name: Ahmet Uzer
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you go to Georgia Tech, you HAVE to take a class with Uzer - you'd be missing out on so much otherwise!

Really funny guy, a warm, helpful professor who clearly loves what he does and wants nothing more than to make you understand the material. If you ever have the chance to take Uzer, you will not regret it.

The class in itself was pretty much a joke, but Uzer was an awesome prof. He is the ideal "college lecturer", meaning he's great at teaching the material and keeping you interested, but he's not available outside of lecture. HILLARIOUS! If anything, go to class for his jokes. (By the way, he looks like a crazy Ben Stein). Very easy class overall.

The class is hard, but it isn't Uzer's fault. He explains the material VERY well. The tests are REALLY difficult, but all of them are. There is a lot of homework, but it's manageable. Whatever you do, DO THE BONUS HOMEWORK. It seems like a hassle, but it is definitely worth it. Uzer knows his stuff, and he's really funny. I recommend taking him.

Insanely difficult class, but he definitely taught me how to think more like a physicist. He will take the time to make sure you understand the material, but he'll grade you as if you're taking classical mechanics, not intro physics. Very funny and intelligent. He will likely remain one of my favorite professors.

analysis.name: Mishal Ahmed
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great professor. Attendance is taken randomly over the semester. All material is covered in lectures, textbook is not necessary at all. All tests and final exam are all multiple choice, and they're all pretty straightforward (there will be one or two trick questions though). Overall a very fair professor. If you show up and pay attention, easy A.

Homework is just the right difficulty, enough to keep a solid grade and still learn a lot. Tests are all multiple choice, and he drops your lowest. Final is cumulative. Possible extra credit from CIOS. I don't like random attendance, especially for an easy class like this, but that is whatever. Good lecturer, you learn all you need to in class.
He clearly cares about students and what they think of the course, responds well to feedback.

Relatively enjoyable class. You get to drop your lowest test! The professor really knows and understands the material, so he is able to answer all questions clearly. His tests did sometimes have tricky or confusing questions, so read carefully.

Quality professor, or actually grad student. Gets grades back in an hour most of the time which was great. Good clear lectures. Fair exams. Very solid choice for an econ professor, would recommend. Only downside is random attendance checks.

analysis.name: Ahmet Erbil
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The class itself (Intro modern) was pathetically easy and shallow. Prof Erbil, however, is an incredibly passionate guy who clearly would have loved to just teach to anyone who wanted to learn, even without requirements/grades/external motivators. Seems to me he wants to go into more depth than the course allowed. He seems like a really cool guy.

I had Erbil for Physics 3. Physics 3 is much easier than Physics 2, and unfortunately he realizes this. Unlike Physics 1 and 2 where the worst test is dropped as a buffer, in his Physics 3 class there is NO hope of redemption after a bad test grade. The final was 10 MC at 25% of your grade: one stupid math error drops your final grade 2.5 points.

I had Erbil for Thermodynamics.  He's a fairly easy teacher as far as grading goes; he's well-grounded in reality and insists that his students do likewise.  He's average when it comes to explaining material or fielding questions.  Erbil's big advantage is that he's very, very concerned about his students' learning.  Overall a solid teacher.

Compared with other physics classes at Tech... his was awesome.  I really enjoyed him... and yes he does talk about himself a lot, but it's all interesting... he knows a bunch of random famous scientists (or so he says).  Anyway, if you can get the old tests... you'll be golden.  Oh yeah... and an 80 is like an A... so that's nice too....

Without a doubt the BEST professor I've had at Tech.  He is always willing to help his students, and you can tell he enjoys teaching.  His tests are very reasonable with most of the averages turning out to be in the 80s, which is very high for a class at Tech.  I really enjoyed the class and would highly recommend it.

analysis.name: Adam Decker
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 106 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: His ratings are high for a reason. He makes lectures for a course that is almost strictly memorization entertaining. Anatomy always ends up with the worst lecture times and locations but it is always worth going. Attendance isn't mandatory, but I would strongly recommend going as he sometimes tests material not in the slides. Very caring guy too.

Hands down my favorite course at GT. I appreciated the course was very challenging and I was up for it. Dr. Decker takes difficult concepts and breaks them down in a unique way so we understand. We just finished drawing the brachial plexus and although challenging it was fun to draw along with him on the whiteboard. I can't wait for Human Pathology

I was really struggling with anatomy and school/life  in general. He was the only professor that took the time with me outside of class to help me. I will forever be grateful for this man. I wish more professors on campus cared half as much as Dr. Decker did.

WE LOVE DR. DECKER! Genuinely the best prof I've had at GT. Lectures are engaging, go to them! Even if you can pass the class without attending, the things he says in person will stick with you for the rest of your medical career. Exams are a bit tough, make sure you deeply understand the content and are not just memorizing. Flashcards are a must!

Had him online for short summer session. His teaching format was powerpoints with attached audio narration on each slide. He seems very passionate about what he does, which makes the lectures interesting and engaging. He also adds some hilarious jokes in there. Really cool. Down to earth. The assignments teaches you about yourself. Take good notes.

analysis.name: Aaron Hillegass
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Hillegass is the GOAT. Dude does it for the love of the game. He's a professor that actually cares about the content he teaches. Lecture is not required but I heavily recommend you go. You really don't want to miss out on them. If you genuinely put effort into learning AI for this class, you'll really come to enjoy his class, which I did.

Professor is very caring and willing to help. But the class is unexpected HARD. Other section is totally different and much easier(really). I think I prepared well for the exam and did well in the previous HARD homework, but the real one hurts me. Be ready to spend tons of hours weekly on this course if you really want to take his.

Prof. Hillegass is a caring and genuine guy. From what I've heard, the exams were a bit harder than in previous semesters, but everything ended up working out, and studying for the difficult exams is rewarded with a deeper understanding of the material. The final competition project was super fun and was an amazing way to apply what we learned.

Professor only allows one submission to autograder per day, making it incredibly difficult to do homework. Homework is also extremely time consuming and covers material not taught in class. Material covered in lecture is very simple but then material expected to know in homework is complicated.

not an easy class by any means, but hillegass is a great lecturer who clearly knows and cares about the material. while i didn't get to interact with him directly, i've heard that he is very personable. there were some hiccups at the beginning of the semester, but he was more than fair with correcting and accounting for any issues with the course.

analysis.name: Aaron Hansen
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This class is rewarding, although difficult. The material is basically just learning how to program a GBA in C. Tests are quite difficult and graded harshly. HW5 is not for the faint of heart. The end of semester project is fun but lots of requirements, so will take up a good bit of time. For the love of god attend lecture, itll help on the HWs

Professor Hansen is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is super passionate about this class and the topic is very interesting. Expect a lot of hw and labs! The tests are very hard and some might even consider harder than CS2110. GO TO OFFICE HOURS! Aaron is very good and caring prof. but the materials are better taught 1v1 than in class

The best class i've ever taken, that being said, get ready to WORK. Hansen's a great lecturer and clearly passionate but the nature of the course is super difficult. At least 5 hrs a week in the first 2 months and 10-15+ after that. He's very accessible and kind to all students, but the TAs carry the course. Go to office hours and recitation!!

The HW took up my wkends and especially the last ones had me (and the whole class) going crazy. Aaron is passionate about this topic, & I respect him. The TAs are FANTASTIC and work their heads off helping and explaining every important detail to us. I wonder sometimes if 2110 would have been less stressful...The final project is fulfilling though.

all-around good guy. he knows this class is insanely difficult and time-consuming, and is trying his best to make it bearable. the TAs really carry this class on their backs; i was practically camped out in office hours every single week. class is fun, but expect it to be your heaviest workload by FAR.

analysis.name: Aaron Santesso
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Santesso is a great professor for LMC2000! He cares a lot about his work and makes assignments feel meaningful and directly related to all the texts gone over in class. He's a tough grader, but he is also willing to give feedback and support--he truly does want you to do well. If you're an LMC major, I definitely recommend starting with him.

The material is very interesting as it's mostly focused on satires in different mediums. Overall, the class requires dedication as the essays are long. Quizzes are weighed heavy, but simply taking notes and studying is enough. His feedback on essays is insanely thorough. Dr. Santesso is funny and passionate about the subject, making the class fun.

Santesso will push you to be your best! However, this felt discouraging when I received harsh grading & criticism on the essays (50% of your grade) I put a lot of time & effort into. Considering his lectures are very fascinating (& him saying B= "very very very good" but A= "exceptional"/"wow"), I recommend him to anyone wanting fun, a push or a B.

i think someone else mentioned but hes a good professor but i just didnt really vibe with him but thats different for everbody. why did i just find out he has a wikipedia page? He tears into your paper but dont take it personally; dont think your writing is goated he'll knock you off that peg.

A lot of people claim Santesso grades too harshly, but I disagree. I felt like all of my grades were fair, and the feedback was beneficial to becoming a better writer. I would say my only "issue" was that he did not use Canvas for grades, so you need to keep track of your own and do your own calculations. Also, participation in class matters!

analysis.name: Aaron Lanterman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Amazing teacher! Clearly has a passion for learning and is a phenomenal teacher! He was super respectful of all students, and willing to help people out. His grading feedback was also very helpful.

This class is still really hard and requires a lot of work.  However Dr. Lanterman's enthusiasm was essential to my success.  If lecture was boring I would have never made it.  He's goofy, but in a very helpful way.  Great class!! Also there is a lot of emphasis on the lab and homework, so one bad test won't kill you.  No curve in my class.
Professor made the subject material interesting and had awesome lectures.

If you get the chance to take a class with prof Lanterman u need to do it. Im taking gpu programming with him rn, I pester him and his TA every 2 seconds and they respond within an hour. He runs all his chats through discord, his lects are all recorded. He is the best u can get as far as a professor goes. No exams in case you are a bad test taker

I'm taking him online in the summer of covid and in 5 weeks he was already 2 weeks behind schedule. He knows the material and presents it well, but doesn't give any tests or quizzes, just a final project. He asks out feedback about online classes which I appreciate, but he also inserts his political views into the lectures. Just teach me signals!

analysis.name: Aaron Hackett
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Majority of your grade in this class will be a project where you work closely with a company of your choosing. Class times is super interesting and really fun.
The professor is a former P&G brand guy who connects theory to application in a way that's easy to understand. My favorite class at Georgia Tech!

Really caring professor and engaging lecturer. He cares a lot about student feedback and always gave us time to discuss and voice concerns/ "I wish you had done this..." about the way his assignments were structured and presented to us, after an assignment was over. Listens and implements the changes too. Loved the course, had lots of group work.

Incredible guy, incredible professor. This class was extremely applicable to the real world, and it was also probably the most engaging class I've ever had. Read the book very closely to make an A on the exam, but trust that it isn't as bad as he makes it sound. Super clear grading criteria. Fair amount of work (all done in class), but worthwhile

Dr. Hackett is incredible and very knowledgeable with a great background in brand management. He really cares about students learning the content. His lectures are interesting and the class is really only focused on two projects and one exam. Definitely READ THE BOOK to do well on the exam. Definitely recommend.

analysis.name: Aaron Levine
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Levine is an amazing lecturer and professor. For his Stem Cell Policy & Ethics class you have to write policy memos and he is very clear on what is needed to be addressed. He critiques your policy with worthy comments so you know how to fix. He is very accessible out of class and is willing to work with you. Definitely would take again.

He's the best teacher I had at Tech. For an ethics class, he's surprisingly unbiased about... everything. This makes his lecture interesting, as he gives different perspectives on many controversial issues. There are clickers, so attend class. Difficulty level is fair, and I received an A fairly easily, even though I didn't give it my all.

Definitely work the old tests and find those answers yourself in order to study for the tests. His tests are just as detailed as the practice tests with some of the same questions. IMO, lecture was somewhat boring, but you need the attendance grade. 3 tests. 2 papers. Attendance. Discussion section.

Dr. Levine is an amazing professor. He's very accessible and knowledgeable, and he cares a lot for his students. He only grades by a few assignments so don't slack and you'll be fine. Final was a take home exam and major grades were group research papers.
Class is interesting and you don't really have to do the reading. Attendance is only necessary to do like 1 PRS questions per class. Also, he is really really attractive.

analysis.name: Aaron Colton
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The grades in this class are mostly projects, each project is different so it's a little more interesting than writing papers. Dr. Colton is really passionate about his subject and his feedback is really helpful. I was struggling in this class for a bit but with the chance for revisions, it helped my grade a lot.

Class is very interactive which is fun. HIs grading can be weird, but is always accessible and he just wants to see students try their best. Heavy reading, but you can finesse it easily.. He's really invested in his topic which made the class more fun. Participate, put some effort, and you'll get the A. DO NOT BUY THE WOVEN TEXTBOOK FIND THE PDF.

Not that many grades just projects. Gives lots of feedback on your projects and you're allowed to revise one project I only got a few more points when I fixed a major issue tho. You're allowed to miss 3 classes and there's a participation grade at the end so I guess if you miss more it'll affect that. We had books but we didn't use them too much.

analysis.name: Aakanksha Angra
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She's great. She doesn't lecture too much, but when she does she does a fantastic job. She provides interesting videos and gives us fun group exercises. We were given everything we could need to succeed in the class. As long as you show up to class and do the online assignments, an A is attainable. I definitely recommend taking Dr. Angra.

She is a horrible teacher. The way that the test are written doesn't correlate to the lectures given in class . The point distribution on the test is ridiculous (15 questions and written response the written response is 22 point! out if the 35 pt test. The way that she grade as well is completely ridiculous if your response does not match you fail.

Unorganized, no communication it seems between her and TAs. 3 exams no drop, no extra credit offered and says she doesnt believe in curves. Unwilling to meet or answer questions at times. Exams are extremely difficult and lecture is too vague. Nothing prepares you for the exams.

analysis.name: Aaron Greenwood
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I learned a lot and I wouldn't change anything about my experiences. If you don't like the road you're on, pave a new one. Or find a different road. But I stuck with this road, meaning I didn't drop this class.

He is a great professor, he really cares about his students. HW is really heavy so it will require lots of work. The only bad thing about him is that he takes forever to grade stuff so you dont really have a way to know how you are doing in class, but in the end he gives everyone good grades just for the effort shown.
HOT. Easy enough if you pay attention, which is pretty difficult when you can't stop staring at those perfect eyes...

analysis.name: Cyrus Aidun
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Aidun is a decent pick for fluids. The class is hard and he goes over practice that is mostly applicable to the tests, but lectures can tend to get boring. With the proper focus, an A is very doable as the test grading is slightly on the gracious side. I took it in the spring and an A actually ended up being a 91+...

Can't ask questions during exam, only at beginning. No calculators. Explained concepts well in class with plenty of examples and grades generously. Curved the class down(??) Extra credit by computer project that adds 10 points onto final grade, nearly impossible to get all 10. Start early as soon as he releases, it takes more than a week to finish.

Dr. Aidun's lectures provided us with great notes even though lectures were not always the most engaging. Your grade is basically made up of just tests. I did well by putting the notes slides in my crib sheet, but I am not sure I actually learned the concepts. The cutoffs for A, B, etc. are decided at the end of the semester (they could go up!)

He's a really good professor! Class was a little boring but he makes up for that by being a REALLY generous grader. Extra credit offered. The final was optional. Exams based on textbook and homework. Accessible outside of class and really cares about you making a good grade. I would know I started the semester failing lol. Best option for Fluids!

Idk why the high ratings. They're wrong. I made an A, but he screwed the class by making the cutoff 91% for A and 82% for B. His lectures are so boring I felt like napping every class. His HW's are just him selecting random book probs. with untaught content you have to Chegg. I did well on tests (90%) by putting slide problems on formula sheet.

analysis.name: AJ Zucchero
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: The most amazing professor I have ever had!!  Can we spell out NOBEL PRIZE

analysis.name: Ron Johnson
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 45 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Go to class each day + listen, you'll get an A. HW optional, pop quizzes. Get old exams/quizzes-he reuses them+do HW IMO: I HATED this man. He's arrogant + demeaning to students. If he's wrong or makes a mistake, he acts like he meant it + that the students are idiots for thinking he could be wrong. That said, he isn't unfair, but VERY IRRITATING

I know that my previous review was deleted from this page, somehow. Johnson is the worst professor that I have ever had at GT. He's rude and condescending, and he's impossible to talk to about grades. He pretends to care with his "motivational" lectures, but when you try to talk to him, he is very rude.

idk how hard the class is over the fall but i took this course during the summer and it was a joke. Don't get me wrong, the course material wasn't the easiest to understand, but with 4 people so far we haven't had any real exams. Our first exam we all took together as a class and he just gave us all 100s. Do with this information what you will.

Dr. Johnson's lectures are boring and he's not lenient with grading/extensions, but he's pretty fair. Not hard to get an A if you 1) Go to lectures and write down every in-class example problem (they are re-used in quizzes and exams), and 2) Participate in lecture (he will exempt students from the FInal who have participated and have high 80s.)

General Johnson knows his material inside and out. He teaches quickly during class, going through dozens of practice problems, but he will always stop and clarify if someone has a question. Go to class, sit in the front, and participate in calling out answers/next steps during practice problems. Exams/quizzes contain 0 extraneous material.

analysis.name: Akanksha Menon
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great professor that ACTUALLY listens to her students. She has decent lectures and slides (they help when supplemented with the textbook) and is very organized. The class keeps you busy with multiple assignments but so do other ME 3345 sections. I really don't get the other comments that speak ill of Dr. Menon. Don't hate the player hate the game.

Most of the heat transfer professors at Tech are terrible, Professor Menon is still difficult (it's a difficult class), but is an incredible professor. Her exams are extremely fair, homework isn't too intense, and lectures are very well made. Go to class and do all the practice she tells you, and it'll 100% pay off.
Just don't take her. Trust me. Your life will suck.

analysis.name: Ian Akyildiz
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: You'll learn more by not attending his lectures. He doesn't curve at all, so ignore his 'don't worry about your grades you can make it up' and seriously buckle down. I highly suggest just not taking his classes, half the class got C's or below in a graduate class.  While the class topics sound appealing, teach it yourself, trust me.

The grading was based on 3 homework assignments, 2 tests, and a final which didn't leave room for error. Don't let the fact that tests are open book make you think they're easy. The test averages were low (C's and D's) and grading was harsh. The professor was rude and often called students out for just asking questions.
Exhaustive class. A lot to learn.

analysis.name: Aki Matsushima
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I had Matsushima-sensei for both JAPN 1002 & 1001. She is so incredibly accommodating to students, if you're sick and miss a quiz or exam she allows for make-ups. Very interactive lectures (expect to be called on at least once per class). I felt 1002 to be a significant difficulty jump from 1001, but matsushima-sensei made the transition easier.

Foreign languages are hard, let alone one that often uses three alphabets in the same sentence. Yes, you'll have to put in the work and you will have to memorize a lot, but Matsushima-Sensei is very clear about what she expects you to know and grow.

She makes it very easy. Great professor.

Matsushima-sensei is an amazing professor. She is very kind, makes expectations clear, and provides plenty of resources for studying and test preparation. Her lectures focus on speaking exercises. You are well-prepared for homework. Foreign languages take attending class and additional studying, but she makes the process very enjoyable. がんばって！

She forces in class participation which is scary at first but you'll get used to it. Pacing is rough at first with the alphabets but the course load is pretty light afterwards. She grades super nicely and gives exam formats beforehand.

Matsushima 先生 is so sweet. Japanese was my favorite class this semester. Attendance is mandatory, but going to class never felt like a chore. There's group work too, but it's fun to get to know other classmates. This doesn't feel like a 4 credit hour class at all. There's lots of extra credit too, so I never had to worry about my grade. ありがとうございます！

analysis.name: Akash Dixit
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

Though I got A's on the tests and obviously understood the material, I didn't do as well in the overall class because his projects were ridiculous.

The class may seem difficult at first. But as soon as you understand the expectations and ask questions. You will be fine. The professor is happy to answer all questions as long as rules are followed.
He super nice. In office hours he spent well over an hour making sure i understood the topic. His grading is a bit inconsistent... but overall he is very fair. He also curves very nicely.

analysis.name: Anila Shree
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Shree was a phenomenal professor. She cares about course content and genuinely wants students to learn. She sets clear expectations but is flexible. Her classes aren't boring and the assignment structure is good. I looked forward to attending class because of this. She cares about students, allowing extensions and flexibility if needed. 10/10!

Professor Shree was my favorite professor by far this semester! She is so passionate, interesting, and understanding. I am by no means a English major but she has a way of engaging you and making you want to contribute in class discussions. HIGHLY recommend her class, it was an amazing experience!
She's very nice and cares about her students a lot. Take English with her for your sanity, especially if it's your first semester at Georgia Tech.
I LOVED prof Shree. She is the chillest prof. If the class needed an assignment pushed back, then it was. The most understanding and fair grader out

analysis.name: Andrei Shubin

As a new professor, he was pretty good and seems to care about becoming better. If you have problems with him, you could just watch Jankowski's recorded lectures since attendance isn't mandatory.

Brand new professor, and his teaching style makes that clear. I ended up just watching Jankowski's lectures halfway through the year. He has an accent and tends to teach out of the textbook. However, he was a kind and caring person, and he was genuinely interested in improving as a teacher. I believe in a few years he will be a solid professor.

This course is tough, but Shubin is extremely kind and caring, and he's always open to answer whatever questions you have, even staying late after class ends. I watched Jankowski's lectures for exam review, but I fault this to this being Shubin's first semester, and I definitely think he'll improve bec he is very open to feedback.
A nice professor with a bit accent

Shubin has a bit of an accent and doesn't elaborate that much but will any answer question you have no matter how long it takes. He is very smart but not the best lecturer. We fell a little behind towards the end of the semester

analysis.name: Angus Wilkinson

review_highlights.comment: He's a cool dude. Pay attention and put in some work you'll be fine. He's really friendly  but never opens his eyes

The main benefit to this class is the grade replacement from the final. Wilkinson teaches in an annoying manner, glossing over some key concepts with his popular saying of "you should have already learned this previously." The exams are pretty difficult, and he leaves no time on the iClicker. Overall though, if you put in the work you'll be fine.

Lectures aren't that helpful because he spends a lot of time off topic or talking about applications of chemicals and things we don't need to know. The class has graded in-class questions and he gives very little time to do them before closing them. Chill guy I guess but maybe more suited for upper level classes.

He closes the clicker questions WAY too fast (basically encouraging student to use ai for quick answer), and he makes fairly simple concepts sound complicated(by shifting off to some theoretical stories). He also lacks enthusiasm in the content of these simple chemistry.

Lectures were really enjoyable especially for a 1 credit class. Great sense of humor, assignments were fine besides the poster and learning portfolio at the end of the semester. Otherwise a very straightforward class.

analysis.name: Antonia Antoniou

review_highlights.comment: I hate statics, but I loved Professor Antoniou's class. She's extremely caring and genuinely wants her students to enjoy learning. Pretty much all of class time is spent on practice problems, but she goes around the room and helps everyone individually. HW is a bit harder, but if you can do the HW, the tests will be easy.

Antoniou was sweet, but very disorganized, making it hard to follow lectures and catch up outside of class. Homework grading was often harsh, and feedback often unclear. Tests sometimes didn't match content we learned in class. I respect her effort and passion, but it was just a bit too disorganized and messy for me.

The professor was amazing. The lectures were well structured and the tests reflected them really well. She gave a lot of opportunities to get help from her personally. Mini projects were fun and easy to do. Most of the content was easy if you paid attention in class. Would 100% take again.

Very nice, but very busy and disorganized. I started receiving 90% of my grades for this class after the last assignment was due, so I had no idea what the grading would be like or what my grade is in the class. She and the TAs waited until the last minute to put grades in and only allowed us to see our total grade once it was final.

Good at teaching content only part was that there were very few actual notes taken. Lots of practice problems but sometimes it felt like I didn't have notes to look back on as to what was happening or why. Optional final clutch

analysis.name: Charlotte Alexander

review_highlights.comment: She is very enthusiastic about the topic and gave good examples in class. You get a double sided crib sheet for every test, so as long as your notes are good then the tests are easy. There are also 2 case studies which are hard to study for, but the class is easy overall. There is no homework which I liked and you don't need the textbook.

Literally one of the best teachers at Scheller. Explains concepts simply using real world, RECENT examples. She is super engaging and intelligent. Not a lot of grades, just exams, random attendance, and case studies. Exams are easy and multiple choice. Case studies are also easy, just review the content before. You also get a crib sheet for exams

Super nice professor, very enthusiastic in lectures. She uses good examples and engages the class, easy to pay attention in her class. Tests were kinda hard but you get a cheat sheet. She was very available for help and going over past tests, genuinely cared for student success. Definitely recommend her as a professor

By far my favorite professor I have had at Tech!!! I thought this class was going to be boring, but the material is actually really interesting and she is super passionate and knowledgeable about it. She makes sure her students are understanding the material and is easily accessible by email and office hours. TAKE HER!!

I 100% recommend her for legal aspects. You get an entire page front and back for a crib sheet on tests (type this). You do need to pay attention somewhat in lectures and show up. The last unit there aren't slides so be sure to pay attention and take down notes. Super easy class tbh.

analysis.name: Alan Ritter

review_highlights.comment: Really horrible lecturing, shocking considering GT should be good at ML. He struggles with basic public speaking (every other word is um, like, basically, right) making it hard to stay engaged in the material. The assignments have little to do with his lectures so youre forced to learn it all on your own. Avoid Alan if possible, at least for 4641.

Professor Ritter absolutely killed my interest in machine learning. It is impossible to follow along with him in lectures as he simply circles and scribbles all over the slides. The projects and homework assignments are nothing like what he teaches in class -- at ALL. The only way to succeed is to teach yourself everything and pray you're close.

Don't go to the lecture, just read the textbook and online resources. He will only talk about the math, not the reasons or concepts behind. He is very good at killing your interest in machine learning. And you will never get answers for any assignments because he wants to re-use them in the future. God bless you if you have to take his class.

Easily the most difficult class I have taken in my time at Georgia Tech. The tests and assignments in the class did not relate to the lectures or material and you are forced to heavy research outside of class to complete questions. Lectures are extremely math intensive, but not very useful since he just says exactly what's on the slides.

Professor Ritter poorly explains material in-class while only underlining the material he is talking about and not writing anything down on slides. Each lecture leaves students lost in the material. Assignments have very little relation to the material taught in the class requiring outside resources to help students guess at an answer.

analysis.name: Anastasios Fragkos
