The processor had a strong accent which did make lectures hard to understand at first but they do really help conceptually! Test were CONSIDERABLY easier than other sections just make sure you can do the weekly studio worksheets and you're good! Also quizzzes were very similar in concepts and problems to the hw so def try to pay attention to those!

Lectures were an unhelpful recap of the pre-lecture videos. I didn't have any issues with his accent. His lectures are super unhelpful. His notes are almost impossible to read, he makes frequent mistakes so the information he gives isn't always reliable. analysis.name: Paul Alonso
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Tough grader but honestly didn't care about that too much. What I did care about was busting my behind the entire semester with an A average, just to get a participation grade that dropped my average by a whole letter. Mind you I had documentation. Not understanding. Maybe he just didn't like me. Made me not want to minor in spanish. Devastated.

He is very knowledgeable on the subject, which made the class interesting. I learned a lot and developed my writing/speaking skills, however he is quite intimidating whenever you speak up (which is required for participation). He takes points off of assignments for seemingly no reason and there's a decent amount of homework so beware of that!

It's a good class. It can be difficult, but as long as you do the readings and put in good effort, you'll get a good grade. Professor Alonso is a little intimidating but has good spirits and wants all his students to be engaged and interested in the material.

Not an easy A. He grades essays harshly, particularly on grammar and Spanish errors. A few presentations, and he assigns lots of reading and movies to watch - like 3-4 hours before each class. He really likes to talk (ramble). He does know his stuff and has strong background in journalism. His English isn't great which can lead to some confusion.

Would not recommend, especially if you want an easy A. His grading is ridiculously harsh and he can't explain why he took off points well either. He also is intimidating and will call you out randomly to answer a question. As much as the content was interesting and he knew his stuff, the stress of going to this class was not worth it.

analysis.name: Allen Robinson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: His lectures were really good, but the rest of the class was not great. The labs take way longer than the designated lab time, and the exams and lab quizzes are a massive time crunch. Thankfully, even though it takes a lot of time, it's not difficult to get good grades on the homeworks and lab reports.

Dr. Robinson is an amazing lecturer - writes everything out on the board. Cleared up many misconceptions from 2040. Exams are super time-limiting. Labs are extremely time-consuming. If you can separate the very stressful exams and lab structure from the great lecture content he is amazing.

~6 hours a week on lab. 6 HW ~3hr . Lectures are GREAT. you must go! Nice person but you need to contact him in person, because he is very slow to email. he has a lot going on (W/F in office only i think). Homeworks and exams graded very harshly, and prep material is limited, but I dont care because I like Robinson and I learned a lot. ~4 pt curve?

He is a good lecturer but has absolutely no concern for the well-being of students. Never replied to students' emails, and impossible to find for office hours. He had confusing due dates and assigned difficult homework, barely relevant to the class, which made everything seem poorly organized.

Prof Robinson is very good at breaking down complex topics into simple ideas, but his lectures are only 50 minutes so they move fast and aren't long enough. Labs each week take varying amounts of time and closer to the end you almost will have to go to open lab hours. Though, if you read the theory in the lab manual beforehand it'll halve the time.

analysis.name: Alex Hsu

I wouldn't recommend the professor as hes poor at consultation and doesn't answer questions for practice midterms and finals or in general. Overall, don't take him.

He just read off slides and did not explain well. But a lot content with details showed in exams. Didn't give very useful resources to prepare for exams and the content from lectures did not fully cover content in final.

All the nice reviews are spam and written on the same day by children, go and read them. He's definitely a chill guy but he's just so so so bad at teaching.

analysis.name: Aldo Ferri
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Attending his lectures help. They're super clear, & I had a thorough understanding of the material just attending his classes. Doing the previous year exams he gives is all the prep I needed to get an A.

if ur hearing good things, it's all true. he's really funny and good at making dyn easy for u. his exams seem extremely scary when ur taking them but he is such a lenient grader that if u try to maximize points, you're completely set. offers around 3 full points of extra credit total if you use every opportunity (DO ALL HW QUESTIONS) take ferri!!

The goat of Dynamics. By far the best teacher I have had at Georgia Tech. Super clear lectures followed by example driven classes to help you understand the topic. Super friendly guy and answers questions clearly. Love Dr.Ferri.

He clearly cares about teaching and it makes showing up to lectures rewarding. He clearly prepared his lectures to make them clear and understandable. Homework can be difficult, and unfortunately does not count towards much of the grade. Exams are 90% of class grade but he gives plenty to prepare for them, and they are not unreasonable.

Fantastic professor. Class can be hard, but that is just the nature of a masters level dynamics course. He is super accessible and a great lecturer. The homeworks are really helpful and he includes the final answer to make sure you are on the right track. The tests are very similar to the homework but don't require a ton of actual math.

analysis.name: Alberto Fuentes
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Fuentes is great. His lectures are interesting, he's clearly passionate about the course material, and grades are diversified among reading quizzes, worksheets, and exams. I really enjoyed INTA 2050 and highly recommend taking his class.

I enjoyed Dr. Fuentes class, the lectures were fascinating; I learned tons. He's a fair grader. Just be ready to take detailed notes if you want to succeed. Readings are assigned 2x a week. Quizzes are on the readings, so take good reading notes too. Exams are bit difficult, but multiple extra credit opportunities at the end. True difficulty: 3.5.

Was an interesting lecturer but the class is way too difficult for an elective class, be prepared to put STEM level effort into a non-STEM class. He doesn't post lecture materials or notes and moves through his notes pretty fast.

Fuentes is great. Lectures are in-depth and thoughtful. He cares about what he is teaching and he's good at it. You actually have to do the reading assignments and attend class to complete the in-class worksheets. Exams are 60% lecture material, 40% readings, but it all really works together. Similar difficulty to an AP history class.

Dr. Fuentes is a great professor-- one of the best I have had at Tech. The work I had to put into to succeeding in this class was worth it since lectures were valuable. I left with so much more knowledge. I really appreciated the readings quizzes at the start of each class because it meant everyone was doing the work and made for a better class.

analysis.name: Amanda Hampton
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: Not the greatest professor but the class is really easy especially if you took calc in high school. I was surprised to see such negative comments about her because my experience wasn't terrible at all. Although some may find it boring, I actually enjoyed her lecture style. She gives so many optional practice problems that undoubtedly show up on the test, so literally just do the work and you're fine.

Students who already took a calc course struggled less with her. There are suggested problems you HAVE to do to succeed (even though there is "no hw"). For an intro calculus class for non-STEM majors, she offered "reading the textbook" as a way to improve performance. She writes out definitions and walks through practice problems rather than teach.

She isn't even a true professor, this class took up tons of study time. By the end of the semester we had been given over 800 practice problems, not mandatory but they are the only way to prepare for the test. The problems she goes over in lecture are a fraction of the difficulty of what shows up on the test. 0/10 class avoid at all costs

I know many had a negative opinion on her, but she wasn't bad, I enjoyed lecture. At the end of the semester she went through everyone's grades and tried to get everyone to a C (minimum). Her exams were very difficult, if you have no calc knowledge, but she adjusted as we went on. Go to office hours, she noticed any effort on your part.

analysis.name: Amanda Stockton

Not a bad professor: very knowledgeable, just frustrating sometimes with poor communication (cancelling class or moving it online last minute, unclear deadlines, last minute changes in homework, doesn't really respond to emails/Teams) and going on tangents getting super far behind in lecture. She does provide a lot of resources, it's an easy class.
Very nice professor who's very engaged with the material. TAs review sessions are also a saving grace for midterms

this class is intense mainly due to the nature of the content. Fair warning, stockton's exams rely very much on critical thinking and synthesis of the content which was very annoying cuz there was no practice for this in class. However, there is a huge curve, idk how I made an A lmao

analysis.name: Mandy Moore
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment:
Wish I had more space, but to summarize:
-Teaching style made the course's fiber arts theme surprisingly engaging
-Graded on participation points (only need 100/130 for an A)
-4 fun & easy projects with minimal writing (video, podcast, presentation, and embroidery)
-Most importantly, she is the kindest and most understanding professor I've ever had

I had a very pleasant experience taking the class. Homework mainly consisted of short readings that were to be discussed in class. The final grade was not done on a points scale and instead was about completion and shown effort over the semester, which took out a lot of stress.
It's very clear that Dr. Moore puts the student first.

Dr. Moore is a great professor! The projects we did were non-traditional, including making a podcast, a blog post, and learning a new fiber craft, which I really enjoyed. She makes it very clear exactly what we needed to do to achieve an A for each assignment, and gives great feedback. She is also flexible with deadlines and attendance.

some readings before class, but very doable and easy (you can also get by without doing the readings). class theme was toy stories (pretty interesting). all the assignments were either process assignments in preparation for the main artifacts or reflections on the artifacts (all easy). is boring occasionally. All the assignments are self-graded!
Genuine participation class. Lots of projects but reasonable class time is given for them.

analysis.name: Amelia Stokolosa

review_highlights.comment: The class is pretty engaging overall, and she genuinely cares about her students. Best class this semester!! I used to look forward to class every week, because yes, it is THAT fun. Would take her again 100% . The exams can be challenging at first, but it's all centralized across all 1553 sections.

Overall super engaging class, she goes a little fast sometimes but takes on the somewhat complex topics in an approachable and clear way. Do not recommend skipping any lectures though as a lot of the concepts pile up on each other quickly, especially towards the end of the semester.
Sometimes goes a tiny bit fast but other than that, she is slay and had us learn a tiny bit of French for funsies. Some classes made me laugh out loud

analysis.name: Amy Stone
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

This teacher had a great personality and was very funny, but was a poor lecturer. She consistently made mistakes during lecture that confused us all. She would need time to figure out problems as if she didn't prepare for lecture. Most of what I learned was through research online in my own time since her lectures were inadequate.
She is not knowledgeable about the subject, but has a great personality.

analysis.name: Daniel Amsterdam
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly

review_highlights.comment: Very caring, allowed me to do alternate assignment when I had not done the reading. Very engaging lectures, and the reading was genuinely interesting, even though there is a lot of it. Genuinely cares about the topics he teaches, and I feel better off having taken the class and learned about the topics we did.

Prof Amsterdam was the best history instructor I have ever had. His lectures were well structured as he gave outlines for each one and his test were all from the lectures (so u gotta go to take notes cuz he doesn't post notes). Tests were very straightforward and the required readings were actually really interesting to read. Really caring

He's an amazing instructor, and even though attendance isn't mandatory, you will need to go to class in order to get a good grade since he doesn't post the lecture content on Canvas. Very chill guy, he dropped a few questions in our tests if he felt that it was confusing. He also dropped our lowest midterm. Make sure to take good notes

Lectures are not mandatory but DEFINITELY reccomended. Studying the material on your own or based off the notes makes the class so much harder than it should. Amsterdam is an amazing lecturer who makes the content  engaging, concise, and easy to follow, additionally he makes it very clear what parts of lecture are important/on the exams

Overall a great lecturer and a good guy. Also, the class is really easy- the only homework is 1-3 page readings for classes and 3 1-2 page "papers" throughout the semester which are essentially an automatic 100 if you do them. You have to go to class though bc notes are not posted online, but lectures are interesting and usually have a 5 min break

analysis.name: Amanda Girard
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can

review_highlights.comment: Extremely and unreasonably tough grader for no good reason in what's supposed to be a fairly easy A class. Gave terrible and unclear feadback on assignments and didn't really follow the grading rubrics that were given. Overall awful, one of the biggest mistakes I made at GT was taking a class with this professor. 0/10

One of the worst professors I have taken at Georgia Tech. Extremely slow and unreasonable grader with astronomically high expectations. She has quite the ego for an LMC professor and will not hesitate to defend herself when asked about grading. AVOID THIS PROFESSOR AT ALL COSTS!

(CS3001) She has some weird policies including dropping students' overall grades by 10% if they miss 2 lectures. Overall mid prof but not the greatest person.

(CS3803) AVOID AT ALL COST. WORST professor ever. RUDE, CONDESCENDING, DISORGANIZED. Does not understand either communication or anything technical, but teaches Tech Communication. More boring jokes and her life stories in class than useful lecture material, but taking notes is required as mandatory attendance. Changes syllabus arbitrarily.

Grades everything last minute and extremely harshly. Talks about nonsense during class yet requires attendance. Has a major ego and is very mean to students. I feel like she's a deeply unhappy person that believes everyone else should be miserable as a result. I'd take an 8am over htis class any day.

analysis.name: Adjo Amekudzi
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Amekudzi-Kennedy was an excellent teacher. You can tell she cares both about civil and about students learning and growing in her class. Exams are graded pretty leniently and she is incredibly kind and open to meeting and talking about anything CEE. The project was fun, and isn't bad if you incrementally work on it through the semester.

Dr. Amekudzi-Kennedy is very passionate about this course but isn't the best at relating to students and student concerns.  The grading criteria is slightly strange and she expects you to do a lot for the class outside of lecture.  She is a great person and very nice but the class was just average and tedious at times.

Group project heavy; you work with the same group all semester. some exams, but easy if you keep up with class content. the final is the group project, which is sort of graded tough. pay attention to techniques taught in class, because this is what they are looking for

Dr. Kennedy really cares about her students. Long homeworks/tests that are graded pretty tough but the group project should help with your grade. She is so kind and responds immediately to your emails. Overall an interesting class that really teaches you a lot about sustainability and civil systems. Probably more work than it needed to be though

Personally, this is one of my favorite teachers here at Georgia Tech! I am very interested in Sustainable Urban Development and although the class is called Civil Engineering Systems, it is amazing how she focuses on sustainability analysis of systems as the basis of the class. Additionally, she is the most respected in her field! So much knowledge

analysis.name: Amy Bruckman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Online community was a pleasant surprise. Had a lot of fun working on the term paper. Lectures are interesting. Beware of the many and sometimes long readings. TAs were excellent as well. Generally an easy grader and very understanding about student concerns. A fun personality on top of all that. Definitely beating the reddit mod stereotype

Dr. Bruckman is one of the most engaged, passionate professors I've ever had. Every lecture kept me interested and was filled with stories that make the material memorable. She's funny, witty, and very kind. She gives clear expectations from the beginning. If you complete the readings and pay attention, you will do well. I highly recommend.

Dr. Bruckman's very caring towards students and her lectures are very engaging and interesting. At the start, there is quite a bit of reading + homework essays, but it gets way easier as the course progresses. Make sure you participate in Section and you'll be just fine. The 2 exams are detail-specific. Very easy course overall, would recommend.

In the first half, you have short papers due weekly. No final, but 2 midterm exams and a term paper due towards the end of the semester. There's a lot of reading assigned, but she basically reviews all of it in class the next day, so I don't read anything. Weekly discussion sections are long but interesting, depending on the people in your section.

Dr. Bruckman is the best professor I have had at Georgia Tech. As long as there is effort in the papers due each class, you will do fine. Dr. Bruckman is incredibly knowledgable, and she does a great job of conveying the material in a way that is easy to understand and engaging. This class is highly valuable and very applicable to the real world.

analysis.name: Amit Prasad
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took this course Spring 2022. I found the lectures to be extremely dry. Prepare yourself to participate in class discussions, which are highly philosophical. Your grade is almost entirely dependent on essays. It seemed to me that if he didn't agree with your stance on a topic, you would receive an unfavorable grade for the essay and vice versa.

The readings can be long at 15-25 pages on average but you will do well as long as you show up to class, participate, and complete the assignments. Discussions in class are engaging and Dr. Prasad is not heavy on lecturing. He cares a lot about students and can give a lot of guidance on the two essays (which were 50% of the class grade).

There was a lot of reading and the material was pretty dense. The class itself though was interesting and engaging and Dr. Prasad was very caring about the students. There are normally three papers and a few small assignments. It's expected you do the readings before class to participate but not required (i.e. no pop quizzes).

analysis.name: Arpit Kumar
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Kumar is a very caring & understanding (gives extension whenever you ask). He is an easy grader, & 50% of essay grade is self graded. In class we watched this one movie, so we did not have any books to read. There was never really any homework except for the projects. Projects were 5-10 pages (2x spaced) & you basically choice the topics.

Really liked the professor and the class was fine and pretty interesting. Just speak up in class for your participation points. He was very considerate and would extend deadlines. He claims you need the textbook, but I would say it's not worth investing in it as we only discussed it a little bit.

Professor Kumar was my ENGL1101 professor for the Fall 2025 semester. He is extremely generous and kind. His course revolves a lot around 5 key projects/essays. These are honestly not hard to do and he makes it so the class is not too much of a time commitment. Would definitely love to be in his class again

The class was overall pretty easy. The professor is nice, but sometimes the class would get really boring. By this I mean that he would talk for a while about basically the same thing. However, overall a nice prof and will extend due date if needed.

Hes a really kind proffesor he cares for his students and is really understanding would take again definetly. Just do the work come to class. He cares what he talks about and his class isn't boring he likes to have giant disccussions

analysis.name: Ariel Fried
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Overall, I would say Prof. Fried made lectures enjoyable and offered a lot of support for students even as a first-time professor at GT. I would pay close attention to the topic you want for ENGL1101 before choosing, but -- if you don't mind learning about the Victorians -- I would absolutely recommend taking Dr. Fried!!

Dr. Fried made English, a subject which I dreaded in high school, much more enjoyable. Empathized with students and focused on useful learning outcomes, rather than assigning endless amounts of readings. She is quite flexible with due dates, and gives plenty of chances for re-submissions on assignments.

She is an excellent professor willing to be flexible on deadlines, and she gives well-constructed feedback to make students stronger writers. Outside of class, Dr. Fried is also very accessible. I couldn't recommend her enough if you have the opportunity to be a part of the class.

Great professor, she actually cares that you understand the material and doesn't assign too much readings. Lectures could be a lot sometimes and the work can pile up fast if you aren't paying attention, not a free A but definitely achievable if you put in a bit of effort.

Dr. Fried is an awesome professor. She understands students are preoccupied with major specific classes and is flexible with deadlines as long as a student shows commitment in class and in other assignments.

analysis.name: Armistead Russell
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Overall structure of the class is super disorganized. His grading rubric wasn't clear the whole semester. Quiz almost every Tuesday and some Thursdays, pretty hard to study for them since all he says is "any previous work we've done is fair game." Practice exams are not helpful 85% of the time.
I did not enjoy this class. Lots of hard material, lectures are confusing. Prof does not explain concepts well. TA saved me. Thankfully, plenty of extra credit opportunities to get a better grade.

This is by far the hardest professor I have ever taken. Lectures consist of 50 slide powerpoints filled with words. Nothing is explained clearly. The lectures and the tests feel like completely separate courses. This is likely a weed-out class. This class tanked both my GPA and mental health. Made me question if I wanted to be in college.

Prof yaps a lot during lectures, lectures are quite disorganized and heavy with information that isn't explained thoroughly. Exams are very difficult and have questions that we have never seen examples of before. A redeeming factor is that he gives quite a bit of extra credit.

analysis.name: Arijit Raychowdhury
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He explains things really well and also shows a lot of care for students. Class was curved quite a lot and he would constantly let the class know where the cutoffs were after each test. Although all his material is posted online, still highly recommend both going to class and reading his online notes, as they supplement each other quite well.
Amazing teacher. He has taught some of the most difficult topics with such ease and coherence! I learnt so much in the class, yet never felt overburdened. He wants the students to succeed.
A good lecturer and teacher, Dr. Raychowdhury knows the material and makes sure you do as well. Homeworks often were very difficult but were relevant to the material.

Prof Raychowdhury is a great teacher and great at explaining the course material. He convered a lot of material but always took the time to explain the concepts slowly. He also found ways to make the whole course interesting throughout the semester.

This is a joke. The professor and the TA just don't give s about it. I get it. As the chair, you'll be busy with who know. But if you can't afford time that you have to constantly cancel lectures 30 minutes before the class and give only four homeworks, you should've handed it to another one. What is the purpose of edDiscussion when nobody answers?

analysis.name: Stephanie Arevecchia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I was excited for CS3600, but quickly grew frustrated. The prof has no clear curriculum, comes unprepared, and answers Qs with “I don't know.” She skips key slides, gives unclear homework, and fails to relate content to AI. So far, we've done 8 graph search algorithms—none AI-related. A class w/ much potential became one I care about the least.

Would definitely recommend her for 2110, MUCH easier than taking it in ATL. She makes the class very fair with assignments, quizzes, and TLs. Reads off the slides from ATL, but you can tell that she knows what she's talking about. Slight language barrier that makes understanding hard sometimes, but overall a very solid prof who I would recommend.

Prior review was lazy & biased, didn't make it through the entire class. Extremely fair teacher & decent lecturer for her first time teaching the course. Could tell she was very knowledgeable, but language barrier hurt a bit. HW heavy, but a very very fair course compared to taking in Atlanta. Would highly recommend and I enjoyed. Also had for 2110

analysis.name: Emily Alicea-Munoz
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 147 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Alicea is by far the best professor for Physics. For those who say her exams are hard and beyond what they believe was taught, you're wrong. As long as you understand the content well and its applications, no matter the question given, you'll be able to apply what you know. Not to mention the generous partial credit given. HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!!!

She is an outstanding professor. I took this class online and found it much easier than the in-person version. The recorded lectures explain the concepts very clearly, and the ample practice tests prepared me well for exams. As long as you pay attention to the recorded lectures and utilize the GPS and practice tests, this class is a breeze.

The lecturer does a great job at giving you ample amounts of practice material, relevant examples through labs and group-work problems over teams, and has access to many helpful TA's while being very responsive to emails and questions on Ed-Stem. Tests are hard, with self-studying being necessary to pass. Hard class, good teacher.
Best professor for physics 2. Took this course online and it was easy.

Dr. Alicea is by far the best Physics Prof at Tech. She takes complicated information and presents it in an easy-to-understand way with TONS of examples. Physics II is a challenging course, and the tests reflect that. However, the grade breakdown allows you to succeed even if you don't do very well on the three midterms and final.

analysis.name: Ari Glezer
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Fluids is one of the toughest classes at Tech. Dr. Glezer teaches fluids every fall, and he is good lecturer. He has a great understanding of fluid mechanics as it is the primary focus of his research. He can assume that students know more about fluids before taking this class. He can also be condescending about not getting concepts immediately.

Fluid Mechanics is a difficult class, but Dr. Glezer's lectures are helpful and include plenty of relevant examples. The 45 min exams are stressful, but not overly complex. Grading scheme is extremely friendly, allowing you to drop the two lowest test scores (can exempt final). Homework solutions are posted with the assignment. Would recommend.

Handwriting was actually atrocious, we spend most of each class asking him what things say. His tests have too short of a time limit just so he can spend 10 minutes lecturing after we finish the test, you could go into the test feeling good and walk out confused if you even know the subject, Better than some professors friends had so ig worth it

really fast lecturer, but lectures are well organized and lots of content covered every lecture. he has horrible handwriting though so be prepared for 5 minutes of every class dedicated to questions of what a word on the screen is. exams are difficult, but similar enough to hw. doing hw and studying lecture examples is key to the class

Dr. Glezer is one of the best professors I have had at Tech. Let me be clear: Fluids is HARD. Plain and simple. Dr. Glezer focuses his teaching on the concepts behind fluid mechanics, which makes his class difficult. But he is extremely clear in his lectures on what will be tested.

analysis.name: Robert Ashwill
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 17 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Let the students focus on their actual work, tone down the class a bit.

Obscene amount of information covered on tests & closed notes. Discussions in this class don't exist because lectures always fall behind schedule. Need to know all lecture and book content. Accuracy graded HW. Few grade padding points. Too time consuming as a non major class. Not worth making space in your schedule for this section of the class...

Rob teaches good lectures but his progress is often slow so that you need to read textbook sections that he hasn't covered but will be on the test to prepare for tests. He is willing to help and answer students' questions yet the tests, for me, are harder than I would expect for a intro-level class. You need to memorize a lot to get good grades.

This class is one that is very easy to succeed in so long as you keep up with the course material. A lot of the material that is covered on exams is talked about heavily during lectures, so even though attendance is not mandatory, it is a key factor to doing well in this class. Prof Ashwill is very understanding and I would take his class again.

Avoid this professor for an intro psych class. This class is doable, but I was always annoyed how much work and I had to put into this class compared to other teachers. If you want to make an A you must memorize the entire textbook and lecture powerpoints. Tests are mc, essay question, and fill in the blank whereas other classes are mc.

analysis.name: Ashutosh Dhekne
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I LOVE this professor. He is passionate about the field, and this is evident in his lectures. His lectures are also interesting and easy to follow. Supplement them with the networking textbook, and you should do ok on the tests and homework. Sometimes the homework/projects were a little vague, but they were never super strict with grading.

Ngl this class is bad after the course refresh; the TA team sucks (always grading assignments late, don't reply on Piazza). Prof speaks with a heavy indian accent & it's definitely difficult to fully understand. He is very passionate tho. No structure to this course whatsoever, no communication.
Dr. Dhekne is an amazing lecturer and cares about students' understanding of the topics.
Great lecturer who clearly enjoys teaching networking and isn't here to make your life painful
Make sure to take CS 3251 with him. One of the best lecturers from my time at GT. Cares deeply about learning instead of exams and grades and sharing his passion of networking

analysis.name: Joy Arulraj
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 24 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He is a knowledgeable & excellent professor in database systems, but his teaching style could improve. No lecture recordings and a presentation heavy approach without practical demonstrations made it difficult to fully grasp concepts tbh. Exams were lengthy & allowing more time would be very helpful. I had high expectations but sadly disappointed.

The core content for this class is very interesting and is taught well, but it is formatted very poorly. Half of your grade comes from two written tests which contain numerous questions on irrelevant C++ trivia

Lectures were a bit slow, but easy to follow from the slides alone. Great introduction to the finer points of C++. Programming assignments were excellent coding practice. Exams were quite challenging, with some niche questions on C++ syntax, but they were satisfyingly comprehensive and curved reasonably. Extremely understanding prof. No busywork.

Earned 95% without doing the extra credit project. Assignments taught me a lot about C++ and databases. Thought tests could be tricky due to potpourri style questions that could be on anything from lectures, but that was alleviated due to a generous curve. Participation was Point Solutions, but that was also curved. Overall, he's a nice professor

This class was great, Prof Joy gives a lot of real world applications and teaches all aspects of designing a complex database system. He is very kind and prioritize learning above grades or anything else. Lots of extra credit opportunities were given. I learnt a lot of C++ and systems fundamentals which were useful as I was new to it. Great course

analysis.name: Asif Khan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Great introduction to semiconductors and very in-depth coverage of MOSFETs. Video lectures are posted on his Youtube and sometimes go more in depth than he does during lecture. Homeworks are fair and pretty much exactly based off lecture slides. Super experienced guy with lots of industry knowledge that he sprinkles into lectures.

ECE3030 with Khan is awesome. Engaging class that will help you understand semiconductors and industry trends on a deeper level. Only complaint is grading takes a long time (over a month for midterm 1), but other than that I highly recommend this course.

Dr Khan is a great teacher! He does speak slowly, but I actually like that because it gives me time to internalize the information and take notes. He also digresses by speaking about related but non-class material in the real world, such as investors, or even what the yield of a chip is, and that's always interesting! Listen and you will learn!

He's a pretty funny guy. The homework is due weekly and there aren't late submissions allowed unless the TAs are feeling nice at the end of the year. The homeworks can be very difficult or super easy, no in-between. The Midterms and Finals aren't very difficult if you pay attention. All lectures are recorded and are on youtube.

Dr. Khan teaches this course at the exact level it needs to be at. He explains many of the topics very intuitively and very clearly, leaving little for the student to have to puzzle over themselves. The homeworks are straightforward and relatively short, and they are generally a grade booster. The class content is also interesting.

analysis.name: Ashley Bradford
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Bradford is a really good health policy professor! This class was not too difficult, but I learned so much! Highly suggest for anyone looking to take a public policy elective class. Each class does have pre-readings, but it isn't too bad, as you could still do well in the class without reading.
She is genuinely so good for US Health Policy. I learned so much and the exams are not too difficult.

Dr. Bradford is awesome! I was nervous to take a stats class but she is an amazing lecturer who helped explain things so well! She's also funny and pretty young, so she's very understanding! The problem sets could be tough, but she was receptive to feedback and offered many ways to boost grades. I would definitely recommend taking a class with her!

Dr. Bradford is an amazing professor and I definitely recommend taking her as she starts teaching new classes. The class is graded by 2 tests and 4 assignments, which are hard but if you attend lectures and pay attention they are easy to get through. She is very helpful, responds to emails very quickly and is overall a fun professor to talk to.

Dr. Bradford is awesome. Her lectures are packed with material, but she does a great job in making sure students understand what is being taught. There are 6 total grades, 4 of which are problem sets, which can be a bit tricky. Overall, Dr. Bradford is an amazing professor and I would recommend her to any student.

analysis.name: Ashok Goel
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I have very mixed feelings. I really like this professor, but CS7637 is the worst class I have taken yet at Georgia Tech. I learned more reading about the topics on Wikipedia than I did in lecture. This professor loves busy work too, so expect a bunch of pointless writing assignments. He just isn't a computer scientist, he's a cog psych guy.

A few problems I had with the class:
-Lectures are mandatory and long, and he always waits for 5 questions/comments from the class
-Assignments are writing heavy
-Class is more cog-sci focused than CS focused (one programming assignment was like 300 lines of if statements)
-part of your participation points are based off talking to AI TAs

Overbearing and uninspiring. Class is bloated with busy work and he throws a fit if you don't ask a question within 5 seconds of him asking if there are any questions. By taking this class, he will run cognitive science experiments on you as a student, which is something I definitely did not want to be a part of.

Course is well-structured and the professor supports his students. TA team is slightly inconsistent and aggressive in their approach to students (Head TA accused half the class of cheating in peer reviews). His accent makes it difficult to understand what he's saying at 1.4x speed. Overall, I liked the slow introduction to AI agents in this class.
Had him for intro to cognitive science.  Great teacher!  Very interesting subject too!  Reccomended for anyone who wants to learn how people think and learn.

analysis.name: Ashley Wheeler
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: (I ACTUALLY TOOK HER FOR 1554) Prof. Wheeler does not give full length lectures and expects you to know all content prior to attending the lecture. She will only do two or three examples that last a matter of twenty minutes. If you have any possibility to take Barone do it, unless you intend to learn from the TA's.

Cancelled class day of the exam 2x so we didn't get a review session. Lectures are hard to understand. Doesn't care about her students at all. Doesn't compensate for cancelled lectures with videos like other teachers, send her students to a different lecture WITHOUT even asking that professor causing students to be kicked out of that lecture

Very unorganized and the lectures are uninspired and unstructured. She does not go into depth on the important concepts and rather than clarifying them, she asks the students on their input (while most of us do not have familiarity). If you take her, you need to make extra effort to teach yourself or from the TAs (saved me). Take Barone if you can.

The midterms/quizzes for 1553 are the same for all professors, and attendance isn't mandatory. Wheeler can be difficult to relate to and hard to follow in class, so just watch Jankowski's lectures on the class page or read the textbook yourself- it's probably the only way you'll get an A in the class but isn't all that unmanageable if you enjoy it.

If you take her, you will often find yourself teaching all of the material to yourself, as she does not go in depth or teach it properly enough to do well on the exams. She does not exhibit expert knowledge on the topic and often leaves students more confused than when they entered the lecture. Linear can be difficult, but she makes it harder.

analysis.name: Sybrina Atwaters
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I thought this class would be an interesting class to take for my first semester here at Tech. I hated this class by the second week. Her tests are so confusing. Most of the questions on her tests are horribly worded. I feel like I haven't learned anything. It also feels like that if you don't believe what she does and agree with her, you're wrong.

The professor is so obviously biased towards socialism that she forced us to write our final exam essays from that perspective. She cited non-peer reviewed research as fact in her lectures, which barely made sense to begin with. She was extremely argumentative and was a poor facilitator of class discussion. Does not round up decimal grades at all.

If you're a Challenge student, beware. She acts superior, overexplains yes/no questions, and loves to use the “threes” like “I came, I saw, I conquered” plus her favorite phrase, “By design.” Midterm questions are confusing, so the study guide is useless. Her TAs don't give feedback around her. One of the worst classes I've had.

Major superiority complex! She grades her students based off of whether or not they agree with her on everything. She tries to push her beliefs on everyone. Whatever you do, do not disagree with her, tell her she's wrong, or speak your mind. All her class is, is an hour and a half long rant of her beliefs and how she's above everyone else.

She thinks that she is some sort of prophet and will berate you if you do not exactly agree with what she does. Her exams are poorly worded and have objective answers with zero curve (nobody got an A) and she marks you absent even if you are in class if you don't do EXACTLY what she says as soon as she says it. Do NOT take this class.

analysis.name: Christina Athanasouli
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Incredibly CARING and KNOWLEDGEABLE professor who has a knack for recontextualizing difficult mathematical concepts into intuitive lessons. She took the time to know all of the students in her lecture hall by name and regularly checked in with her students to make sure they were prepared. Easy to talk to!

Math 1552 was hard, but with Christina, she made it easier. She really cares about her students, she learned every single person's name in the big lecture class and made sure to check in with them to see how the class was going. The class itself is hard, and she tends to go very fast, but I would definitely recommend and would take again with her.

Awesome professor that truly cares for each student. Was always early in class to talk to individual students, learn names, and chat. SUPER accessible outside of class. Great lectures with sufficient practice and test-application based problems. Tests are usually on the tougher side (especially multiple choice), but the optional final helps a lot.

Professor Anathasouli is amazing! Although Math 1552 is hard as a Tech class, she did an amazing job. She is always super prepared when she comes to class with slides, and she posts practice problems too. She genuinely wants her students to succeed and learned everyone's names and met them outside of class/office hours if they needed help.

She goes out of her way to remember every students' names and puts lots of effort into her lectures. I never attended since it was my 8am, but I used the online notes. I would still recommend attending. There are many ways to improve your grade and maintain an A, lots of extra study material and opportunities provided.

analysis.name: Athulya Ram
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: No homework or textbook assigned. Lectures were absolutely phenomenal. Studios were required instead of HW by giving participation points (20% of grade). Tests were very reasonable and weekly quizzes were similar to material covered in studio. Professor was extremely accessible outside of class.

probably the best professor I've had at Tech so far. She explained the concepts very well and made integral calc so easy to understand. make sure to attend studio though to get a lot of practice problems to prep for tests and quizzes
Overall she was a good professor and very caring, her pacing during class was just off sometimes but she posts her notes on canvas so not a huge issue.

analysis.name: Athanasios Mantalaris
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He is a very sweet man who cares a lot about the students, but is not the best teacher. He would emphasize main points over and over instead of working through problems. Only reason I really understood the class was because of the amazing TAs. Still got an A because the TAs graded and they were lenient because they would watch him not teach us.

BMED 2210 is a boring and easy class. Learn it by yourself. Dr. Mantaralis isn't helpful and the TAs were sometimes clueless. However, this is not a stressful class. All materials are straightforward. You don't need to rely on professors and TAs a lot.
You need to read the book to really grasp concepts and examples. He is funny and very enthusiastic but does not answer questions well. This class is just poorly run in general.

analysis.name: Hassan Attarchi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I found Attarchi's lectures very difficult to follow. In retrospect, I probably would have done better skipping the class, teaching myself, and showing up to weekly quizzes. I didn't have much exposure to calculus before this class and his lectures really didn't help me grasp concepts I didn't know. He was, however, very caring and willing to help.

Very caring teacher. Wants to see you succeed, but the tests are just so hard. Even as someone who took AP Calculus in high school, the questions asked are very difficult and unlike the questions we see in our homework. Homework is due every Thursday at midnight. Actually do the homework even if it's only a tiny percentage of your avg. It'll help.

Let's just start with this: there are homeworks due every Thursday at midnight. There are also weekly quizzed averaging over just a few sections of the book that you will take in either the first or last 10-15 minutes of class. NOW HERE IS THE STRUGGLE: you do well on the quizzes and the test questions look crazy, never before seen. TOTAL BS CLASS

I'll be honest, I rarely paid attention in lecture and never went to office hours, but the few times I did listen to him it really paid off. There is homework due every week but it's honestly not too difficult. The online transition was pretty rough as expected for a math class, but he moved so many due dates and gave tons of extensions. Great guy!

He was really accesible outside of class and willing to help, but the problem is I don't think he remembers what it is like to not know the subject, and so he explains it as if we already know what's going on. the accent makes things a little difficult to understand too. He is caring when it comes to personal problems and will move a quiz if needed

analysis.name: Austin Christian
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Amazing and incredibly funny professor. He was always super helpful during office hours. 3 exams, HW, quizzes, and a final. Allowed for makeup exams. Gave practice exams that were very similar to the tests. Very good professor to take multi with.

LOVE HIM!! take him if you can, he is such a good professor. he knows what hes talking about, and makes the lectures make sense. he encourages office hours like no other, and when i went he was so kind and helped. dry sense of humor also. his practice exams help a bunch. pls go to his class he deserves it. slay austin!!

Took him for 4107. Has to be the best math professor I've taken at tech. I would take him over any professor. Knows his stuff like the back of his hand and legitimately cares that you understand the material. Could not recommend this guy more.
I took him a year ago and to this day say he was the best math professor ive had at GT. Take him if you can. He's super accessible at office hours too. Can't say enough good things about him.

Professor Christian was one of the best math professors I have had! His lectures were very engaging and he made a point to learn the names of everyone who went to office hours. He would also give a study guide before each exam that would greatly help with the exam's content. Midterms were pretty easy compared to other teachers. He was worth it!

analysis.name: Philip Auslander

review_highlights.comment: This was an acting class. As an aspiring actor, I NEVER walked out of a single class feeling good about myself as an actor or even person. He was very rude, curt, and un-constructive in his comments/grading. Does not care and will not help u achieve your goals (even if they are class-related). Very subjective grader. Different opinion  lower grade
He is the worst teacher ever.  He is a very hard, unreasonable, grader.  His class is very boring.  He is a very dirty, nasty person who's office and body is filthy.  DO NOT TAKE HIM!!!!!

Lectures are hard to pay attention to, there are no materials to study for the tests that actually reflect what the test will be like, and the only time I ever learned content was in recitation and by struggling on the HW. Take anyone else.

I took this in my first semester here at tech. It was very difficult at first, but there are lots of resources like past exams and your TA to help you. Prof. Juang is a very chill dude and he's pretty caring if you just reach out to him with your problems. I would say the hardest part of this class (besides attendance) is doing well on HW.
You should just ask ChatGPT to explain the content to you during lectures, since attendance is mandatory, and this guy acts smug while proceeding to say nothing of value.

Not very good at explaining anything, relates himself a lot, and doesnt seem to actually know whats going on. The second professor that taught the other section of the class did a much better job and seemed to be the only one that actually knew what was happening.

analysis.name: Claire Berger
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Wonderful lady, decent lecturer. She truly cares about you as a person, not just as a student (helped me land a research position). Exams get tougher as the semester goes on and homework can be hit or miss. Attendance is technically required (in-class clicker questions). Final project instead of exam, pretty much a guaranteed A on that.

Without having any prior physics experience, this class was very difficult for me and Professor Berger's lectures were only somewhat helpful. For the first half I found it manageable, but toward the end I found it easier to watch videos online than attempt to understand her explanations. That being said, she cared about the students deeply

She wasn't the best lecturer, but she cared about each student. I recommend reading the textbook because a lot of her lectures are just simplified explanations of the textbook. If you want a better explanation of what she says in class, read the textbook. She's also a nice grader and gives good explanations on your assessments, so that's a plus.

Berger's personality and vibe is great but the lectures were generally unhelpful. She went over concepts pretty quickly but the examples were sort of helpful. Labs were generally pretty good at helping you understand material. Tutoring will be your best friend. The test are absolute hell. If your taking this class, try to get Munoz.

Professor wrote on the small board at the front of the class for a lecture of over three hundred students. Instead of explaining the material she chooses to derive equations while running her class like a reverse classroom. While the only saving grace is the fact that her courses are Modern physics. Best suggestion would be listening to Munoz.

analysis.name: Mohammad Najjartabar Bisheh
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: HW easy and only 6. Exams were not, and the exam reviews were very different than the exams despite the professor insisting that they'll be similar (at least you can have 2 cheat sheets). Good extra credit (5 points). This was his first semester, so there was disorganization, especially with the dates of when things were due and exam dates.

Pretty solid professor and class overall. The grading is pretty generous considering we have a pretty easy final project and can get up to 5% added to our final grade with extra credit. You get this ec by being in class though so attendance is required. All in all he's pretty nice and helpful and the class isn't too difficult.

One of the better stats professors out there. He has a very generous grading policy, gifting you up to 15% free if you just show up to lecture. Tests were a bit difficult but doable if you studied. Final project can be a lot of work. However, he does random attendance checks and you need to be in class.

First sem teaching but did his best. HWs are easy, but nothing is representative of exams. Cheat sheets allowed but even then exams are difficult. 5 entire points of EC from random attendance quizzes. One group project, last exam during regular class time on the week on finals. Nice and respectful, just a wonky class structure.

analysis.name: Vicki Birchfield
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: For INTA 3050- very nice professor and VERY easy class but her lectures are so disorganized. she tends to ramble for the entire class with no real point. Hated going to class, but worth it for the A!

Took the course in Fall 2021. Vicki has a notorious reputation for going onto tangents but she is an incredibly caring person and will do everything she can (both inside and outside class) to get to know you and help.
She was the program lead for FYFA and while she loved to go on about tangents, she is one of the nicest people I've ever met.

I've had Birchfield for another class before. She can definitely be scattered and hard to follow sometimes, but overall, she's a very good professor. While she and I may not always have same or similar opinions, she's not the sort of professor to hold it against you or effect your grade. I'm looking forward to taking a third class with her.

She does not directly use the book she says is "required" for class, but requires students to read several pages of it for each class module. Her field trips are not always well planned. Her slides are clumsy and filled with text, and scheduling of assignments is done verbally only.
She led a study abroad I participated in during Summer 2014. She was clear, concise, and was clearly vested in making sure we all learned from the trip. One of the best professors I've had at Tech.

analysis.name: Laura Bier
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining

review_highlights.comment: 4 textbooks barely used.dont buy. u can get by by gogling the readings. And unless you have to turn in a paper, dont bother doing the readings. Too much assigned and a complete waste of time. Ask her for her expectation on midterm papers because she is alot stricter when grading those. Class borng. she needs to learn 2 teach rather than readng ppt

Her lectures tend to be kind of boring, but group discussions are engaging if you're caught up with all the readings. Assignments are extremely easy and tests consist of memorizing terms and writing an essay, which she grades fairly. I wouldn't recommend buying all the books, since you can get by without reading them.

She is a nice professor. She gives out everything that is going to be on the midterm and final, so study that a lot. I thought she was going to grade easily because she is nice but she grades essays very strictly. I wish this class was more of a discussion, but instead she lectured a lot. Don't turn anything in late.

For the most part you will pass if you read and understand the textbook, which the tests are directly based on. Most classtime is devoted to lectures which ho more in-depth. The teacher is very enthusiastic about the topics she teaches.

She's super passionate about what she's teaching. Lectures can be long, but interesting. She took weeks to grade things, which was rough. Just pay attention in class and at least skim the readings and you'll get an A.

analysis.name: Mario Bianchini
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I enrolled in this course as an elective but was pleasantly surprised by how engaged I became in its content, as the professor does a great job in conveying his enthusiasm. With few graded assignments, as long as you put in the expected effort, this is an easy course to succeed in. 100% would take again.

Favorite course of the semester! Classes were discussion based. The readings were extremely interesting, and our class got to vote on topics to cover for the last few weeks. Tests were based on ability to apply concepts from class, and were very similar to the short weekly responses. Professor was very kind and respectful of everyone's opinions.

Very open-minded and respectful of everyone's opinions in this discussion-based class. There is a lot of reading and writing involved, and while the material is interesting, I wish the class was more engaging. Positive attitude and willingness to listen to feedback.

analysis.name: Steven Biegalski
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I'll be honest- I have no interest in Nuclear Engineering, and just had to take this class to graduate. However, Professor Biegalski was by far one of the best professors I had at tech. He teaches very clearly. His tests are extremely fair. He really cares about the well being of his students. I really wish I could have had him for more classes.

I encourage you to get to know Dr. Biegalski both inside ad outside  of class.  Assuming you like him, see if you can get involved in his research.  He send another girl from my class for a professional conference in Hawaii this past semester for her to present he research,  that would be a good GT experience,

Also ask him about fly fishing.

I had Dr. Biegalski for NRE 3112, and on multiple occasions he made it clear that he really does care about his students. Dr. Biegalski also does a good job lecturing and answering questions, as well as just being a really chill and affable professor. My only complaint is that he oftentimes is too nice and students would heavily abuse that.

I took his class to graduate during Spring 2020. He is definitely in my top 5 favorite professors at Tech. He teaches the material extremely well, is interested in getting to know all of his students, and I had a ton of fun learning about nuclear reactions, reaction design, and nuclear energy. I wish he taught more classes.
Very engaging professor and made me even more interested in nuclear engineering.

analysis.name: Bill Todd
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors that I have ever had. Class is a mixture of case discussions and guest speakers. Grades are based on one test, three short essays, class participation. Prof. Todd has a wealth of industry knowledge and does a great job helping students understand healthcare. He's very lenient grader. Show up and try; you will make an A.
This was a great class with a bunch of guest lectures from people in the health care industry. I really enjoyed this class

Professor Todd really cares about his students.  I would suggest taking this class even if you are not interested in healthcare.  Straight up grades, two essay tests, case assignments, and class participation.  Professor really wants students to succeed. LOTS of guest speakers

Class was pretty easy. Just show up to class. Most of what you see on the test was said in class, so attendance is key. He's also a pretty cool guy. His stories are interesting. He has a lot of connections so he's someone you would want to know!

Such an interesting course. If you have any interest in healthcare, take it. Professor Todd is the best professor! He has a discussion based class about half of the time and excellent guest speaker the other half of the time. He is genuinely interested in your success as a student. I wish I could take this class every semester!

Thermo is concept heavy, but Dr. Bhamla's biggest strength is explaining concepts. However, he doesn't have time in class to work out many numerical problems. 2130 deserves to be 3 credit hrs. Recitation/TA office hrs are key for understanding those. He expects you to be a good critical thinker. His homeworks are tough, but his exams are fair.

I get the vibe that he doesn't actually know much thermo conceptually. He's not bad at teaching per se, though he doesn't give much explanation. Terrible at answering questions, but he does try. Doesn't understand much Thermo and classes are a mess.

analysis.name: Nathan Blackburn

Genuinely made Orgo a breeze, you can tell he loves it and knows a lot. Flipped classroom, but the lectures really help you lock down concepts because practice is built in. He wants you to succeed and will give CIOS bonus and extra credit opportunities. Just such a nice guy overall.
He has a great way of making difficult concepts easy to understand and is an incredible lecturer.

analysis.name: Justin Blann

Extra credit opportunities were given.

His grading scheme was forgiving, so long as you put forth the effort needed. My only regret is not having more time to dedicate to his class.

Such a fun class and professor! Unique approach of teaching valuable acct content in an enjoyable and low-stress format. Assignments include many small group projects, a few pop quizzes, and the final was a slightly larger group project. One of my fav classes I have taken at GT, so ABSOLUTELY take it if you need an extra MGT/accounting elective!

Professor Blann is super nice and accommodating!! His lectures are alright, but the class is pretty straightforward. I would only say that I felt like the online section got much better grades than the in-person section (I was in-person section). Attendance is basically mandatory since he has mini quizzes for attendance almost every class

Professor Blann is a great professor! Although the class is a little boring and lectures are mostly just him reading slides, Professor Blann provided several extra credit opportunities, homework's that really helped for the test, and a flash card on each test. He also is very understanding and will help you if needed. Overall, good class!

analysis.name: John Blazeck

review_highlights.comment: I had him for chbe 2140 thermodynamics. He's a very nice and knowledgeable guy. Blazeck is tough, but a great lecturer and clearly a nice guy. No curve or crib sheet is absolutely brutal, but his exams are fair. His homework is very long.

Actually ended up really liking chbe 2100 with Blazeck. Pretty sure it was his first time teaching, but lectures were well organized and straight forward. He made it pretty clear what you need to do to succeed. Grades pretty easy relative to other teachers for 2100 and tests weren't too crazy. Would definitely recommend. Very understanding as well.

analysis.name: Ryan Blunck
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Mythical pull of a professor. Great professor. Lectures are engaging and clear. He clearly cares about his students. Goes question by question when explaining what is going to be on the test. You will not regret taking his class.

He's the best!! He clearly cares about his students and tries his best to make accounting fun. BEST PROFESSOR AT SCHELLER! If you're considering taking Accounting 2101 with anyone other than Professor Blunck, DON'T. I can't stress enough how amazing he is. He set up his class in a manner that makes it easy for all his students to succeed. Accounting is a difficult subject, but Blunck made it much more digestible.

Blunck is the most fair professor ever! He prepares you super well for each test and quiz and basically gives you the concepts you need to know for every question. If you pay attention in class, everything else is easy! 
 
Side note: This class is great to prep for interview technicals. Highly highly recommend!

analysis.name: Greg Blekherman

review_highlights.comment: His voice is that of Gru from Despicable Me. He is clear.

His class was the hardest in my degree, but I always felt confident because I knew he was always there for us. Lectures were very good, and homework did a very good job preparing for the exams. He was also very helpful in office hours. He did have both a final project and exam, which always annoys me, but other than that, I highly recommend.

Dr. Blekherman is great. He is funny, insanely intelligent, and a great lecturer. His domain of knowledge stretches far beyond the course I took with him, and it shows. Disclaimer: I took this class dual enrollment 
I see so many people saying he was a very tough professor and that the practices were nothing like the exam. Practice exams don't have to look like the exam: they are designed to test you over the content on the exam, which they did. He was also generous with partial credit. The class had good rigor.

Blekherman is truly a funny guy. I appreciated how he injected humor into math, which is rare in my experience. The class itself is hard but Blekherman's lectures are fairly engaging. As far as 1553 goes, he is a fairly standard grader and the work is mostly the same across all professors.

Where do I even start with ol' Blue. Blumenthal is one of the better lecturers and while he may move fast, he covers everything necessary to ace the tests. Just hope he doesn't eat Twisted Taco before class and you will be alright.
Blumenthal's lectures are good, but I couldn't enjoy them because the course was super easy. A good load of homework, but not too bad.

analysis.name: Jacob Blevins

Jacob Blevins is a professor that actually cares about the quality of his communication skills.

What more can be said about the great Jacob Blevins that hasn't already been said. Blevins is hands down the best instructor for 2110. I took the 6:30 pm to 9:15 pm section but it was worth taking considering how much this man respected our hard work in the class. 2110 is hell, but he will make it WAYYY easier than the other instructors for 2110.

analysis.name: Bolei Deng

a great lecturer, learned a lot in class and its very clear he cares abt the students. projects and exams all have extra credit portions, everything is graded reasonably. hw is a bit difficult but he is very helpful during office hours and it is reasonable to what we are learning in class. great guy would definitely take him again.

one of fav profs at gt, great guy, hard class but explained clearly. very fair prof. 30% 10 hw 1drop, 1exam 15%, 3project 10% each but 1st is free, 2&3 use matlab. 25% final not cumulative. bonus on tests. has zoom link for class and records. only criticism: he talks quiet. you will actually learn dynanmics here unlike patil where its a free A lol
