Lectures can sometimes get boring but he makes the content easy to learn homework almost every week but its not hard and helped me learn the majority of the content, plenty of extra credit. Solid professor who cares about economics, practice tests are super similar to actual tests

Easy course. Grading relies on exams heavily but they're easy as long as you do the practice exams and homeworks on time. Generous EC opportunities. Required $70ish online textbook and homework system. Great lectures and slideshows, though exams are easy enough that it won't matter even if you skip a couple of lectures.

I thought I could get away with skipping the lectures bit it was almost 9% of my grade - I would've gotten an A otherwise. The class is not hard, the homework assignments can be tedious but there is extra credit. The tests are just like the practice ones he gives and he reuses the same format and types of questions.

He is an amazing lecturer who is also very understanding and clearly just wants you to feel good about the topic. His exams are definitely more challenging than other ECON 2106 exams because he tests on applications not just concepts, but I think you get a far better learning experience.

analysis.name: Bryce Truitt
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Soft, squishy professor under a cool, detached exterior. Great at teaching; explaining concepts in clear, concise manner. Reasonably understanding about late assignments and exceptional circumstances. 

If you show a genuine dedication to your learning, he will match you.

Make sure to show up to class. Class is just walking through the homework assignments step by step. I learned a lot. The assignments are not something to procrastinate. He is intimidating/ AI-like at first, but he's pretty chill and is very helpful and understanding.

He's an adept teacher, but he cannot “make” you into anything that you aren't. If you're willing to put in the effort, he will help you to build whatever it is, design, career, project. 
There is definitely a human being underneath it all, but don't depend on it. 
I learned a lot with him. 
Pro tip: values novelty more than anything else.

Bryce is intimidating at first, but he is a genuinely caring teacher. Architecture is VERY difficult & his teaching style (moves very fast/leaves no room to catch up) emphasizes that. But, if you put in the time, GO TO OFFICE HOURS & ask him questions, you'll be fine. There's only 10 assignments that make up your whole grade so lock in right away!

Great professor, don't be fooled by his tough, robotic exterior, he's a true sweetheart, cares a lot about his students. If you're willing to put in the work he'll work with you and make you incredibly successful. Difficult to understand his vocab at first, but you become accustomed to it and truly learn a lot.

analysis.name: Bo Zhu
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Bo Zhu is a wonderful professor. He's accommodating towards students and a great lecturer. He's passionate about computer graphics, and he's very kind and helpful. The homeworks are fair. Start early. The mesh subdivision homework is the hardest. For the tests, study the test review. I highly recommend him as a professor.

Prof. Zhu is a great lecturer who does a really good job of breaking down difficult concepts. He's clearly passionate about what he teaches, which makes lectures enjoyable, and he also offers Zoom options and recordings. The class is well structured with eight projects, a final project, and two online, open-note tests. I recommend taking his class.

This class has 8 super easy hws, 2 medium-difficult quizzes (depending on whether you studied hard or not), and a final project. I expected this class to be difficult or take a lot of my time, but it was honestly so chill. The instructions for the hws are very straight-forward and clear, and I never got stuck at all. Bho Zhu loves what he teaches.

Dr. Zhu is a goated professor. There are 8 straightforward programming assignments, 2 open-note take-home online quizzes, and the class overall is great. He's super knowledgeable and clearly knows his stuff, if you can take him for graphics, 100% do it

Took undergrad AI graphics (4803) but it was identical to 8803. Probably one of the more interesting and fun classes I've taken at tech. Projects are very approachable and the course is designed really well, but brush up on pytorch and NNs before taking. GOAT Zhu and TAs are very helpful on Ed. Hope this class becomes a permanent media/intel option

analysis.name: Brian German
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very nice professor. Lectures were pretty boring, but slides were really good to study off of separately. HWs were long but not too hard, we also only did 3. Course is split into aeronautics and aerospace halves. The exams and HWs for the aerospace half are much easier. Exam grading was kind of harsh, also grading for HW and exams took forever.

Prof. German is a really nice guy, and his lectures are super understandable. That said, he can drone during lectures which makes them a bit boring as he goes through slide decks. Homework was infrequent which made preparing for tests and quizzes difficult (2 test + 2 quiz = 80% of the course grade). Would recommend over other 3330 profs for sure.

German is a great professor for vpro. His lectures felt very easy to follow and understand. Probably the most well spoken professor I've ever had. HWs closely model what the tests/quizzes look like so it's easy to prepare for those. The class does focus more on aeronautics than spacecraft, but overall worth taking regardless of which you prefer.

German is legit my FAVORITE professor at this school. He is absolutely the nicest person you will ever meet, and he lectures like he's babying the class, NOT in a demeaning way but in a charming way. The homeworks are very straightforward and tests are IDENTICAL to homeworks (literally just apply eqns!). Low stress but you'll still learn a ton!

It is clear that German is vey passionate and excited to be teaching vpro. He tends to drag out lectures but is very clear and enjoys expanding on things not covered by the slides. Exams are very fair but homework often involves a scavenger hunt. He is super nice, caring, and will answer any/all questions. He is such a girl dad and girl boss

analysis.name: Brian Woodall
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took this Spring 2024, was a really fun class very interesting. Class was made up of mostly discussion posts/research project, with one multiple choice test that's a bit tricky (basically pure memorization) but totally doable. Professor is really understanding and willing to help if you reach out to him as well.

Such a sweet professor! Several of my classmates in his INTA 3203 (Comparative Politics) class all agreed that it was the easiest international affairs classes that they had ever taken. If you take the notes and study a little bit before each quiz, then you should be able to get an A. There were two projects which were very clear & straightforward.

This guy's the goat. Such an easy class - if you do the work you should not only pass, but get an A as well. His lectures aren't the most engaging but he always ends well before class is over. The whole last month is a project and we didn't actually meet once. We don't really go over the readings on the syllabus in class.

I always enjoy Dr. Woodall's classes immensely. He's an extremely kind and genuine professor and gives interesting lectures that are actually engaging. The structure of his projects is straightforward and it's easy to get an A as long as you put a little effort into the class. He's hands down the best professor I've had.

Really easy class. I took this to fulfill my social science credit and even without previous knowledge it wasn't that bad. Almost because there was very little homework, one test the entire year (20 question multiple choice), and the entire last month is a group project

analysis.name: Andre Brock
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Brock is awesome! He cares deeply about his field and makes it clear to his students. 3404 is a low maintenance course, so much of your time in the class is based around in-class discussions and discussions on Perusall and Piazza. The big turnoff is that he can be vague with your grades. Otherwise, if you need a humanities class, pick Dr Brock!

Dr. Brock is by far one of my favorite teachers ever; he was very personable and knowledgeable, and I appreciated everything he put into his class. He was not too difficult, but I appreciated how he held us to a certain standard of participation and work. He created an environment in class for me to want to contribute a lot.

Dr. Brock's class is very accommodating to students and the course material for Science, Tech, and Ideology was very thought-provoking. However, the class organization can be stressful for students and he is not transparent about grading. Despite that, take his classes if possible--such an interesting and caring professor!
Brock is awesome. He actually cares about the material, assigns interesting readings, and engages with the class in a respectful and fun way. Love this dude.

Dr. Brock is a very passionate teacher, but if you do not share similar... political ideas, he's quite inciting. Other than that, mostly interesting discussion. Graded on comments left on the twice a week (heavy) reading, formal comments on student write-up, and your own formal write-up on one of the readings.

analysis.name: Dylan Brewer
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 32 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Made sure that every lecture was engaging and provided examples that connected concepts to daily life. Lots of extra credit, including for attendance, but tests counted for a large amount of your grade. As someone who had never taken econ, I found the textbook useful because some small test concepts were not explicitly mentioned in lecture.

Great guy, great professor. Brewer is a very relatable and caring professor while also being interesting and knowledgeable in Environmental Economics. Class was engaging. Had reasonably difficult homeworks and readings of economics papers. Very understanding if you ever needed a due date moved. Actually cared about his students. Take home tests.

Dr. Brewer is an awesome prof. I took him for Environmental Econ and moderately enjoyed the class. With lectures being 75 minutes long, I felt it got boring at times, and my attention waned as the class went on. The class is interesting enough, I like Dr. Brewer's lecture style. He's a funny guy and you can tell he has a heart. Take his class!
One of the greatest profs in the econ department. Absolutely loved him, highly recommend. Took him for ECON 2106, Fall 2025. Class was rigorous, but he was excellent.
super chill and gave us extra credit just for showing up. the content itself was sometimes hard to follow but you can tell he really tries to make his lectures entertaining

analysis.name: Robert Burgess
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I took this for T&M so my experience was different, but I'd be remiss if I didn't mention how good of a lecturer he is. It's so rare for me to actually feel refreshed after lecture, but Bob knows how to talk to an audience and keep 'em engaged. If you're taking this class w/him for T&M, don't be afraid. Bob doesn't bite.

Extremely helpful and entertaining.  Easily the best professor I had in my time at Tech.  I was amazed that he was an associate professor, and knew more and could teach more than the tenured professors.  Highly recommmended.

GREAT professor. Tests are open book and easy if you attend class and copy down exactly any notes he writes down. Lecture isn't mandatory but important to attend because examples he works are almost identical to the tests.
Whatever class he teaches, take it. You will learn a lot and enjoy it more than any other class through college.

One of the best professors I've had at Tech. It won't be an easy class, but he keeps it interesting/amusing and is very helpful. You can easily get a B, just not the easiest class to get an A. Not really the point, he's the kind of professor you want to take for the teaching, not the grade.

analysis.name: Whitney Buser
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: An extremely interesting class that was taught incredibly well. Every lecture felt like it gave new information and the papers were extremely interesting. Just be sure to keep up with the weekly readings as some of the higher level contents are on the exams. Group project is also pretty interesting and isn't too much work.

Dr. Buser's lectures were solid but our final grade was the average of midterm 1, midterm 2, and the final, which I thought was very harsh. This course is math heavy compared to most other econ courses. I wish there had been more example problems or practice exams but the tests were pretty fair so long as you reviewed the lecture notes/powerpoints.
Took her course in behavioral economics. Very direct and teaches you what you need to know. Course expectations were clear and reasonable. Learned a lot. Lectures were also fun and engaging.

I had Prof. Buser teach ECON2105 for iGniTe, but that class wasn't available to rate for some reason. Good course that covered the basics of macroeconomics. She made the lectures fun and interesting, and the grading was very straightforward.

Very test heavy but easy as long as you review the lecture notes. I would recommend going to class because she wrote on the whiteboards primarily. Truly a great teacher, still consult her for advice today

analysis.name: Susan Burns
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
This was one the best classes I have ever had. I did not expect to be interested in soil, but it turned out to be really interesting. There is alot of work, though. Six homeworks, five labs, and three tests, plus a final project. 

She did not curve individual test grades, but curved final grades at the end of the semester.
During lecture she just reads off 100+ slide decks. The homeworks and labs are alot. The tests were pretty difficult and she doesn't curve until the end so you have no idea what your standing is.

GT needs more professors like Prof. Burns. She is tough but very straightforward in lecture and fair in grading. It is clear that her primary goal is to make sure we learn the material, and she helps in any way she can. Engineering economy is tough but SO useful and her lectures make it clear, so don't skip class. Thank you, Prof. Burns!

Professor Burns is definitely one of the best profs I've had at Tech so far. She's very knowledgeable, breaks concepts down well, tries her best to make lectures engaging, is invested in her students, and is somewhat harsh but fair in grading (but she also curves). If you have her for 3000 expect a lot of writing

analysis.name: Andrew Buskell
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: LOVED Dr. Buskell---always led super interesting discussions and is super funny, caring, and intellectual. The readings could get lengthy but the very flexible in-class discussions make up for it. There are no exams, simply essays and presentations which are very doable, but just take a lot of time and thought. It is very easy to do well though!

Dr. Buskell is an absolute gem. He's caring, passionate about teaching, clear on expectations, and just a great guy to be around. Reading assignments in Perusall and discussions in class, but they're never overly-lengthy. It's a laid back environment where you feel encouraged and workload is balanced perfectly. Would take ANY class with him again.

Weekly accessible + interesting Perusall readings; centered on class discussion; Prof is really approachable and genuinely cares about his students and the material; excellent and timely feedback on papers and projects that makes it easy to plan ahead and implement change for later iterations; my favorite class of the semester!!

analysis.name: George Burdell
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: What an amazing professor. He is the GOAT when it comes to this class. He is very knowledgable and seems to know everything. Not very accessible outside of class though, don't really ever see him. But he is great and would def take again.
Mr. Burdell is AMAZING. He can be hard to find, but he's also everywhere. Being that he graduated with every major and accomplished much more, his stories are very inspirational.
He's hard to find, but he's the best. He's a multi-major professor. If you are undecided take one of his classes and ask him for advice. He will be the light that will show you the way.
Professor Burdell is, hands down, the best professor at Tech. In fact, he was a CS major before it was cool! I hear he's also the man in the Buzz costume... GO JACKETS!!!
I would take him again anytime. I took him after hearing about him from some friends.

analysis.name: Burak Hatinoglu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Had a deep understanding of the course, and if you didn't understand something during the lecture you could always go up to him after to ask questions. As long as you put in the work and show up to class then you shouldn't have a problem. He is also extremely accessible outside of class and will really try his best to answer questions.

He has a deep understanding the material and is proficient at answering questions during lectures. Most people (including myself) have to watch videos from Jankowski, another GT 1553 professor, to supplement lectures. However, if you can keep up with everything he reads off, then you will probably be fine with just the lectures and studio.

He is not that bad, although you might get bored of his lectures, you can still find what was taught in class on the classroom canvas and the studios help reinforce what he taught. Obviously, it helps to come to class especially because even if you zone out of class, as long as you approach him after class, he will explain it again.
Thought he was going to be very bad but after a couple of weeks I got used to his teaching style and he can be funny sometimes. Also very kind and accessible outside of class.
The professor read off the slides for most of the lectures, I didn't lead anything from his class.

analysis.name: Justin Burkett
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Took Game Theory II with him the first semester it was offered. Lectures were pretty dry but taught clearly and explained the material well. Homeworks aren't graded so three tests make up most of your grade although there is a decent curve. Grades generously but the class isn't super easy and you still need to study for all the exams.

I had him twice for two separate courses; lectures can get kinda dull; weekly homework, midterm and final. Course material is kinda difficult to grasp, but he grades fairly lax; he extended deadlines a few times so he understands students' workloads; problem is sometimes book and lecture don't match and homework is from book, but again, lax grader.

I really enjoyed Dr. Burkett's game theory class. He is very thoughtful and considerate and purposeful about everything he says. Very knowledgeable and good at answering students' questions. There are about 8 problem sets of homework, two midterms, and a final. The concepts can be a little hard to grasp, but an A is still possible.
Good professor overall, though the class itself was a little boring. We spent a *lot* of time defining terms to use, and that could get complex. Weekly homeworks but not too difficult or too long.

analysis.name: Charles Byrd
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Byrd is a really great lecturer who tries to keep the material interesting and accessible, and IMO succeeds. He clearly cares about the material and his students; he also posts amazing lecture notes in addition to his slides. 4646 content is quite straightforward, esp. if you've taken 3600, and his tests are very fair.

I really enjoyed going to his lectures. Professor Byrd is really helpful and good at clearly explaining concepts that can be hard to understand, and is always so kind to people who have questions. His tests are also really practical and doable if you go to lecture and read his notes, which he kindly posts and redrafts for us.

An excellent lecturer and really nice guy. In terms of difficulty and workload, his is about the same as any other section of CS 3600 - a moderate amount of work and you have to understand things beyond the level of the projects to pass the exams, but if you do that it's not hard to earn an A.

analysis.name: Byung-Cheol Kim
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Easiest class I've ever taken. Practices test sometimes identical to the actual test. Rarely went to class but about once a week he offers 5-10 points extra credit on your test. Read the book and did online homework to get an A.
You have to be trying to fail this class. Honestly, the homework practically does itself and if you do the homework and put in the tiniest amount of effort you'll get an A
SUPER easy! He gives so much extra credit you can make up an entire test and then some, if you come to class and do the extra credit you'll get an A or at least a B

He's very nice and really wants all his students to get A's. If you go to class, you can get good grades on all of the tests and homework assignments without studying. Also gives out a LOT of extra credit.

analysis.name: Keagan Callis
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Does not teach well at all, no point in showing up to lectures. Also super disorganized, would never post notes, or announcements. Super hard to reach outside of class, would never respond to emails either. Studio is where I learned everything.

Tbh stopped attending lectured after the first 2 months bc they tend to be very slow and boring. I felt like studios were much more helpful to learn content because we practiced what we learn so attend studios and make sure to do the practice exams that are posted because the exams are pretty much the same questions and format.

He often shows up to class late seemingly in a rush - also seems like he is learning his presentation slides as he goes along. Like he is surprised by what is on them. Gets half of the questions wrong and doesn't have a clear format for how he wants to teach. Get someone else, but 2 hour linear you can somewhat learn on your own. For 1553 not 1552

I went to the first class, and immediately knew it wouldn't be worth going ever again. ADHD, disorganized, doesn't stay on schedule. There are videos posted on Canvas by a much better professor you can just watch instead. Homeworks are very fair, and tests are quite easy. Overall, I would take him again ONLY because lectures weren't mandatory.

terrible unorganized lectures and cannot answer ed discussion/emails to save his life. our section was apparently the easiest tho idk. exams are not horrendous but often harder than his practice exams. quizzes were incredibly unfair and he didn't do much to remediate the consistently failing quiz averages.

analysis.name: Carolyn McNamara
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Lectures and office hours were the key for this class. She was awesome in office hours and broke concepts & practice questions down very well. The tests were kinda difficult, so redo the problem sets while changing information given. Group project was really interesting as well! Dr. McNamara is easily one of the best professors I've had at Tech!
Clear and fair. Grading criteria sticks to what's in the syllabus.

Dr. McNamara is an amazing lecturerer. She comes to class prepared and really knows the content. Her problem sets can be difficult. Use the TA for help with them. Her exams are also a little tough sometimes but she curved them to be a B average minimum.

analysis.name: Robert Caraway
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 16 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: VERY kind and respectful. Its clear he wants you to succeed, NOTHING is meant to trick you or set you up for failure. Come to class and do the HW. Exams are VERY fair and grading is forgiving. Effort is rewarded. Lectures could be better tbh (concepts need time to marinate, not totally his fault), but if confused watch Jeff Hanson on YT. Good Prof.

This is the professor who will bring candy during a midterm & is very helpful with questions The lectures are example heavy, so expect to get a lot of practice. The grading scale can be kind of harsh if you are not on top of your assignments like me, but even so I've learned a lot in the class.  If you put in the effort, you will get a good grade.

Very direct lectures that do not waste the 50 minute block. The in class practice questions and the homework questions prepare you well for the tests. Be prepared to spend some time on the homework questions and do not procrastinate. Office hours are also very helpful for better understanding course material and homework problems.

Loved him! He was a great lecturer that explained things in a way that made sense, but he was also great at answering questions about things that don't make sense. He was always friendly, told us what exams would be like and never put things on exams that we didn't go over in class, and tailored homework to be perfectly aligned. Highly recommend.

Professor Caraway made statics way easier by being open to all questions to ensure everyone understands the material and being lenient on exams and grades. Class feels less forced to attend since he keeps lectures concise, fun, and engaging, and his final project was really fun to work on. 10/10 instructor who genuinely cares about your success.

analysis.name: Richard Causey
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: Very cool teacher. He is funny and always willing to help. Book is completely unneeded, don't waste your money, just go to class and take notes and you will get A's on all the tests. Tests are straight from lecture and almost exactly the as practice tests. Just go to lecture, read notes, take practice test and the extra credit never hurts.

Dr. C is so amazing. I looked forward to going to every lecture. He teaches based on studies and key concepts, which made his lectures easy to follow. He teaches for you to learn and clearly knows his stuff. As long as you take notes and ask questions, you will do well. There are 3 exams and lab, each worth 25% of your grade, so effort matters.

Doesn't use any textbook but just goes over concepts he wants to cover. Only way to get material is by writing notes in lectures. Shouldn't have been a hard class but the tests have a lot of weirdly worded questions. Somehow after 2 years of GT pre-med classes this is the only class I couldn't get an A in, which is ridiculous for a gen psych class.

Dr. Catrambone is a great professor who teaches in an old-school way -- just notes on the board. He's an engaging lecturer with dry humor and witty remarks. Tests are a majority of the grade, and while essay based, the TA is very picky about wording, making it hard to score well. At least 15% of the class will get an A, but it will be hard.

Very fun class, don't bother buying the book, but don't take this class if you don't plan on attending.  Tests are long but lecture based.  I love his teaching style and recomend the class.  Plus he's funny and explains things very well.

analysis.name: Antonio Cardentey
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Expect to participate 1-2 times each class, and make sure you're doing the weekly assignments and readings since those same topics will be brought up during lecture to be discussed. Really enjoyed the times I got to speak with native speakers around the world for 30 minutes, and learn more about their lives while also improving my Spanish.

Dr. Cardentey's sheer knowledge and clear passion for the subject matter were refreshing. You could tell throughout the course that he truly wanted his students to understand the nuances of the region through sci-fi, as it would improve us as students across all of our various majors. Truly recommend!

I took this course online, and it was great. Because there were no in-person lectures, we had to do 50-minute weekly Zoom conversations with small groups, but they were pretty low-stress. Dr. Cardentey gives great feedback and his class has helped me fine-tune my Spanish skills. He is also very caring and flexible. Definitely recommend!

Dr. Cardentey was extremely knowledgeable about all of the course material and was extremely interesting and enthusiastic in his lectures in class. This always made me excited to come to class and I feel like I learnt the most in the class, compared to the numerous other Spanish courses I've taken thus far at Georgia Tech.

prof cardentey is amazing! almost all assignments are collaborative, and i left the class feeling way more confident in my speaking skills. 10/10 would take this class again and would recommend to anyone taking spanish at tech!!

analysis.name: George Burdell

Just by having George as a professor, Scheller should be #1 business school in the nation (Wharton who?).
Burdell has had a bigger impact on my life than anybody else, and taking his classes have been the highlight of my college experience.  Run--don't walk--to register for anyone of his classes.

Dr. Burdell is faultless. As if his classically handsome good looks aren't enough, he is a true scholar and so accomplished. His THWG101 class was inspired, and his research on the devastating effects of the red and black color combination on brain cells was fascinating. Highly recommend going to his office hours (inside the T of Tech Tower).
Literally a God of a Professor. I've heard he's been here forever and I've never heard anything bad about him. He is the sole reason I passed THWG101.
The looks of Jon Hamm and the brains of Al Einstein

analysis.name: Cecilia Testart

I enjoyed this class, even though it was a little bit boring sometimes (it was an hour and a half long). But she is definitely a good professor!

Prof. Montes-Alcala was the best Spanish professor I've ever had. She's brilliant, highly organized, demanding but fair, funny and very attractive! I appreciated him. He's definitely one of the better combo professors when compared to the others. Reasonable tests and homework. Lectures are pretty good. This class was really hard though and I dont think even the best combo professor in the world can make combo a seamless experience. If you suck at math, buckle in your seat belts.

Class is very test heavy, however lots of practice tests/finals were provided. Id recommend taking him but its still a difficult class. He made it suck a little less though. He is not condescending to stupid questions and made me comfortable to ask away to my hearts content. His notes were a little strange so take your own notes.

Professor Cervantes was incredible. He is extremely approachable and cares immensely for his students' success in his class. But definitely the best choice for 3012.

MATH 3012, in general, is probably one of the hardest class I've ever taken content-wise. He made this class much more bearable and showed genuine care and respect for his students. W Teacher. Dude is the goat. Take this class if you want to pass and actually learn the material. Plays music and gatech football highlights at the beginning of class, and always walks in with a chick-fil-a lemonade. Im tryna be like bro when I grow up fr.

Very enthusiastic in every lecture, brought great energy. Study sessions in class for big tests (2) which are all multiple choice. Dr. Ciavatta was nice, but he simply is not the best professor for genetics and is not the most knowledgeable on the subject. He relied on ppt slides that were pretty vague and uninformative. He is approachable and listens to the students. He is one of the few professors that seems to care about the students. He is fair and knows the subject well. Go to class and do the homework. Great professor.  The class is not bad, just study and do the homework.  Make sure you study a lot for the first exam because it's really hard; the department made it so you don't finish it on time.  The second one is not bad, and neither is the final.

Has an accent but it isnt bad, lectures were pretty helpful, curves the class at the end, would say very good teacher compared to other calc 2 professors, one of the easier math classes I have taken at Tech

He's very easy to reach via email and is always trying to make the experience better for the students he teaches. The video lectures are well done and help you work at your own pace which I really appreciated.

If you are at all interested in jazz, take this class! Video lectures are pretty short but very thorough. I had fun going to jazz clubs with friends for the concert reports. Tons (up to ~30%) of easy extra credit. 4 online honorlock exams that are pure memorization of facts.

The lecture videos are very lighthearted and delivered well, and this is one of the few classes I've seen where the instructor is perhaps more active than the TAs. Information comes out pretty early, and there's plenty of support in online tutorials if you need help.

He was great as a professor, the projects were a bit hard at times but if you start early it's fine and you should get through them. Just be expressive and make music you like and write that in the review and he will understand where you are coming from.

This often results in class grades on tests being low, but he will curve (I think 75% is typically an A)

Di Leo is an experience. A true force of nature. His AE 3140 notes/exams/quizzes are exactly the same as he uses for AE 6115 and the qual exams given to prospective MS students in his lab. Will it be easy? No. Will you come out of 3140 with probably the best knowledge of structures that you can get as an undergrad? I'd bet money on it.

The professor is a good guy, reachable and really understands the material, but the TA Jamshid who grades all exams is very harsh, strict and unforgiving in grading, resulting in a very low average on all tests. Would be better if the Prof chooses another TA.

Structures is really hard and this was his first semester teaching, but he did really really well (even though the test averages were in the 50's, uncurved thankfully). He really knows what he's talking about and also really believes in feedback and seeing what we think about the class. He is very quality and I recommend for any class.

Structures is known as one of the "hard" classes in AE, and Prof. Di Leo makes it bearable! Without a curve, we would all have failed the class, but we know from the start we get a curve. He makes the lectures interesting and makes sure the class is learning. He makes activities to help us learn. Great professor!

review_highlights.comment: Very good professor and cares about her students. There is a lot of writing assignments in this course, but she gives you plenty of time to complete them and they seem decently relevant to computer science fieldwork.

This class is probably the worst I've taken here during my time at Tech. Attendance for this class is mandatory. The class is at 8 AM, and if you miss five classes, they will fail you. How nonsensical. This class is the epitome of "this could have been an email." If you have to make attendance mandatory, make your lectures worth my time.

Too many components to your final grade. For example, a 1000 word essay is just worth 5%. Although she is lenient grader, the amount of work is a lot more than what you'd expect. However, if you like reading and writing, its an interesting class.

The ratio of the amount of work for an assignment to its percentage on the final grade is insane. Get ready for writing long essays, documents, and presenting. But if you put in the work, you will get the grade.

Dr. Coblentz is a fantastic professor and super passionate about the class. She will call on you to answer if no one speaks up, but participation is not graded harshly. She manages to sneak in real-world applications such as creating a video essay and group website/app project. She also greatly streamlines the portfolio-making process from Day 1.

analysis.name: Richard Cowan
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Really easygoing professor; the material and tests/quizzes are extremely straightforward. He wants the students to succeed. He even throws in a joke here and there to make the class laugh. Great Professor.
The course is rated highly for its difficulty due to the professor's old-fashioned teaching style. Assignments are administered exclusively through physical papers rather than online platforms.

ME2110 is a timesink, but Dr. Cowan makes it fun. Your grade is determined more by your studio professor and TA, but if you have Cowan as your studio TA (like I did), he grades well and is easy to reach out to. Final grade bounds are extremely flexible, most will get an A even with an 80% final grade as long as you show you tried and put in effort.

Dr. Cowan is a nice professor but you might have to really work for your grade. His exams really test your understanding of the subject and he is a tough grader. Be sure to understand as you learn each topic. He does not curve the grades.

Lectures are great but a lil dry and really dense towards end of semester. Really makes you work to understand the concepts. Grades tests fair but tough and paper pretty easy. Super accessible in/out of class and really helpful. know the hw inside and out and don't use online sources to help you figure them out or it'll hurt on the exams. take him

analysis.name: Thomas Conte
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: This is one of the hardest classes I've taken, but the professor was very helpful. He explains concepts clearly and has a great sense of humor. Lectures are informative, though it can be hard to keep up with notes since laptops aren't allowed. Because the material builds quickly, it's easy to fall behind, but he provides many resources to catch up.

He's got a great sense of humor, explains things well, and you can tell he really cares. Lectures were informative and entertaining, but often difficult to keep up with when taking notes since he disallowed laptops. It's easy to fall behind or get lost, since everything builds off what's before it, but he gives enough resources to catch up easily.

Loved Conte's lectures. Definitely a hit-or-miss depending on personal preference, but I thought his lectures were fairly straight forward and in logical order. As long as you paid attention in lecture, there wasn't really a need to open the textbook. Projects, homework, and quizzes were clear and reasonable. Would recommend 10/10.
Great professor Did an excellent job of explaining topics to students. Everything learned in one class tied in really well with the next class. Skipping class will really mess you up though...

Prof Conte is a great guy who gives very enjoyable lectures. The projects, especially if you don't have a great background in architecture, are really hard. They are also graded in an interesting way, where you basically get a 65% credit by default, but to earn the rest of the points you need to get the project 100% correctly implemented.

analysis.name: Thomas Crawford

review_highlights.comment: Great prof! Very reading heavy and class was just discussion over what was read. 4 essays very light grader with good feedback.

MY FAVORITE TEACHER EVER. I am impressed every lecture with how knowledgeable he is. He is so engaging. There is a discussion post for every reading and a reading every class. 2 take home essays & a final project but he's a very very easy grader as long as you try. an A is very achievable if you are attentive and enaged during discussion.
This guy is the absolute goat ! I loved having him as a teacher and I hope everyone gets to take his class !!!!

Took Literature and Medicine with him, super cool topic and awesome professor. Very understanding and easy grader. Basically if you put a little bit of effort in and have reading comprehension skills and participate in discussion once, you'll get an A. The material was good, prof has some fun lore, sometimes a little boring but overall great lmc.

This man was born to be a professor. He is probably one of the best lecturers I have had at Gatech. Depending on the class, you will have to read a lot but it's 100% necessary for the tests and final project. For LMC2100, the tests were all take home essays and he was super lenient with grading as long as he sees that you understand the readings.

analysis.name: Ernest Croot
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Croot could not possibly care less about the fate of his students. He spends his lectures reading bullet points off of his phone, rewriting them on the whiteboard, and then waving his hands and saying "So obviously, this is trivial." The book isn't incredibly helpful, but it at least points you in the right direction for figuring out what to learn.

By far least favorite professor at Tech. Was very rude when I asked questions during exams, lectures were extremely boring and really helpful, homework was unnecessarily difficult. There was a problem he had to un-assign because he realized even he couldn't solve it. That said, HW grading was generous, and he curved exams when everyone failed.

Exams 5 questions each (final 10). He is a generous grader all things considered but he writes the exams to have a median of 75, and if the median is lower, he curves everyone's grades to get there. Lectures are not great, most skip.
Mid1: Mean 84 Med 91; Mid2: Mean 77 Med 75; Final: Mean 72 Med 70 (pre curve).

He's dry, but solid, starts from the basics on every topic, he once checked if we knew what a prime number was. You need strong math instincts for rearranging problems because he goes quickly there. Use his bundled notes, they're great, 100 pages of study material, jump around, study what you need. Runs his office hours like the navy, in and out!

I stopped going to lectures just because I could not follow along, his teaching style just didn't fit me. You need to focus more on learning the theory to succeed. Tough tests, lenient grader, and there are curves.  He seems interested in the topics though, just wished he posted notes after class, his canvas page was empty all year. Not tech-savvy.

analysis.name: Kelly  Cross
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Cross is genuinely not a professor. She did not teach our lecture section ONCE, just got up to preach about wellness and "doing what we've been doing". Only reason I'm not rating a 1 is because the TAs pretty much teach the course anyways, so it doesn't affect much. Homework and quizzes are difficult but if you study with a group its not bad.

Had her for BMED 1000 and it was fine. She is kind of mean and not very understanding. I interacted with her minimally since it was just a 1 credit class, but I would not take her for an actual class.

Ok so Dr. Cross isn't terrible. She just...wasn't really there. Only take her class if you're comfortable self-teaching 99% of it. I hear GT is making improvements to BMED 2110 for future semesters, though, so it might get better than it was for us. Her biggest mistake was giving 1/2 the class only 2 hours for what was supposed to be a 3 hour exam.

Dr. Cross appeared to be a nice person but if I'm being honest, she didn't know anything in regard to BME. If you asked her a question, the first thing she would ask you is if your question made common sense, which is not something that I want to hear if I asked a question. She also shorted us on time for the final exam by an hour. Don't recommend

never showed up to class, and when she did it was to tell us to practice mindfulness, eat, sleep, and preach condescendingly to us about the course material. She does not know anything about the material. I asked her a question and her response was, "think about it." Im sorry, what did i take this class for? TA's make or break the course

analysis.name: Cameron Crotts
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took history of jazz with Prof. Crotts over the summer. Class was taught either by him or his coworker friend. Tests are not hard if you memorize the slides. Content is really interesting and a nice break from these rigorous STEM classes at Tech. Highly recommended for that Humanities credit.

Wonderful class. Laid back instructors and interesting material. Bonus: we got out early almost every day. Great choice for a humanities elective or free elective during the summer. If you do anything in this class, you will almost certainly make an A.

This course is great if you need an easy A humanities course. I took this course online over the summer, and it was async and ended in the first week of June. There were three exams and one paper, which can be exempted if you get 100s on all three exams. Crotts was very caring and lenient, and he provides all the material you need to ace the exams.

One of the most easiest class at GT if taken online. The classes is comprised of 3 exams and 1 paper, all of which are really easy. The summer online class is asynch and self-paced. All the resources to do good on the exams are provided in Canvas. The research paper is extremely light and templates are provided as guides. Extremely recommend!

Took MUSI 3630 during the summer semester for my humanities credit. Best humanities to take. Very interesting (especially is you love music) and easy to follow in a such a fast-paced semester. Crotts is super understanding, very helpful, and very accessible. Would definitely recommend if you want an easy, interesting GPA booster + humanities req.

review_highlights.comment: If you haven't taken AP stats in HS , don't expect to get over a C in the class

Smart professor , but teaching is not for everybody ! If you care about your GPA , don't do it !!!!!!!! Many students dropped this class because of the way it was taught . Expect ridiculously confusing problems and expect to get 10,5,20 out of 100 on your quizzes ! . (Did not get an A+)

There are good and bad professors and then there's Tovey. Literally the worst professor I've had so far. Not a good intro teacher to IE. Listen to the reviews and avoid AT ALL COST. Very disorganized, gives no partial credit, and should not be teaching at all. If you cherish your life and your sanity, you would listen to me and avoid tovey....

Do not take AT ALL COST. His grading makes no sense and it seems like he doesn't even grade correctly. Just gives points where he wants. He makes up the questions for the tests, and the answers have no clear explanation or reasoning behind them. He just slaps answers together with no clear thinking. Ok class but bad professor.

This is the hardest class I've ever taken. I did not take AP stats in high school and I have no idea what is going on in this class. Every time I show up to lecture it feels like I've missed a lecture in between. He is very unhelpful and is often incredibly condescending to his students. Do not take 2027 with him or you're gonna have a bad time.

analysis.name: Courtney Crooks
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment:
Professor was unwilling to discuss or move assignment dates, frequently released assignments late, and didn't post lectures after she said she would. Essays questions were very complex for the maximum length. Lectures were randomly mandatory and often dull. Easy to get an A, but professor was not easy to work with.
Class taken was CS4263.

Dr. Crooks is so knowledgeable in the field of cyberpsychology. Her lectures were so interesting and covered a lot of different topics related to online behavior and security in depth. Your grade is based on 4 short (2-3 page) reflection papers and 1 final (10-12 page) paper. She's a really easy grader and willing to help you out. Take her!

Very nice, but essentially reads off of the lecture slides. Don't come to class unless you care about the small extra-credit pop quizzes, otherwise look at the study guides she posts as well as the definitions for the book's vocab words and the tests will be a breeze. Very easy grader, very simple tests.

Dr. Crooks's section of General Psych was so much easier compared to others. We had 5 tests that were not cumulative and easy. Going to lecture is completely optional. As long as you read the textbook and can answer her study guides, you will be fine.

Class was super chill. She largely reads off the lecture slides which she also posts. She also provides a study guide before each exam. The exams are also multiple choice. Easy A and very little effort put in.

analysis.name: Cristina Riso
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Aeroelasticity is an extremely difficult class regardless of which professor is teaching it, but Dr. Riso is one of (if not my favorite) my favorite professors at Tech. Although this is only her 2nd time teaching, She's super caring and extremely flexible with deadlines, and is willing to hold additional office hours outside of her normal hours.

AE 4220 is probably the toughest course in the AE curriculum, but Dr. Riso is fantastic. Her lectures are great, and she is SUPER nice. The homework and exams were brutal but fair. Do not expect to pass by just memorizing how to solve the problems. At the end if you're on the edge and you have an outlier score, she'll bump you.

Difficult class. Extremely nice and caring professor. Dr. Riso is willing to sit with you 1 on 1 outside of regular office hours to ensure you understand the material. Everything is take home, but don't lower your guard. The exams are difficult because they require you to actually reason through the concepts to solve the problems.

Great professor, but the content in class as a whole is too advanced to be offered in undergrad imo (not Dr. Riso's fault). Unsteady aerodynamics - a graduate level topic appears in dynamic aeroelasticity, and you need a pretty good grasp of it to understand concepts such as aeroelastic flutter.

AE6230 Actually. 
Professor Riso is amazing. She is extremely reasonable and helpful. The lectures are well structured and to the point. The lectures and assignments complement each other very well. I learnt a lot in her lectures.

analysis.name: Jim Craig
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Took Dr. Craig for COE 3001 in Fall 2016. Homework assignments were incredibly difficult and time-intensive. Lectures lacked organization and were not helpful. Incredibly smart guy, great personality, but he made what should have been a simpler class much more difficult than it needed to be.

The professor is knowledgeable (wrote the textbook), but lectures are outdated—he mostly reads notes with little practical application. Few graded items; the final is 45% (avg was 57.5). Homework is time-consuming (5–8 hrs). Generous curve, so most get A/B. Advice: Skip class, self-study, and prep using past exams/homework, help classmates, pray.

Random question bank 10 minute biweekly quizzes. Homework is 25% while each exam/project is 5%. Final is 45%. Dr. Craig is a professor who has a severe disconnect between the course material and his students. Uses custom notation, changes it randomly, and very unclear when explaining topics. Usually only prof to teach this class, best of luck.

Yet another one of those GT profs who is plenty smart but has completely forgotten how to communicate to people for whom the material is new. He has lots of resources, which seems to be in lieu of streamlining the class. The homeworks are always huge and have to be done with one specific "method" he makes up. Each usually takes 8+ hours.

Incredibly smart, but has gotten so out of touch as to what it is like to learn new material. He will skip past the foundation for many topics because it's "so easy that anyone can do it." and skip straight to difficult problems. He only allows 30 min for tests that would easily take over an hour. Very condescending to any questions someone asks.

analysis.name: Cuyler Warnock
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: WARNOCK MY GOAT THE GLAZE IS REAL whoever called him the Lorax is so accurate my guy knows anything and everything about math. He is so passionate about Linear it rubs off onto you and he really tries his best in lectures to explain everything in layman's terms. Linear is hard but he makes it doable/even easy. I will miss him and his teaching sm :(

Professor Warnock is an excellent lecturer with some of the most clear explanations I've experienced. I've heard of other students even saying they come to our lectures instead. He also projects his voice really well. Even in the back of a 200 person lecture hall with no mic, I can hear him perfectly. I recommend him to anyone who can get him.

Grading: 3 Midterms + 1 Final (worst midterm 15%, all others & final 20%). "Bucket point" system for the other 25% (need 70pts/120 for full credit)

Lecture: 9/10; Passion: 9/10; Communication: 10/10; Flexibility: 9/10; Test Prep: 10/10

Quirks: Bad handwriting, likes teaching 8:25 a.m. MWF

Recommendation: Would be my first choice for this course.

W professor. The class is pretty hard but if you lock in you can definitely get a good grade. I would also recommend reading through the course textbook Lay Linear Algebra since it follows the course really closely and goes into more details than the lectures have time for, and you lowkey need that for the true and false sections on the tests.

Extremely accessible outside of class. Best linear lecturer by far, took his time to clearly explain material and did not rush through the content. Provided great reviews for the tests, and clearly cares about the success of his students. If you have a different lecturer and are struggling, try to come to his instead as attendance isn't mandatory.

analysis.name: Christian Cuba-Torres
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Real solid professor. Has helpful handouts for each lecture. Clear and straightforward with everything.
He does a good job with his lectures and provides handouts to help students follow his lectures. He is available outside of class and grades/curves fairly.
He is a great teacher who cares about his students. Will take him again gladly, even if he's only teaching an 8 am.

This course is quite tough and requires constant practice; however, Dr. Cuba helps as much as he can by providing: useful notes, midterm reviews, and great lectures. The class averages for all three exams were quite low, but he compensates most everyone who never gave up. Not an easy A.

The ratings who gave Dr. Cuba a 2/3 for kinetics are unreasonable. Though the midterm average was not the best, he kept that in mind and lowered the grade cut-offs based on our grades. He cares about his students. His fill in the blank notes are nice. He records his lectures, so if you miss something in the notes, you can always go back to watch.

analysis.name: Andrew Culbreth
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Culbreth is certainly one of the best professors I've encountered at Tech! His enthusiasm for philosophy is clear to see in his passion infused lectures. He'll challenge your thinking and his own as well, and it's quite honestly a marvelous aspect of his teaching. There is a fair amount of reading, so just pay attention and it'll be fine!

I took Dr. Culbreth for his Philosophy 185 course Emory this past semester, and I have nothing but the highest regard for him. Dr. Culbreth challenges his students to tackle discussion, find meaning and interpret text. He is a passionate, caring and immensely intelligent professor whose courses are rewarding and I cannot recommend enough.

The most passionate professor you'll find! He has definitely made philosophy fun, and during lectures/Q&A sessions you can see his eyes glow when he talks. Very reading heavy, but he supplies reading guides as well. Excellent class
Great teaching style. Cares about students

analysis.name: Jianbo Cui
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: His accent is very hard to understand, and to be completely honest, I don't go to class very often because of it. Still, he's a really nice professor and is more than willing to answer your questions. He's very accessible outside of class and understanding if you have to make up quizzes. If you have concerns, you can email and get a quick response.

Dr. Cui's accent is very heavy and it's hard to understand what he says sometimes. However, he definitely knows his stuff and he tries very hard to help his students; he's extremely good at listening to student feedback and clearly wants you to succeed. As long as you sit up front, follow along in lecture, and do your homework, you should be good.
He speaks with a very thick accent that makes him hard to understand in lecture. He teaches the content fine it is just hard to understand him.

Very heavy accent, but fairly competent lecturer. The structure of his lectures can be hard to follow but you can adjust to the accent. The textbook is free, online, and is an absolute godsend that can carry you through the class, regardless of your prof. His tests and quizzes are on the easier side for 1553.

Really heavy accent so it was hard to learn the already hard math subject. Tries to help out but I learned more from the TA. I just read the textbook, did the HW, and went to tutoring. Definitely more helpful than the professor himself.

analysis.name: Amalia Culiuc
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Math at Tech is HAAARD, but Amalia is both fair, supportive, humorous funny. The way she approaches lectures is very effective: she lays out the basic maths concept, explains it again in layman's words, then does a few examples. Practice your homework until you understand it WELL or you'll suffer. She curves, so don't freak out. Also: OFFICE HOURS.

Tests are fairly straightforward, shouldn't have to study too much; weekly quizzes which help a lot; lectures are easy to follow; Amalia is easy to reach outside of class and gives good feedback; class curved at the end.

She explains things clearly. She also moves at a very reasonable pace and reviews concepts in class instead of rushing through the material like the other profs. She's willing to answer all of your questions and she's super nice. She does make a few mistakes on the board though but she'll give out candy for every 15 mistakes she makes!

I had a lot of problems with this class, thankfully Amalia did her best to make my time easier. Gives very good feedback and is very responsive and helpful whenever you have concerns. She is very clear about the topics you should know for each exam and is more than willing to give a bit of a curve for the sake of fairness.

By far the best math teacher I have had at Tech. She explains things very clearly and moves at a pace so that you don't feel like the class is a week ahead of what you are understanding. The lectures are very interactive and she strives to get students involved during lecture. As long as you do the homework and go to lecture, the tests are doable.

analysis.name: Ken Cunefare
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: The material in this class was super interesting to me. Dr. Cunefare has a definite interest in the material and does really try to get students to enjoy it as well. The class can get pretty tedious, and the homeworks are commonly over things we haven't covered yet in lecture.

Fantastic professor who actually made me interested in the content. He gives you everything you need to know in his lectures, and by the end of the semester, he makes sure everyone gets a fair grade, even if the semester is tough.
Enjoyed the IC Engines class.  It was difficult but Dr. C's lectures were well planned and the material was clearly presented.
Disrespectful to students. Doesn't care about you.

analysis.name: Dan Kotlyar
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Hands down the best professor I have ever had. He provides all lectures as printed, fillable pamphlets and is a very good lecturer. Homework follows lecture content and is harder than exams. Grading is done quickly and very fairly. I always wanted to go to lecture because he was very funny.

Absolutely named Dan GOATlyar, one of the best professors I have had. I would definitely take another course with him. All notes were very structured and the homework was challenging, but followed them closely and he was easily accessible for questions or office hours.

The class is hard and daunting and its easy to get lost, but: Homework is very representative of the lectures, lecture notes are clear and concise, and Kotlyar is genuinely interested in what he's teaching and is good at it. You will need to stay focused in class, but he's generous in grading and his tests are the most fair I've seen at Tech.

Had Dr. Kotlyar for NRE 4210. He is easily my favorite professor in the NRE department. He is able to clearly explain complex subjects with ease, and his lectures are full of useful diagrams and equations to support the theory. He made the class a bit too easy this semester, but it was still incredibly informative. GT is lucky to have Dr. Kotlyar.
He makes the otherwise difficult material easier to understand. He's humorous and a genuinely good lecturer.

analysis.name: Denis Tsygankov

review_highlights.comment: Where do I even begin with Denis... he's just been an amazing professor each time I have had him. He's nice and understanding and is by far one of the most human and enjoyable professors in the BMED department. If I ever see a course being taught by this man, I'm snagging it as fast as I can!

The lectures are okay. The PSS sessions are the most helpful and generally indicate what will be on the test or quiz.

He leans heavily on prior knowledge, especially from statics. He will teach you the problem solving methods which are straightforward, but get harder through the semester, and he expects a lot of self learning.

"No hope" is the advice he gave for studying for one of our exams. I really liked his lecturing style, he was very funny.

Be prepared to see things on exams you haven't seen before is my only warning.

Great Professor! The real gem comes during PSS where his humor, talent, & knowledge shines. Makes PSS fun to attend and also allows you to learn a lot during class through focusing on problem solving. Biomechanics is primarily graded by (2 tests + final) which are 25% each, so watch out for them and DO THE HOMEWORK without looking at the answer key

Denis is one of my favorite professors I've had. He's funny, lighthearted, and wants you to succeed. "I want to give you all A's- you just have to help me out a little" - Denis. The class is math and computer science heavy. Recitation sections were set up as group activities that was similar to homework and exam questions.

Before taking that course I'd read on RMP that she made tons of mistakes when teaching;this is VERY TRUE. Every single lectures and every single examples she was making a mistake and followed it by "Oh, I made a mistake guys can you tell where" like no I can't I'm still in the learning process..? Class is an easy PASS though bcs of the grade scale.

Professor Curtis was an extremely difficult professor. Her lectures were not engaging and she made so many mistakes always asking students "Could someone point out where I went wrong?". decent prof/lecturer. she did make mistakes pretty frequently but most were caught by students and corrected, so i thought it was fine. the class was not too hard in my opinion, but i did take and understood ap physics 1 previously, which was basically the same as 2211. curtis obviously isnt as good as alicea, but she's still ok to take imo

She was okay as far. Her lectures were often harder to follow, and she explained concepts in a way that wasn't always productive. There are definitely worse physics 1 professors, but if you can get Alicea that would be the best. Overall, the class wasn't too bad, the labs/bucket points help with grades, but the tests are very difficult.

analysis.name: Shijie Deng

review_highlights.comment: Professor Deng is very accomplished in quant finance, but the teaching in this course did not match its importance as a core QCF requirement. Arguably one of the most important courses in the QCF program, but it's horribly taught by Deng. He spends most of class talking through the slides on theory/proofs and then glosses over real applications. Quizzes and tests are very hard.

My biggest gripe were the homeworks. I was a math undergrad but the amount of effort expected for biweekly homeworks was ridiculous. The homework questions often covered material completely unrelated to anything presentend in lecture! And of course the homework averages are really high because I'm sure everyone is cheating on the homeworks.

While the concepts covered were quite extensive his learning style is heavily theory based and he mostly just reads from the slides. The exams are twice as hard as the homework and ask you to apply theory to the most convoluted examples. He does care about the topics though so if you are interested he's a great resource
Overall solid professor, with good lectures. Tests are difficult but fair for a graduate course.

analysis.name: Chaitanya Deo

analysis.name: Christie  Debelius

review_highlights.comment:
Dr. Debelius is AMAZING! end of review. 

She's really caring about students, understanding, funny, and gives you extra time on assignments + chances to redo. Just make sure you manage your time and not take advantage of her extensions. Her class is such an easy A because she makes it engaging during class time w/ minimal homework. She's great!

Dr. Debelius is such a caring, understanding professor, and you can tell how much she wants us to succeed. Our unit was Romanticism, and I genuinely enjoyed doing the projects that we had. She is very lenient with grading and late assignments. The assigned reading can be a bit of work, but the pieces are genuinely interesting. Highly Recommend!

Dr. Debelius is a really great prof. The class has 3 main "Artifacts," and she uses specifications based grading. They're different multimedia projects and honestly aren't too much work, as she guides you through them and allows for revisions. Show up to class and do your work, but do be prepared to read quite a bit every night.

Dr. D is not only a great professor, but a great person in general. It's clear that she wants her students to succeed - but not to the point where she lets you get away without doing any work. The course is designed in a way that if you put in proper effort, you are guaranteed to get the result you want.

Dr. Debelius is a very caring and understanding professor, especially with deadlines and if you have other things going on in life. The projects weren't super heavy and she gives plenty of in class time to work on the larger ones. Also gives detailed and concrete feedback on assignments.

do not take. laughs at students proofs and is rude, and expects you to know everything.

Grade breakdown 
15% homework

His teaching was horrible. I don't know if it's because he's new to teaching but he basically reads off slides only; literally shows us what's on there and that's it with almost no explanations. Stopped going to lecture because he just read off of the slides that were posted anyways. He sped through class because he would skip things or not explain. He was nice if he understood what you were talking about. Has an accent but it's not impossible to understand.

review_highlights.comment: This guy is AMAZING. He makes every class interesting and cares about his students. Honestly one of the best professors I've EVER had. The only downside is that each test is 1/3 of your grade, no participation or extra credit points.

Great teacher, had great examples for lectures and made coming to class very enjoyable! The best teacher to teach law, very nice and funny. The exams are online through canvas, and quizzes online through textbook! Would take again and highly recommend.

I took TBGEN 218 with him at UWT. He knows what he's talking about in class and is very engaging and makes the class interesting. You do need to show up to class to get the extra 14 max points. Doesn't really help you with tests/quizzes if you email but will answer in class and help you out. About 10 quizzes and 3 exams all online at home.

Professor Dhooge is by far and away one of the best professors at Scheller. Lecture can get boring during certain subjects but he keeps it interesting for the most part.
I loved Professor Dhooge! He made lectures engaging and interesting. Although the tests are challenging, if you pay attention during class, you should be fine to get an A.

She is an incredibly thoughtful professor who is aware that most people have to take it because it's required, brings a warm and positive energy to the class that is very refreshing. Tests are very fair and don't try and trick you with questions and are accurate to how you understand the material
Very thorough explanation and makes difficult concepts unbelievably easy to understand! Super sweet professor too.

Geninuely amazing professor!!! Be prepared to pull all nighters for this course. He did his absolute best to ensure that you knew what you needed to know for this course. He was nice and you can tell he cared about the content but I also think he was kind of immature because he was upset people didn't come to the lecture that he made: non-mandatory, unrelated to the exam content, and was pretty boring.

very kind and funny professor, but the grading was a bit wonky for the course. he didn't really have a rubric and graded based on how much others included in there answer - most information = highest grade. you have to read journal articles and give a review on them in class and he definitely likes to add his opinions.

I could not recommend Dr. Diggle enough! This course was very engaging and unlike any other course I've taken at Tech. Love this man he's just so nice and accommodating. He knows my name somehow even though I sit in the back row and don't march. He treats everyone with respect. Great guy and great class. Would 100% recommend taking band at Georgia Tech too

Wonderful band director! Will definitely be doing band as much as I can!

review_highlights.comment: Fun, good times. Lots of material and an intense workload, so be wary if you don't have an AE background.

His class was not very helpful to say the least. Classes were awful. 3+ hours of lecturing and most of the time it wasn't even about content. Took class time to explain how he knows so many famous people yet he has been at the same place for 40+ years teaching.

Dr. Mavris spent lots of time into preparing this course. He structured it so students from many different backgrounds get up to speed with aeronautical engineering topics. It's very challenging as multiple courses are condensed into a single class (that's what makes aircraft design challenging). Nonetheless, it's an amazing learning opportunity.

The set of classes ASDL students take with Doc (Dr. Mavris' nickname) are insanely difficult, but they will make you a better engineer and a better thinker for sure. We call it the bootcamp for a reason. It will be grueling, but if you can brave through the challenge, you will be quite literally "build different" from other engineers

Course material is relevant to the subject. Volume of material is absurd and needs to be parsed into 2 courses. Tests do not effectively measure student's grasp of concepts, ie deductions for not using certain terms regardless if answer correctly addresses question. If you don't need the course, don't bother.

analysis.name: Dina Khapaeva
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Took ML 2500 in Spring 2025 and it was a phenomenal class. She is extremely well knowledged in the topic and a fantastic lecturer. No exams but instead your grade is determined by two presentations and two essays. While the essays are long, she is a generous grader and you have freedom in your writing. Great professor and would strongly recommend!

Dina is very passionate, caring, and warm. I truly appreciated her as a professor, and I hope that I will be able to have her again. Though sometimes the courses focused more on discussion than on the grammar I wanted, she always made herself available for extra help, demonstrated that she truly cared about her students, and taught me how to write!

Slightly disorganized and confused. However, she is very very intelligent and her knowledge of culture and language is immense. Her class is unconventional, but if you show her that you care about the material, the grades come easy. She's not the usual disgusting narcissist that many of the other professors are here, but will take some flexibility.

Professor Khapaeva is incredibly knowledgeable when it comes to Russian culture, film, and literature. Her lectures can seem a bit long and repetitive, but the participation portion of the class keeps it engaging. Be prepared for paper writing- these will determine your grade. She gives good feedback and grades on the nicer side.

I'm a physics major, but I took the class because I thought a "history of fiction" class would be interesting, however it wasn't what I expected. It seemed that she didn't have any sort of direction when teaching. None of the material was connected in anyway. Other than two simple tests we had a 10 page final paper.

analysis.name: Sean Dolan
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty

review_highlights.comment: Spring 2025. Nice guy and you can tell he is intelligent and well-learned.
