I'm sure he didn't mean to be harsh and he did let up when he could tell I was panicking.

He was definitely well informed on the topics of the in class discussions, and he is also very helpful when you ask him for ideas on structuring your assignments. There is almost no way to get a bad grade as long as you complete your assignment on time.

You can tell this professor really knew what he was teaching and he really seemed to care about what was taught. Though he tends to go on a ramble once in a while, he makes it clear what to complete and how to complete it. He's super flexible with deadlines (and gave us a rewrite) and as long as you try you will get an A on every single assignment.

Wonderful guy. He deeply cares about what he teaches and it is so evident. The topic was Ethnography, so it was a little hard to grasp at first, but interesting.  There is sometimes a lot of work but you will get an A if you put in effort. I loved taking Dr.Dolan's class. Only complaint is that he doesnt grade in a timely manner.

Was not a terrible class, grading was easy, but he left pretty much all of the assignments to be graded in the last 2 weeks of the semester. There's a lot of writing in the course, but it comes in bursts - half the time you have no HW, and the other half you have a lot of work to do in order to complete before any of the large projects are due.

Previously recorded lectures are posted online and attendance isn't recorded in lectures though.

Prof Kim is a nice guy and wants to see his students succeed but because attendance isnt mandatory numbers started to dwindle throughout the semester. nice guy but he goes really fast and could not understand much. Basically useless to go to lecture. Just watch the online videos on Canvas instead and save yourself the struggle.
Super nice guy but it was just hard to understand him. Learned from the textbook and online lecture videos, attendance is not mandatory.

I should have gotten an A in this class but honestly I was just being a slacker, would totally recommend!

Very funny, caring and respectful of students, was accessible outside of class and would extend deadlines if needed all to accommodate needs he saw. (MSE6600) Honestly he is a very enjoyable teacher and is very easy to talk to. I went in knowing absolutely nothing and feel like he's very accomodating and helpful. Homework is difficult but he makes sure you understand all you need during class. Would recommend

Clearly values students time, and he extended all of our homeworks if we asked. Pretty much tells you what will be on exams and how to prepare

he definitely can be hard to follow and understand and you will be teaching yourself a lot BUT he really cares about the students (often extends the homework), he is super passionate about the class, and is so open to helping however he can. The tests are harder than the practice tests though so do study.

Dr. Douglas-Green is a very kind and enthusiastic professor. She gives very constructive feedback on assignments and she seems like she really wants you to do well.
BMED 1000 is a pretty annoying class so not Professor Douglas-Green's fault. Make sure to pay attention to due dates and citations in this class.
Thank you Simone Douglas-Green for helping me understand the material. I wish you the best in life. Students, you will enjoy her class.

Super lenient grader, just wants you to succeed so as long as you can make yourself watch the vids you'll be good. Only downside is paying for the course but so worth it.

Could genuinely tell he cared about us students. Broke the material down well but class was designated practice time. Lectures were videos we had to watch on our own time so if that's not your thing beware.

Dr. White's class is tough, but doing the homework, watching the videos, and going to class makes all the difference. His class is flipped, which really helped me to understand the types of questions that would be asked an how to do them. His office hours are amazing. He will sit down with you and walk you through the homework until you understand.

Dr white is insanely intelligent but sometimes it makes it hard to understand what he is teaching or saying because he is so smart. His assignments are super long and he's a tough grader. His exams are also super hard and impossible to finish but he curves. He expects a lot but is super nice. Just be mentally prepared lol

Professor White really wants you to succeed in his class. The whole course is curved so that an 85 is an A, 75 is a B and so on. He also has one test drop so a lot of students did not have to take the final. All of his lectures were posted online and then in class he would work through practice problems.

analysis.name: Doug Yoder

review_highlights.comment: 2 Hr 8AM is hard enough already, but he speaks softly and gets too into the math that doesnt help understanding. Textbook is best. exam prep was a practice exam that didnt match actual; no key provided. Recitations are only good option for review. Exams are hard, with recently improved grading. Not a bad person, but his teaching didn't work for me.

Very receptive to feedback from students. Super talent lecturer and I recommend going to class even if its at 8am, you'd benefit a lot. Exams were super doable if you put in effort.

He is the absolute worst prof I've taken. Crib sheets are allowed but don't help much since he only allows formulas, no labels, no notes, no diagrams, and NO UNITS. His lectures are fairly good I guess, but they cover material beyond the textbook, and he does not cover all the textbook material you need to know, which balloons the material so much.

Dr Yoder purposely makes any class he teaches more difficult than it needs to be. He asks for feedback and then ignores genuine advice when you give it, only responding when you give him compliments. There are many students who take his class 3 or 4 times, and they under stand the material, but Yoder's exams always get them.

Genuinely cares about students. Replies fast to email and piazza.  Grades on understanding, so math errors don't count much off.  But then exam problems sometimes have a nuance or twist.  So you have to learn for a good grade.  Lectures helped me with the textbooks.

analysis.name: Donald Webster
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: Great guy. Honestly, pretty straightforward class. You get a crib sheet for every test, which you honestly don't even need. Just go to class and spend a fair amount of time studying, and you should have no problem getting an A in his class.

Dr. Webster has to be one of the kindest professors at Tech. His class was set up well where you would watch the notes online before class when there were notes, and you would spend the entire class doing practice problems. Dr. Webster did an excellent job doing a problem on the board every class, and he was very helpful if you had any questions.

Extremely helpful in office hours (attend them!) and insanely knowledgable. He made the class very straightforward. Don't underestimate exams though- the partial credit was not generous. Do the in class problems, and if you don't get to them in class make sure you go over them on your own time the same week. Allot plenty of time to study for tests

Dr Webster is an amazing professor. He is always available for answers despite the fact that he is a chair and is fairly busy all the time. Class format also helps you study and understand the material better. Lectures, homework, solution, past exams.. etc are on t-square.  Tests are straightforward. He grades fairly with plenty of partial credits.

The best lecturer I've had, made me much more interested in physics after taking his class as a non-physics major. Difficult course, but grading is pretty lenient with open book exams and lots of extra credit.

review_highlights.comment: Pretty good lecturer in a class that could use some better structure. Most lectures were easy to follow with helpful examples. Homeworks were fair and graded very leniently. Some exam questions were hard to understand and work with, but were graded fairly. Would reccomend!

Dr. Hummel is a fantastic professor who really seems to care and be passionate about teaching ME heat transfer. He connects a lot of the course to his NRE experience which I liked because it makes the class less abstract and more applicable. Fair grader, but it's heat transfer so its just a tough course by nature, wouldn't take it with anyone else

Had Dr. Hummel for NRE 4214, and he did a decent job teaching the content. He is a bit disorganized, and seemingly randomly hand-waived a lot of theory sometimes while diving deep at others. He may not understand theory as well as he should, but he is funny and cares about his students, and he will respond to emails timely. Very lenient grader.

Dr. Hummel is a newer professor, and is still figuring out the best way to lecture to and test his students. Tests were kinda unpredictable, but he's a very good professor, and he's really funny. Give him another year or two to figure out his teaching style and I think he'll be one of the best heat transfer professors at Tech. I def recommend him.

Dr. Hummel was not the best professor I have had at Tech. I feel like with better lecture organization, test structure, and accessibility outside of class my experience would have been A LOT better. The content was presented in a nonchalant manner that sometimes made it hard to follow. He was a nice guy and even funny, but not the best

analysis.name: Dianne Leader

review_highlights.comment: Tests are worth 75% of our grade, and there are 3 tests that count, so be mindful of that. I found that lectures were so boring that I couldn't even fall asleep if I tried. She genuinely cares about the subject matter that she's teaching, and is knowledgeable, but she fails to pass this passion on to her students.

Lectures consisted of slideshows. Each test is 25% of your grade, but you have 4 (including the final) so the lowest doesn't count. The tests seemed harder than the material we learned in class. Dr. Leader is a very sweet lady, but I struggled a lot with this class despite it being an introductory course.

I got a 95% in this class, and I received a B for my final grade, if that tells you anything. Dr. Leader is incompetent with technology. If you can't use technology, just use Canvas and PowerPoint, and have TAs calculate final grades. But Dr. Leader does not do that, and it caused repeated issues this semester that significantly penalized students.

If you have the option, I strongly recommend NOT taking her class. She rarely responds to emails. Her exams are extremely detailed, covering material that was not addressed in lectures. I was excited to take this course because of my interest in psychological disorders, but that enthusiasm was quickly diminished by the way the class was taught.

Super chill professor, but she definitely expected way to much out of us for an "Introduction to Psychology" (and made me HATE psychology if anything). Spent 20+ hours studying for each exam (which is crazy) despite being attentive; also exam questions had lots of ambiguity, and she shot down any exam contesting. Lectures were boring asf too.

analysis.name: Andrew Nance

This professor is a D1 yapper and he would always overexplain a topic which made some things, like homework unclear. He's also very by the book when it comes to giving people grades. You have to follow the assignment requirements down to a T to get a perfect score. He does give extensions on assignments if you talk to him though.
This professor is amazing. I had him for 1102 over the summer and I learned a lot in his class and had fun with the projects he assigned us. Definitely take him if you have the opportunity.
Total Karen. Not serious. Probably reads on weekends and grades like it

analysis.name: Dragomir Davidovic

review_highlights.comment: Professor Davidovic has a good sense of humor, and is better at lecturing than many of the other E&M professors. However, he is very disorganized, forgets to assign homework, and goes extremely slowly through the course content. Our final was on 2 chapters, as this was all we sufficiently covered. Good lecturer, bad administrator, fun experience.

Overall, Professor Davidovic is one of the best professors in the physics department. Electrodynamics is a difficult class, but he is more than willing to take his time to explain difficult concepts. He also has a great sense of humor. I would recommend taking.

Davidovic is constantly unprepared for his lectures and makes many mistakes which end up taking time, assuming he doesnt give up and ask you to figure it out on your own. Ive no doubt he has a good handle on the material he teaches but he can not express it to others well. Thankfully, he followed the book exactly, and the book was written well.

I took this class in Fall 2022, and his tests were take home. However, the tests were SUPER long/hard so I would spend 8+ hours on each one. I think he said he is not doing online tests anymore. We were supposed to cover 6 chapters but we only got to 3 because he went really slow. He lectures straight from the textbook, so no need to go to class.

Professor Davidovic is one of the most caring compassionate professors I have ever had. He's extremely careful to make sure students feel comfortable in his class and extremely flexible when extenuating circumstances arise. He also usually responds to emails within minutes or seconds of being sent. Lectures and tests are reasonable, good textbook

analysis.name: Andrew Newman
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Some of these old reviews are pretty bad but his class is much easier now! Lectures are fast paced, but Dr. Newman is super nice and good at explaining things. Grading came from weekly quizzes (open note) and labs (my TA was super helpful), so overall, not very difficult. My class was for EAS majors so class structure may be different for others.

I took EAS 3610 - Intro to Geophysics. I really enjoyed this class. The lectures were really interesting and Dr Newman did a great job of explaining difficult concepts. The class only had a few homeworks and in-class labs. I highly recommend it.

Andy is a great guy who enjoys answering questions about anything you have. He is passionate about the material and does research related to the class. There were weekly quizzes (open notes), an optional final (open), and a ton of nice information to learn. As an atmosphere person, I didn't feel bored out of my mind, he is very easy to listen to.

Professor Newman is helpful when you ask for help and his notes make sense, but his tests come from out of nowhere. He asked the TA's to take the tests and my TA didn't turn his in because he was embarrassed. He will treat you like a grad student so if you want a breezy easy class, I don't suggest Professor Newman. There will likely be a curve.

Newman is an engaging lecturer, but this course covers a LOT of material. It is difficult to tell what he finds important, and some of the test questions come out of nowhere. If you like your grade after the first 3 exams, you can skip the final. Go to class! He gives pop quizzes that go toward extra credit, and it is why I could skip the final.

analysis.name: Andrew Zangwill
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Zangwill is a boring lecturer and enjoys criticizing the GT-issued textbook and teaching things "the textbook doesn't bother to mention" about physics (even though they probably won't show up on the test). In my opinion he didn't explain anything in lecture in a way that was useful on the tests.

Dr.Z is an excellent professor and lecturer, the problem with his classes and why people don't excel is because his test aren't exams on the knowledge you would learn from the resources given to you. The homework, class notes, and book will not help you on his test even with it being open book. His test are based on intuition on what's in his head.

Dr. Z is the worse professor I have ever taken. He gives no partial credit on test, even for simple adding/subtracting errors. If you like going to class, memorizing what's written on the board, and blindly regurgitating it onto a test then this is the class for you. He is very rude if you go to his office. Also, he doesn't know math notation.

He goes into a lot of theoretical rigor and if you take the time to actually do his derivations/calculations by hand (especially in your own time), you will be beyond prepared for the exams. If you have questions go to his office hours he's pretty chill and will take time to explain. His slides are different, and I think if used well, are better.
I've had professors before who were strict or maybe even a little unfair, but Professor Zangwill is the first professor I have ever had in my life who was genuinely mean.

analysis.name: Alex Draper

You have to come to class and you need to stay on top of your work. Also, please ask as many questions that you need to and you should be ok. However, personally I wouldn't take him again.

Dr Alex Drapper is one terrible professor, he needs to be removed from the school. He lacks teaching skills and overall overload the exams with topics other than what we actually study for. He has very little consideration. Don't take him and save yourself and your GPA.

Dr. Draper doesn't teach - plain and simple. He expects you to learn on your own through the online textbook rather than during his class, and I think that throws a lot of people off since it is just an intro class. Study the textbook and TICA's THOROUGHLY - dit's entirely possible to get an A if you do that.

He thinks group work is more important than lectures. Many people failed his class. They worked very hard. I worked very very hard to pass a class because of his exam structure and his lack of teaching. 

He doesn't teach during class. He assigns too much work. His exams are structured poorly. He grades slowly.

This class is a joke because you don't need to understand why anything works and you can still do amazing. analysis.name: Kelly Duquette
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you have to take an 8am English class, please pick this one. Dr. Williams' class is not an easy one (by common definitions of the word), but if you put in the effort you will succeed in this course. Btw she also responds to emails pretty quickly and makes efforts to help students the best she can!

Can't get any better than Dr. Duquette. She was simply amazing for 1102. Even though our lectures were bright and early, I was always excited to go to class. She is extremely caring and accessible outside of class if you have any questions. The projects were mainly group-based and fun to work on. I HIGHLY suggest taking Dr. Duquette, even at 8 am.

Goat. Everything is clearly laid out and she deeply cares about each student's well-being. It's an appropriate level of work (perfect difficulty) and is interesting. Grades easy. Extremely helpful and relevant feedback. Brings treats for students' birthdays. Incorporates input from students. No flaws. Wish I could take her for all my classes.

This class overall was easy, and Dr. Williams is nice and understanding when you ask her about assignments or need help. The assignments were slightly more work than I expected to spend time on, but overall would say this is a fantastic teacher.

I think this English section is a little more difficult that others. She grades somewhat harshly, with averages for the Artifacts being around a 90. She learns everyones name though and always makes a welcoming environment in class.

analysis.name: Michael Dutcher

review_highlights.comment: super sweet and funny guy! really caring and personable. only gripe is the attendance policy (u will fail the class is u miss 2+ classes) but that's generalized to the class so. class itself was not very helpful if im being honest, but it's only 50 min/week. hes super accessible outside of class and will give u sm chances to makeup absences tho!
this class actually helped me get my 1st internship. he cares a lot and is willing to help at anytime. super awesome and grades lightly.

Super useful class if you're looking for an internship, a lot less so if you already have one. But Dutcher is still a great professor, and the homework isn't that difficult. Like someone else said, it's heavier at the beginning of the semester and gets easier, but it all feels a bit inconvenient for just one credit hour.

Class had no organization or structure- just a final project at the end with no rubric or grading guidelines given. I learned nothing, and received a b despite contributing to the project and attending most lectures.

I found Mr. Dutcher to be incredibly kind and knowledgeable. His best quality is his honesty when it comes to your career field, career ideations, and yourself as a person. The homework is heavy for the first half of the semester but is really light the second half. It's also all really good homework and actually relevant to your life.

analysis.name: Suchismita Dutta

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Dutta is very sweet. You arent required to participate in discussions often but you are expected to read out loud if she calls on you. If you arent an amazing speaker and have troubles or anxieties when giving presentations, she is very understanding. She is also willing to round up your grade as long as you finish the flash writings on time.

A very participation heavy class. She makes you read out loud during class, and as someone with anxiety it was a horrible class to take. I also felt that reading the texts out loud during class was a waste of time when it was our assigned reading before class. If you have anxiety choose a different teacher. If not, you'll be fine I guess.

Was very flexible with deadlines and patient with students. Wanted you to participate and add to daily class discussions. Did often change her mind about criteria for assignments, which could be confusing but was a pretty easy grader. Had relatively low expectations for students. Seemed to genuinely care about students' well-being.

Dr. Dutta is fantastic and one of the best English teachers I've had. She is very accommodating and genuinely cares for her students. Her class was so interesting and I looked forward to going. Very discussion based, not much work outside of the few major assignments of the course. Take her class if you get the chance!

Very caring and understanding professor. I wasn't super interested in the topic at the beginning of the course but the assignments were interesting and engaging and I ended up enjoying the class. Did not take much time outside of class to complete major assignments.

analysis.name: Lane Duncan

We did some cool stuff in his class like nude figure drawing and sometimes he takes his class to piedmont park to draw.
Compared to other professors at Tech, he's at least completed a few actual construction projects; maybe a house every few years.
Really excellent. If you have a chance to take his watercoloring class, take it. It's a hard class, but he's a very good professor--excellent.

6517 is a ML class for people who already know ML. Currently 5 weeks in and completely lost, Dr. Dyer does a poor job explaining and moves too quickly.

The entire class seemed to be about writing fake journal articles. She does not provide prompt feedback - still waiting on a grade for something completed 10 weeks ago. If you want to be a writer, this may be the class for you but if you want to learn machine learning, avoid the prof if at all possible.

Dr. Balog's lectures are so boring; he's monotone and quiet, and his slides have lots of info on them. It's so hard to stay focused in class because it's so boring. analysis.name: Edward Conrad

review_highlights.comment: CHOOSE A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR! Truly one of the more awful physics classes I've ever had. He never actually taught in lecture. He just gave clicker questions on what you're supposed to learn reading the book. And the clicker questions count towards your grade. The only time I really learned in this class was when he left and another teacher taught.

This professor doesn't know how to communicate the lectures very well. He goes too fast with is powerpoints and it is hard to grasp the material in class. I only when to class because there were clicker questions. To succeed you need to know every word in the book. Tests were 5 questions, so if you miss two you fail.

His lectures are not the most helpful as far as the course goes. He often diverges from the textbook, which leads to pretty interesting lectures, but unfortunately not useful for tests. Tests are 5 questions, and they're straight from homework/book. Clickers are large part of grade, and they're often about what he's lecturing, not the book topics.

Too many people give this guy a bad rep. Truth is, I think it's hard to find a professor as fascinated by physics, and if approached after lecture this guy makes very interesting conversation. Yes, the tests are generally 5 questions multiple choice and one free response, but lots of them are quite common sense. Read book, do hw, you'll be fine.

I'd honestly avoid Conrad if at all possible. He doesn't really teach, but rather just gives clicker questions all class over material that you haven't actually learned in lecture, but are supposed to have learned through reading the book. He's not very helpful during office hours either because he doesn't know how to "dumb down" physics enough.

analysis.name: Edward Keene

The class is not easy?there is a lot of reading and writing. But you will definitely learn. I highly recommend his class if you are interested in the subject matter.

He's a pretty cool guy, gotta love the British accent. It's nothing but essays/papers. When you write the essays, and he says you are arguing a point, ARGUE a point. I got a mediocre grade on my first one because I did more commentary. Once I made that adjustment, I blew the other test essays and papers out of the water. Pretty easy B.

A lot of reading, but it isn't always necessary as long as you understand what he is talking about. Two papers in the class and the tests are all essays but he helps you out on those as well. Overall the class is really not that hard as far as college classes go.

Very interesting class.  Note:  Papers ONLY.  However, a STRICT and CONSERVATIVE word count is required, making the papers very challenging.  Also, there is quite alot to read, although it is not all necessary.  It does, however, help considerably.

Very difficult for an intro class. Chapters and chapters of reading out of the book as well as additional readings posted on WebCT were required. Only allows two absences for a MWF class. Nice guy but he talks a lot and is a tough grader.

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Egerstedt did an amazing job teaching Linear Controls. If there is anything called an "Ideal Professor", then Magnus is it. Each time he explains a concept, you feel like giving him a standing ovation. He is funny,charismatic & extremely intelligent. Taking ANY course under Magnus will be the best decision of your academic career. Also, his homework & exams are based on the lectures, so no sweat....

Pr. Egerstedt is the closest thing you can get to a perfect professor. His teaching style is unrivaled. The course is very structured and you don't need much prerequisites. The homeworks and tests are fair and can ace them if you study well. Too bad he is now chair of ECE and no longer has time to share his genius with the students.
Wonderful professor, he made me revisit concepts I already knew in an original way.

fun; appropriate homework (difficulty and quantity). Great lecture! Even I already knew almost all the materials before taking this course, I still find it fun. Plus, his insight give me a different view point on this subject.

Dr. Eichel is easily the best professor I've had. Everything about the class is engaging and interesting it's hard for me to give him lower than a 5.0.

He makes sure to assign works that are both educational and interesting, so the readings are very entertaining and the projects are fun to do. His lectures are very fun and he is very caring and respectful. As long as you do all of the assignments given, you'll get an A in the class.

analysis.name: Amit Einav

She may seem nice but its very fake. She always talked to me with a very passive aggressive and condescending tone. If she was a student she would be the student who peer grades your test harshly and purposely gives you a bad grade.

very caring professor if you participate. some parts of the class seem a bit out of scope for a freshman english class, but theyre pretty fulfilling to complete. its a lot of work at the start of the year and gets lighter until the end of the year.  
if you go to office hours for major assignments youll get a lot of good feedback

review_highlights.comment: Three exams and a final. Only 3 of 4 count towards the grade so the final is optional.  The best way to study for exams is practice tests and reviewing the lecture notes and slides. If you do that you will get an A in this class.

Ingall is a good option for EAS2600. Grade is 75% tests (lowest test is dropped) and 25% lab. You don't need the lectures to pass tests because they're given online and open note. Lectures themselves are interesting if you do decide to go to them, but you don't need them. Labs are easy and straightforward, you only need an hour to do them.

Grades entirely based on exams and lab work. Lab work is pretty fun, easy most of the time. Content itself is on the more interesting side imo. Don't have to attend lecture, reading the slides is enough. Exams are online and unproctored. Read the slides and do practice exams and the exams shouldn't be too difficult. Get to drop lowest exam score

Thermo with Ingall is pretty easy. He is SUPER nice and knowledgeable. Sometimes lectures were hard to follow or homework was quirky, but he is very accessible outside of class and the grading is lenient. (He will zoom if you need help!) The material covered is basic, but it touches all the bases. Highly recommend attending class and participating.

Dr. Ingall is a great professor! He makes thermo concepts easy to grasp. Lectures aren't mandatory, but I would recommend going because there are helpful worksheets in every class. Homework can be hard, but office hours are very helpful, Dr. Ingall is always available. Also, he is so kind and rounded me up to an A because of my effort he noticed.

analysis.name: Liz Hutter
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class is a joke, it has nothing to do with the Health Sciences and she grades it super difficult for not reason at all. Only grade she has put in since midterm is the big Interview grade after giving out homework every single class. It is impossible to get an A in this class. For a health science class this professor does it completely wrong.

This woman is a joke of a professor. She thinks herself better than her students, and made that clear. Her grading rubrics are completely useless and are subject to opinion. She doesn't follow her own guidelines, yet expects students to read her mind. She assigns an unfair workload for a 3 credit hr class. Do NOT take this woman's class.

She is super nice and helps with whatever you need. Grading seemed to be really tough though. It is an easy B but the people who got an A really had to work for it. Also there are no tests or quizzes just a lot of busy work and some big projects at the end.

analysis.name: Elisa Dainese
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Will 100% recommend. Took the class over the summer. Lectures are very interesting. There is reading, but it's manageable. Grading is distributed almost equally over quizzes, discussion reports, and projects. Quizzes are very easy. Projects involve lots of research so don't procrastinate! She gives amazing feedback and is very approachable.

Do not recommend as a humanities. During the summer, her quizzes are easy, online, & open note, but she assigns 30 page readings and doesn't clarify instructions on big projects until 4 days before. Made everyone cram and then questions why we hadn't finished earlier. She posts lectures though; makes her class easy but boring and way too much work

Professor Elisa is so kind! She is very good with disability accommodations and is incredibly patient. She gives very interesting lectures and records them in case people are sick. The course work is reading-heavy (reports based on 10-20 page articles) but there's lots of time to get it done. She also gave us grace periods for every assignment.
Very reasonable workload. Most papers graded by TA's who are available to contact prior to paper submission. Group projects and papers are entirety of grade.

analysis.name: Elliot Moore
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Most people would say the material for this class is pretty hard, but Dr. Moore makes sure you know exactly what you need to do in order to succeed in the class. He emphasizes the important topics and explains them very clearly in a funny way. 10/10 professor and would take again.

Dr. Moore picked up this class from another professor and taught it very well - he clearly has tons of experience in ML. Homeworks could take a long time and were tedious, but lecture slides helped a lot. Exams were take-home/open-note and mostly conceptual.

Really good lecturer, the class is super hard since it is considered a weed out for electrical engineers. Homeworks are super hard but the tests are around the same level so doing good on homeworks means doing good on tests. Test 3 is really hard regardless. Supposedly the fall professors are better. Go to all lectures and recitation.

Worst grading scheme I've ever seen. Only 2 exams, 25% each, and a 30% final. Exams graded in canvas separate from written work. If you get a final answer wrong, the max credit you can get back for your work is 50%. That is what killed my grade in this course. On our 2nd exam, the range of scores was from 0 to 60 out of 60, with an average of 30.

Always an entertaining professor even when the material is a bit dry. The class as a whole is very difficult, but it's made bearable by the professors who teach it. Dr. Moore knows what he is talking about and is more than ready to share it with students who have questions. Enthusiastic, funny, knowledgeable. 10/10 would take again!

analysis.name: Ellen Zerbe
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 9 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took BMED 1000 with Dr. Zerbe and thought she was great. The class itself wasn't my favorite, but she clearly cared about all of us and was passionate and knowledgeable. All of her expectations with assignments are clearly laid out in rubrics and you have opportunities to resubmit work if you really mess it up. Overall great prof!

she's a really good professor but she grades REALLY harshly. when they say you can't miss anything from the rubric your REALLY cannot miss anything from the rubric. make sure your group has the same work all around consistently and always tell your group mates when you change something because it WILL affect their grade.

The professor is chill and passionate about what she teaches. The class is fine, but be careful of due dates since they don't post those on Canvas. You're responsible for submitting the assignments on time, but figuring out when is confusing.

I had Dr. Zerbe for BMED1000 and really appreciated her engagement and enthusiasm in the class. She genuinely seemed to want us to succeed in the course and beyond and has made me more excited for what my future in BME could hold.

Made it clear how each unit was supposed to contribute to something broader. Some of the assignments felt redundant but none of them were hard. If you get a good group (they're randomly assigned at the beginning) then it's light

analysis.name: Emiliano Gutierrez-Popoca
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I would recommend Professor Gutierrez for 1102! This class was focused on Shakespeare, and while I am not a huge Shakespeare fan, the class was interesting and not hard! No exams or essays; rather, you work either independently or in group projects. He is very accessible, and he loves when people participate in class. Overall, a very chill class!!

awk lil guy most times. put in SOME form of effort and you'll end w an A. dont like how useless going to his classes felt w presentations every session about how to do work when we've been in school for quite awhile now... didnt LOVE the topic but also not the worst ever. dont take the 5-6:15 time you will never want to go. would retake!

Class is very easy with a light workload. However, I would take another section of 1102 if available. The topic is Shakespeare which got very boring and the assignments were super repetitive. But if you are just looking to get the credit this course is by no means bad. Its just that there are better/more fun options with other professors.

while his lectures got a little boring from time to time, you can tell he's really passionate about his discipline. he is an extremely nice man, and before breaks would bring little treats for the class and wish us all happy holidays. he's a very easy grader but will also provide useful feedback on projects. he's very approachable as well.

Dr. Emiliano is a great professor, very sweet and enjoys what he teaches. The class isn't difficult, but the lectures were pretty boring. The workload is extremely manageable and there were plenty of group projects throughout his course.

analysis.name: Eliza Markley
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 72 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: This is not an easy A class. I put more effort than one of my ECE classes. If you want to do well go to office hours with TA. Test are honor lock with camera and extremely tricky even if you did the reading. It's manageable to get an A just have to do the readings with notes & the final 10 page research paper. All writings are graded very lightly.

Lazy professor that does not take any pride in instructing this class. Makes this class hard not in the sense that the material is hard, but quizzes you on the most random facts and quotes from random people. Only picked this class because it was online asynchronous and honestly it is not worth it. Take Psych for your ethics requirement guys

Got an A, but this class was very hard and terribly structured. The professor is fine, she does accuse AI use often, but I was able to resolve mine with proof and get credit. The course itself is the issue: dense textbook, six heavy quizzes worth 60%, no extra credit. Unless you love ethics, do not take. TA's were great though, go to office hours.

This professor accuses you of using AI by using AI. You can't make this up. Reports you to OSI, and OSI is very slow in processing. Gives you a 0 before due process which is ironic for an ethics class. 6 quizzes and 3 long papers. Few lectures that are pre-recorded years before, badly organized, you pretty much read and teach yourself everything.

Don't take this class if you care about your mental well-being. It will eat up all your time. Lectures are prerecorded and unhelpful. You will be reading the textbook for hours a week. The quizzes are very specific + difficult. I found myself dedicating more time to this social science credit than my major classes. Can't wait for it to end.

analysis.name: Emma Hu
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: We didn't learn that much in MSE 3025 but I don't think that's really her fault. I think she was a fine lecturer but the content was just pretty simple and I think she was aware of that bc she didn't really care if we paid attention or not and would end lectures early/cancel class more than most to not waste our time

Lectures are extremely dull, covering what feels like 20 mins of content in 75, but tests are open notes and the content is extremely straightforward. Print the notes and take them to exams and you'll do well. Very little programming in this numerical methods class, except for one (very simple) project.

Class is based on participation, 2 tests, and a final. Participation is a bucket point system, and any extra points are extra credit. Tests are very similar to the practice tests she gives to help study. She gave very good lectures that taught what you needed to know. only complaint is that I wish she used piazza, ed discussion, etc.

She had really good lectures often complemented with long textbook sections (optional). Her study guides did not do a great job of covering exam material, though. I also wish she was more accessible outside of lecture; it's tough reaching her, and there was no forum where students could ask questions. Not a bad professor all in all.

Dr. Hu is a great teacher! She is very kind and she truly cares about each student getting a good grade. She always has office hours and reviews exam questions during them. The class is based off of homework memorization.

analysis.name: Emily Sanders
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She is the best ME 2016 professor by far. While homeworks may take a little bit, office hours help a ton, and her homeworks are much more doable than other professors. Her lectures really help with the homework as well. Her tests are extremely fair and straight forward. Probably one of my easier classes this semester.

Dr. Sanders is very knowledgeable and super accessible for help. Homework can be hard, but she's ready to help if you're willing to work earnestly. Homework every week (Matlab coding) and written exams ( straight from lectures). I would take her again!

Sanders is the best option for 2016. Her lecture notes are very clear and you can probably get away with just that and the textbook, but I'd recommend going to class. Her lectures were directly related to the hw and exams (which had no matlab btw), which other 2016 profs had a problem with.

Lecture material is all there but the HW was sometimes very confusing and took minimum 6 hours weekly. Exams were fair and the practice exams helped a lot. Course itself is boring so can't blame the prof on that. 2 midterms 1 final and 10 HWs.

analysis.name: Stanislav Emelianov
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Stas is a very entertaining and enthusiastic lecturer. He has a harsh style of lecturing and even harsher tests. However, he truly does care about the class and does want to see everyone succeed in their own ways.

I can't recommend him enough. He's explains complicated concepts very well holds engaging lectures. He's VERY flexible with due dates and is very down-to-earth with what he expects from students. Exams are very reasonable and can easily be studied for by reviewing HWs and previous exams.

Awesome professor, he knows the concepts and cares about students. One time when I didn't submit a homework assignment, he emailed me to check that everything was alright. He has a great brand of humor and makes concepts interesting and intuitive. Tests are average difficulty, as it homework. He has great availability for office hours.

Best professor I've had at Tech so far. Extremely effective lectures and is very accessible outside of class. Class is set up so that you don't have to stress about grades. Assignments and exams are very reasonable. Provides A LOT of resources.

analysis.name: Alex Endert
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 13 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Endert is a great lecturer and very caring professor. Topics were relevant and I learned a lot, even though I usually don't pay attention in "memorization-based" classes. That being said, the beginning is a little boring but it gets more interesting later, and the final project can be fun if you have a good group. Exams and HWs are easy.

Good choice for an easy elective. Endert is a good lecturer and is engaging to listen to. He is also in general a friendly guy and makes himself pretty accessible. Homework assignments were very straightforward, and so were the exams if you just attended/watched the lectures. The bulk of the class is the group project, so just pick good teammates.

Professor Endert doesn't really teach in this class, instead every class is led by a difficult student group who lead a presentation on an assigned paper and the class discusses. Class ended early every time but the discussions and topics were interesting. The assignments were graded easily and not very time consuming.

Lectures are recorded so attendance isn't required. Unfortunately the lecture content is very boring, but not difficult. There are also coding labs that progressively get harder in Javascript D3, and you need to learn it yourself since lectures don't cover it.

This course is structured with one paper each class, all culminating in a group project. The assignments were moderately time consuming but interesting and ultimately easier than other classes.

He is a great lecturer and has great command over the topics, and the class interactions were quite interesting.

analysis.name: Enlu Zhou
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: By far the most frustrating professor I've had. Doesn't respond to piazza posts or emails (only when convenient), 2 quizzes worth 40% of your grade with extremely minimal prep, homeworks sometimes skipping lectures ahead. When I asked what I could do to improve my grade, I was told that she was not God from her directly. Do not take her class.

The structure of this class has it to where two quizzes taken during the beginning of the course have a LARGE impact on your grade but really they are both tests. She is also not receptive if you don't form a quick understanding of topics in the course and is very hard on regrades even if there are actual mistakes in the grading.

2 quizzes each worth 20%, 1 is a review of 2027. 2 projects each worth 20% with 2 hours to complete them. She's rude when you ask questions and moves to fast when going over simio. Half of her HWs have nothing to do with what we learned in class. Always finding myself using previous notes to do her HW. Not a "hard" class but she's unbearable.

Probably the worst professor at Tech. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS. She will spring surprise assignments on you due dead week, if you ask her for help she'll tell you about her straight A college career, and she reads off of he other professor's slides. She has no idea what she's doing. 10/10 would not take her class again.

The previous ratings don't apply anymore, she completely changed the course syllabus. She has two "quizzes" which are 20% each and covers maybe half the material in the class. The midterm and final project are really difficult and are not a good representation of the material taught. Teaching is ok but it is hard to follow the presentations.

analysis.name: Emily Weigel
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Out of the 3 biology professors that taught BIOL1510 for fall 2016 (Choi, Kerr & Weigel), her test was the most straight forward. Like her test was my first A, my first decent test score. Her lectures are pretty cool too. I feel like they probably planned this on purpose to give us hope that we might have a chance in the class or something.

Dr. Weigel taught the latter half of general ecology which honestly saved my grade from the first professor. Her lectures and expectations are incredibly clear and comprehensible. She is an overall friendly and approachable, as well as knowledgeable, professor who cares a lot about student progress and feedback. 10/10 would recommend.

Dr. Weigel is a very caring and nice professor...but her style of teaching is somewhat vague and you need to know how to code (use R) for the final project even though she rarely teaches it and provides the prompts for assignments. Her test questions are also vague and the TAs are harsh graders. However, the grading scheme is fair.

She was very kind even though the content was a little boring. The grading criteria was very helpful - there's two schemes that maximize your grade! Each test had 2 parts with one being multiple choice and the other part being a "take-home" test that you can work on with a group. The final project was a lot of work so be sure to have a good group.

I took this course in the Fall of 2021. Professor Weigel is passionate about what she teaches. The coursework is not demanding, but does include a lab, which is where most of the work for this class will be done. If you find Biology boring, this will not be a fun class, but it will be easy. If you like it, you will love this class with Weigel

analysis.name: Mimi Ensley
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Dr. Ensley is by far the best English professor I've ever had. Initially, the course topic ("What is English?") seemed boring, but the readings and projects she assigned made it a lot more interesting. While her grading is strict to the rubric, she gives great feedback and is flexible (especially during COVID). Great choice for ENGL overall!

Very fun class. Most of the readings were interesting. Lots of class discussion. The grade is primarily in a few projects, which are graded generously. I asked for time extensions on nearly all of the projects, and Dr. Ensley was always happy to give them, even though I didn't give much of a reason (basically I had quizzes in other classes).

Dr. Ensley was a blast of a professor. One of the single nicest professors I've ever met. The class involved a lot of reading different books and passages as well as discussions about them, but Dr. Ensley made sure that engagement was interesting and worthwhile. Fully recommend for any class you have to take with her!

Dr. Ensley is super sweet and caring, especially during COVID. She cares a lot about the class material, although I did not find it to be that interesting. She grades fairly and gives a lot of feedback, although some of the homeworks and assignments feel unnecessary and like a waste of time. Decent choice as a prof

Take her! She's a wonderful prof and was extremely considerate that I took her class from a totally different timezone (12 hrs ahead). Gave extensions as needed. Very clear with feedback and helped me with non-class writing for a personal project. Great person, wish I could have taken the class in-person with her.

analysis.name: Martin Engman
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I found him really difficult to understand so lectures weren't helpful, and I relied on the book.  He has very few things he grades on (6 hws and 3 test + final) and there is absolutely no curve on anything.  He gives a recommended hw list  and you should absolutely do it.  Tests are pretty straight forward but some discontinuity in grading.

Test are reasonable but if you make a few small mistakes, it can easily drop your grade. He is against curving the class and has a set grading scale. If you make  below an 80 on 1 test, it is very difficult to bring it up to an A. It is easy to learn from the book and in recitation. He has really bad handwriting and is difficult to understand.

A cool guy, helpful during office hours and obviously very smart, but the grading is harsh. He expects you to memorize everything but only tests a few things, so I always felt like I was wasting my study time. A lot of the homework is optional, but if you don't do at least most of it your grade will suffer.

Mumbles a lot and talks into the board during lecture as he writes on the chalkboard. Tests seemed fair enough, but he does not curve and calculates your grade by just adding everything so its out of 500 or something. Homework was 3 mymathlab assignments and 3 written ones from textbook (not sure why we even had to use mymathlab with 3 homeworks).

Marty is so boring and hard to understand (he mumbles a lot and sounds like he smokes a pack a day). His handwriting is terrible, and if you are confused and try to ask questions, he is not helpful. By the end of the semester his lectures were almost empty. The only way I learned was by teaching myself or at recitation. DO NOT take him.

analysis.name: Enid Steinbart
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Worst Professor I've had at Tech.

Ok so she is a really nice person, but her class is tough. I lost a lot of points because she had weekly quizzes which were worth 25% of the grade in the end. I would say make sure to give you all from the beginning because she doesn't curve or give any extra credit. Other proffs had huge curves with similar grades, so I wish I had someone else.

She teaches well. We had tech issues for a bit but its good now. She is by far the best multi option. PROFESSORS MATTER FOR MULTI (things arent standardized). Her tests were pretty straightforward and quizzes exactly like homework (but no partial credit on quizzes due to MML). *note this was a COVID class so tests/quizzes may be different format

Lectures are long but worth going to, just be ready for lots of proofs that you won't be expected to know. She works lots of examples that are similar to what you'll see on a test. She's very approachable and wants to help her students. Tests are manageable. Only get 3 tries on MyMathLab homework questions.

She flew through the material. Explained concepts clearly but did very few example problem. Seemed bothered when students asked questions in class. If you can learn from a book this prof. is for you. You better have a good TA thats all I have to say.
